News.title: US midterm elections: The sectors bracing for potential shift in balance of power in Washington
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Corporate America has been preparing for a potential shift in Washington's balance of power as US midterm election results loom.

If Democrats show strongly, analysts and strategists say clean energy, housing, and healthcare stocks could gain, while artificial intelligence, data center, and defense firms may face greater legislative scrutiny.

Polymarket, the world's largest prediction market, puts the odds of a Democratic sweep at 72%, while Republicans keeping the Senate alongside a Democratic House win stands at 23%.

The chances of Republicans holding both chambers are a slim 6%, as a Reuters/Ipsos poll shows President Donald Trump's approval ratings at a career low over living costs and the war with Iran.

open image in gallery Americans had their final chance to make their voices heard on Tuesday ( Reuters )

A divided Congress would still grant Democrats enhanced power over funding and investigations, though overcoming any presidential veto from Trump would remain necessary.

Investors are closely watching these sectors:

Potential beneficiaries of a blue wave

CLEAN ENERGY

A strong Democratic showing could reinforce expectations that federal support for clean-energy development will remain in place, analysts said, benefiting companies such as solar maker First Solar FSLR.O, residential solar installer Sunrun RUN.O, inverter maker Enphase Energy ENPH.O and clean-power developer NextEra Energy NEE.N.

The Democratic-controlled Congress passed the Inflation Reduction Act in 2022, devoting hundreds of billions to climate and energy-security measures, including expanded tax credits for renewable energy, nuclear power and EVs.

In case of a divided government, brokerage UBS sees room for bipartisan legislation to speed up energy and infrastructure approvals and expects nuclear power to get backing from both sides.

Democrats plan to scrutinize the Trump administration's efforts to roll back emissions rules and could use the Congressional Review Act to overturn regulations that make it easier to sell gas-powered trucks and SUVs.

Automakers Ford F.N, General Motors GM.N and Stellantis STLAM.MI, which have scaled back EV plans and lobbied for looser rules, could face pressure.

HOMEBUILDERS

UBS said the Trump administration would continue to implement the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which Congress passed in late June, to increase the availability of affordable single-family homes.

If Democrats take both chambers, they could add affordability measures, including restrictions on large institutional landlords, though those would still face Trump's veto, UBS said.

The PHLX Housing Index .HGX has slipped close to 5% so far this year as the prospect of higher interest and mortgage rates weighs on the sector.

Sectors at risk from a blue wave

AI AND DATA CENTERS

Analysts expect a Democratic majority to bring greater scrutiny of AI, potentially pressuring data-storage and memory names such as Micron Technology MU.O, Sandisk SNDK.O and Seagate STX.O, which have rallied this year.

A slowdown in AI and data-center spending could also weigh on semiconductor-equipment makers AMAT.O, LRCX.O, KLAC.O, power providers CEG.O, VST.N and data-center builders PWR.N, VRT.N.

open image in gallery A divided Congress would still grant Democrats enhanced power over funding and investigations ( Reuters )

A Democratic majority would be more likely to use subpoena powers to compel tech executives to testify under oath or hand over records related to harmful AI-agent behavior.

Also, voters in at least 10 states could consider ballot measures that could impose new restrictions, permitting requirements or pauses on data-center development.

Still, Societe Generale said the AI trade is likely to remain intact as Democrats are unlikely to secure a majority large enough to override a Trump veto and key federal agencies remain under Republican control.

HEALTHCARE

Healthcare faces a mixed outlook under a Democratic sweep, with greater scrutiny of Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans potentially weighing on insurers, though TD Cowen sees limited risk of major industry changes and broad structural reform.

The S&P 500 healthcare sector .SPXHC has jumped more than 19% this year to record highs, trailing only energy stocks, as investors rotated into defensive sectors amid market volatility.

A Democratic-controlled House would heighten the possibility of raising taxes to fund a fiscal program that includes more health spending.

"A Democratic sweep could create greater momentum behind measures targeting healthcare costs, consumer fees, prescription drug pricing and areas perceived to contribute to affordability concerns," said Magdalena Ocampo, market strategist at Principal Asset Management.

DEFENSE

Defense stocks rallied in January after Trump called for a $1.5 trillion military budget, above the approved $901 billion, but they have since surrendered most of those gains.

A budget vote is unlikely before 2027. Democratic control of the House could bring military spending back under scruntiny, with analysts noting Congress has yet to appropriate funds for the multibillion-dollar contracts that big defense contractors signed to replenish stockpiles.

However, with the Iran conflict showing no sign of ending, companies such as RTX RTX.N and Northrop Grumman NOC.N continue to see robust demand for arms, pushing their backlogs to record levels.

FINANCIALS

Morgan Stanley analysts said additional oversight under a Democratic outcome could slow the pace of regulatory easing, but was unlikely to derail it.

A Democratic Congress last overhauled bank regulations with the 2010 Dodd-Frank law, which tightened capital rules, created a consumer watchdog and imposed new trading restrictions.

A stronger GOP hand would support regulatory clarity and policy continuity. Keeping conditions favorable for mergers and acquisitions and sustaining capital markets activity are a big earnings driver for large banks, Barclays analysts said.

Quarterly results from JPMorgan JPM.N, Citigroup C.N, Goldman Sachs GS.N and Wells Fargo WFC.N earlier this month suggested that a dealmaking and trading boom that powered record first-half earnings may be slowing.

CRYPTOCURRENCIES

Analysts say the election is unlikely to have a significant impact on cryptocurrency prices but will likely influence how quickly crypto legislation moves through Congress.

The Senate failed in September to advance the Clarity Act amid Democratic opposition, and analysts say a Democratic-controlled Senate would make it harder for the crypto bill to be revived next year.

Reuters has reported that Democrats in Congress are preparing investigations into crypto companies tied to Trump and his family, arguing the dealings present potential conflicts of interest.

That could generate adverse headlines and legal risks for some publicly listed firms in the crypto and blockchain industries, attorneys told Reuters.

News.title: Steve Kornacki gives Republicans a ‘wild card possibility’ that could see their election hopes increase
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

While recent polls and historical precedent favors Democrats ahead of Election Day, systematic polling inaccuracies could alter the outcome, according to NBC News chief data analyst Steve Kornacki.

Kornacki addressed the issue of widespread voter skepticism related to pre-election surveys Tuesday while discussing how to analyze the data on the Today show.

“In the Trump era in particular, we’ve seen these elections where the polls haven’t just missed, they’ve missed badly,” Kornacki said. “And they’ve missed in a specific way in the Trump era: they’ve missed Republican voters, pro-Trump voters, especially in states like some of these battleground states — Iowa and Ohio, some of these Midwest states.”

He noted that Kansas could be one state to monitor for potential polling discrepancies.

Kornacki explained that pollsters have been receiving significantly higher response rates from Democrats than Republicans. While survey organizations attempt to adjust their weighting models to compensate for the imbalance, he noted that the disparity leaves open a “wild card possibility” for the final results.

‘In the Trump era in particular, we’ve seen these elections where the polls haven’t just missed, they’ve missed badly,’ Kornacki said ( Getty )

Kornacki’s assessment aligns with recent disclosures from major polling operations regarding non-response bias. Survey administrators have continued to experience difficulty reaching Republican voters during this election cycle, the The New York Times reported.

“This cycle, Democrats are once again responding to Times/Siena polls at a much higher rate than Republicans,” wrote political analyst Nate Cohn. “Across these final battleground polls, registered white Democrats were about 30 percent likelier to take the poll than registered white Republicans. That’s actually a bit higher than in the final polls in 2020.”

The potential for an undercounted Republican electorate comes despite baseline metrics that favor Democrats.

A recent national poll conducted by NBC News showed Democrats holding a 52-43 percent advantage over Republicans on the generic congressional ballot. Historical trends also heavily favor the opposition, as the sitting president’s party has gained seats in only two midterm elections since World War II.

News.title: Unai Emery endures heaviest European defeat as Villa manager after unwanted gifts
News.content:
While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to prove nightmarish experiences.

His record at Barcelona’s home now reads as 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

Emery will have detested the goals conceded. He spent much of the match marching up and down his technical area and this was his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager.

It was also his 55th birthday but from the moment Villa midfielder Joao Gomes gift-wrapped Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

News.title: Gabonese TikTokers fight back against toxic skin lightening products
News.content:
There is a buzz among the pupils at Nzeng-Ayong 2 primary school in Libreville, the capital of Gabon. At least among those who use TikTok. Black Choco is here: social media personality, entrepreneur, and a bona fide celebrity. With the fervour of a revivalist preacher, she takes over the lesson. Today’s topic is kwandza, the Gabonese term for skin-lightening.

“Is kwandza good? No! It’s like pouring boiling water on your skin. And we don’t do that, do we?”

Why do people want to become white, she asks the pupils – boys and girls between eight and 12 – before answering the question herself.

“To please other people! Aren’t you proud of your skin? Our skin is our identity!”

She asks a handful of pupils to stand up. “Look at them! Aren’t they beautiful with their dark skin? Let them hear it!”

“Gloire, you are beautiful,” the whole class chants.

News.title: Newcastle fans turn on Jaissle as defeat triggers relegation concerns
News.content:
Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

News.title: US dairy worker dies from bird flu as outbreak rages in cattle
News.content:
“People at greater risk include dairy workers and others who have close or prolonged contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus. Transmission of avian influenza between humans is extremely rare and has never been documented in the United States. Public health officials are continuing to monitor individuals who had close contact with the patient for symptoms,” the health district said in a statement.

Experts say the US bird flu outbreak is not only costing the dairy industry millions of dollars but also raises the risk that the virus could mutate to spread more easily between mammals. They are also concerned that authorities are doing little to check the spread.

Marc Johnson, a virologist at the University of Missouri, told the Telegraph last week that the outbreak in dairy cattle was “completely preventable”.

“Cattle infections last only a few weeks before the animals recover. If infected herds were simply isolated until the outbreak fizzled out, it would stop.

“But cattle keep being moved around, spreading it into new states,” said Dr Johnson, referring to the way the US dairy industry operates, in which cows are routinely transported across state lines, whether to join new herds, for breeding, or to replace animals at large milk-producing operations.

A bird flu outbreak has also been raging on a mink farm in Utah for the last couple of months, according to news outlet ProPublica.

Jonathan Ball, professor of molecular virology at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, said allowing a virus to rage unchecked raises the risk of it mutating.

“Viruses like influenza are constantly exploring new hosts, and more often than not, it burns out. It’s not quite got the right combination of genetic changes to allow it to efficiently infect, efficiently replicate, and then efficiently transmit to the new host. But the longer these steps - adaptive changes, so genetic changes - are happening in these sporadic outbreaks, the more likelihood you’ve got of it mutating. It’s a bit like a one-armed bandit machine - if you keep pulling that handle, eventually you’re going to get three cherries,” he said.

News.title: First ever trial of long-acting injection against malaria to launch in Africa
News.content:
Dr Cristina Donini, executive vice-president of research and development at MMV, said the compound would be “complementary” to existing tools, rather than replacing them.

“The vaccine is doing a fantastic job in infants but if you could add onto that another tool that can cover a broader population with a longer regimen then we would be in a very good position to eliminate the disease,” she said.

Children in malaria-endemic regions are already given prophylactic drugs during the malaria season and studies have shown that these combined with the vaccine are highly effective. However, resistance has developed to these drugs and they have to be given monthly.

The malaria season in Africa varies by region but usually peaks after periods of rainfall. If the season lasts longer than three to four months it’s likely that people would need two injections. However, Dr Donini and her colleagues are working on a second generation LAI which they hope would provide year-long coverage.

Full costs have not yet been worked out but Dr Donini said affordability was an important factor in assessing the LAI’s suitability.

“It’s too early to say whether it will be cheaper than an injection - hopefully, yes. The beauty of it is that if you simplify it and decrease the number of injections needed you decrease the cost,” she said.

LAIs are gaining traction in the fight against infectious diseases - Lenacapavir, now being rolled out after being approved in 2025, provides almost 100% protection against infection from HIV and many believe it could help end the HIV pandemic. There are also LAI candidates in development for the prevention of tuberculosis, treatment and prevention of which usually relies on daily pills being taken over many months.

Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK, welcomed the launch of the trial.

“Thanks to sustained investment in malaria science including here in the UK, we are now on the brink of a number of breakthroughs which could turn the tide on the fight against the disease. And the long-acting injectable, specifically, could be a valuable addition to this toolbox as it has the potential to provide sustained protection from a single shot, avoiding the need for repeat doses.

“This phase of the trial also builds on earlier research conducted in the UK, highlighting the importance of the UK’s ongoing role as a malaria science superpower and the value of continued investment in malaria R&D. We look forward to the trial progressing further and eagerly await the results.”

News.title: Arsenal nous frustrates Liverpool as 14-year Anfield hoodoo ends with statement win
News.content:
It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

News.title: Tears flow for Antonelli after becoming youngest champion in F1 history
News.content:
Welcome to our coverage for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Today could be the day for Kimi Antonelli, the day he becomes a Formula One world champion. In fact it is very likely. All he needs to confirm the drivers’ championship is to finish ninth or higher. If George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not claim victory then he is champion whatever happens. Given his season so far, it is difficult to see the title fight going to Brazil next week.

What chance of a decent race here today? The first few laps are often entertaining as the pack bunches up and there are plenty of chances to overtake early on. Generally the top four teams have been close together (last week in Austin excluded) and it is possible to overtake here, though it is not exactly easy.

Qualifying yesterday as an intriguing and close session. Hamilton secured his first grand prix pole for Ferrari, by just 0.009sec from the Mercedes of George Russell, with Charles Leclerc of Ferrari a little behind him in third. Then came Max Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar and Lindblad. Liam Lawson was disqualified on a technicality.

Ferrari have been an up-and-down team this season but have been strong without really delivering on it fully in the last few rounds. Could they secure a third victory of the season today? They do not really need to worry about losing second in the constructors to Red Bull or McLaren and Mercedes are too far out of reach in any case.

In any case, the biggest story is likely to be Antonelli’s coronation in Mexico. Hamilton has won titles here before for Mercedes, will the Italian give the Silver Arrows another fiesta in Mexico City? The race starts at 8pm GMT and we will be here for all the build-up, live updates and reaction from it.

Sports.title: Gabby Logan forced to apologise as Bruno Fernandes swears on live TV after Man Utd’s epic comeback win over Roma
Sports.content:
Next

GABBY LOGAN was forced to apologise after Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes swore live on TV after his side’s 3-2 comeback win over Roma.

The Red Devils produced a miraculous turnaround after a bleak first half at Old Trafford.



Matias Soule struck in the first ten minutes before Ex-Aston Villa star Donyell Malen then made it 2-0 from the spot after Ayden Heaven’s handball.

United were left reeling at half time but Fernandes pulled one back from the spot – after his first missed effort was retaken – before Mateus Cunha won it with a late brace.



The incredible result could have very well saved Michael Carrick’s job for now amid rising pressure on his position.

Emotions were high after the final whistle and Fernandes gave an emotionally-charged interview to TNT Sports – insisting he wanted to win “every f***ing game” for the club.



When asked about Carrick’s future, he replied: “We don’t need to save anyone’s job.

“The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is someting we needed as a group of players and staff.

“We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together.

“It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

“The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn’t performing. And that’s fair.

“Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

“The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

“And it doesn’t change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.”



Fernandes had previously fallen out with Carrick after hitting out at his manager’s tactics following a 4-1 defeat to Como last month.

The Portuguese playmaker was then dropped for United’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth before they had clear-the-air talks.

Sports.title: Man Utd ratings: Diogo Dalot has another rotten outing but Matheus Cunha puts on attacking masterclass despite red card
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED pulled off another sensational European comeback after a 3-2 win over Roma to hand Michael Carrick a much needed boost.

United fans staged protests against the ownership but the quality of coaching came under the spotlight after yet another defensive collapse.



United avoided a 10th game without a win since March 1978, despite Roma leading 2-0 at half-time following Matias Soule’s strike and Donyell Malen’s penalty.

But the hosts, battered and bruised by the toxicity from fans, fought back through a Bruno Fernandes spot-kick and two goals from Matheus Cunha.



Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated and slated the United players from a bouncing Old Trafford.

Senne Lammens – 6

The Belgian was a sitting duck in front of arguably the worst defence in the Champions League. A good save stopped 3-0 before the the break.

Welcomed a quieter second half after his outfield players finally decided to show up.

Leny Yoro – 5

The central defender started at right-back and was often himself sprinting towards his own net with Carrick asking his players to push high.

He naively backed off in the lead up to the penalty being conceded. Looking stronger in forward areas and coping reasonably well with the mayhem.

Harry Maguire – 5

Guilty of dreadful mistakes with poor clearances glued straight into danger zones at every turn, putting Lammens in all sorts of trouble.



Another player who improved in the second half, but Roma’s attacks had stalled by then. Had three chances to score from quick corners in the second half but could not level.

Ayden Heaven – 5

A 20-year-old defender should be allowed to nourish and develop, but Heaven is always given a baptism of fire.

Roma’s cross flew over him to a sitting Soule before he conceded a penalty a few minutes later when Soule’s shot hit his low arm.

Looked overwhelmed and you can hardly blame him. Thrown in after Carrick dropped Lisandro Martinez following his needless red card at Chelsea.

Diogo Dalot – 3

No man’s land. Dalot left the entire left side vacant when Roma had possession to allow Soule the Freedom of Manchester to touch, wait and slot past Lammens inside 11 minutes.



Carrick had Dalot and Yoro as auxiliary wingers, and it was schoolboy defending at times. Somehow assisted Cunha’s leveller.

Kobbie Mainoo – 6

Back in the line up after a month out, but gave up possession too easily for Marten de Roon intercept a loose pass in the lead up to the opener.

His long range shot just before the break was United’s first on target attempt. The England midfielder improved in the second half when United had possession.

Carlos Baleba – 4

All the excitement about the £70m singing has quickly dried up. The 22-year-old was behind the pace and launched a free pass out of play behind Yoro before the break.

He pulled his right hamstring when he was through on goal with a tap-in available 30 seconds after the restart.



Bruno Fernandes – 7

The skipper found his spark after scoring a retaken penalty, having been let off the hook when encroachment erased an awful first attempt easily saved by Roma’s third-choice keeper.

The strike ended a goal drought that stretched back to the 4-0 win over Sabah on September 10.

He fumbled a first half shot and instantly threw his arms into the air in disgust over Baleba’s scruffy pass.

United are yet to trigger his one-year extension or agree fresh terms with their out-of-form captain. We might have to envisage a world without Fernandes at Old Trafford.

Amad – 5

The 24-year-old was not clinical enough and is guilty of too many touches inside the box.



Gets into good positions but you rarely believe he will score. He is without a United goal since December 14. Replaced by Shea Lacey, who was more threatening.

Matheus Cunha – 8

After a drab first half, the Brazilian soon became United’s best player saved the day, playing with anger and venom.

Scored two, won the penalty, launched himself topless into the crowd beneath the away end and was given a standing ovation after his sending off.

He was brilliant in the second half and cleverly rattled by the fan backlash inside Old Trafford, which helped his performance. Booked for his wild celebrations and picked up a second yellow in stoppage time.

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

Linked up well with Cunha but poor touch let down a decent breakaway. Painfully unluckily when his strike bounced between both posts straight after Fernandes’ penalty.



Had a couple of opportunities to push through on goal but just didn’t have the pace.

SUBS:

Youri Tielemans (Baleba, 50) – 6

Had a positive impact the ball.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Shea Lacey (Amad, 75) – 7

The teenager provided more than Amad in his 12 minutes on the pitch. His incredible pass assisted Cunha’s second. Should be gunning for Amad’s spot.

Lisandro Martinez (Heaven, 75) – 6

Dropped to the bench after his reckless red that condemned United to defeat at Chelsea. Was booed by Old Trafford when he came on after a month of antics.

Matthijs de Ligt (Maguire, 88) – N/A

Mason Mount (Fernandes, 88) – N/A

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha sent off and denied standing ovation minutes after last-gasp double inspires Man Utd turnaround vs Roma
Sports.content:
Next

MATHEUS CUNHA went from hero to villain against Roma with a dramatic brace and a red card.

The Brazilian forward netted twice in three minutes to propel Manchester United to a much-needed win in the Champions League.



United looked down and out against Roma at half-time as the players were booed off after falling 2-0 down.

But a second-half resurgence saw them claim a famous win after a penalty from Bruno Fernandes and Cunha’s brace.



The former Wolves star was full of excitement after his second goal as he whipped off his shirt and jumped into the crowd.

This earned Cunha his first yellow card and then a late challenge on Leonardo Balerdi followed moments later.



The referee wasted no time in showing Cunha his second booking and his red card.

Fortunately for United, they were not made to pay for Cunha’s red card and going down to ten men.

Michael Carrick‘s side were able to hold on to the 3-2 scoreline and claim only their third win of the season.

Goals from Matias Soule and Donyell Malen had put Roma in a commanding position before the break.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

United defender Diogo Dalot took the brunt of criticism for the first goal as he was far from the correct position.

The players were booed off by the fans at the break and Alan Shearer slammed them as “embarrassing” on Amazon Prime commentary.

United suffered another blow early in the second half as midfielder Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury.

But they were handed a way back into the game after winning a penalty for a foul on Cunha.

Fernandes failed with his first effort but with was given another chance due to encroachment.



The club captain made no mistake with his second attempt, which allowed Cunha’s heroic goals to win United the game.

Sports.title: Man Utd 3 Roma 2: Matheus Cunha inspires stunning comeback from 2-0 down that might just save Michael Carrick’s job
Sports.content:
Next

YOU had to be here to see it, believe it.

From utter despair, the brink of humiliation, to a comeback win to earn a place in the Manchester United book of legends.



And while this most astonishing of triumphs came from nowhere, it might, just might prove an unlikely turning point.

The night when Michael Carrick went from dead manager walking to getting the chance to prove he deserves the job after all.



As Matheus Cunha scored twice in the space of three second half minutes, transforming another defeat into a glorious triumph, United went from zeroes to heroes.

Battered and broken for 45 minutes, seemingly set to suffer a defeat that would leave scars for ever, only to somehow, against all the odds, end up with a first win in 10 games.

Sir Alex Ferguson will have loved it, seeing one of his old stalwarts throw caution to the wind and be rewarded for his gambles.

A night which seemed to sum up everything that is wrong with United finished with roars of sheer, delirious joy.



Sparked by Bruno Fernandes’ twice-taken penalty, Cunha then had the maddest of final minutes.

First the Brazilian was in the right place when Leonardo Balerdi’s air-shot gave him the chance to sweep home from close range – an absolute gift.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Then, as the roars became deafening, Cunha did it again, waltzing through to smash in off the post from a tight angle, stunning the Roma fans who had previously bellowed their lungs out.

That was followed by a second yellow card and a slow, disbelieving walk to the dressing room.

Yet when the final whistle went, there were no villains in red – an hour after there had been a whole cast of them.



At the interval, the surprise was that United and Carrick were not already dead and buried.

The manager’s decision to ask Diogo Dalot and Leny Yoro as auxiliary wingers, totally ignoring their prime roles, seemed utter folly.

If that was the plan, it unravelled inside 17 minutes as United’s chronic inability to do the defensive basics bit them once again.

The opener summed up just how poor United are.

Bad enough was Kobbie Mainoo coughing up the ball just inside the United half yet the lack of reaction was criminal.



Rodrigo Mora, wide on the left, had an age to see the day-dreaming Dalot was out of the picture – 25 yards the wrong side of his man.



And when Heaven – in for the benched Lisandro Martinez – missed the ball completely, Matias Soule had time to pick his spot past the exposed Senne Lammens.

Carrick went back to his bench for a video nasty replay but – after Cunha failed to get on the end of Bruno Fernandes’ cross – the horror show was back.

This time, Dalot was on the edge of the Roma box as the Italians played up the field, before Harry Maguire added his name to the list of villains.

Soule looked to have wasted the chance to feed the lurking Malen only for Maguire to hand the ball back to him and when Heaven’s right arm blocked the Roma man’s shot, Spanish ref Jesus Gil Manzano pointed instantly to the spot.

Malen, a force reborn since he left Aston Villa for the Italian capital in January, sent Lammens the wrong way.



Cue the second stage of protests, a cascade of tennis balls thrown onto the pitch – far more effective at stopping Roma then United’s back line or the green and gold balloons released before the start – as Carrick was left perplexed and mournful.

The last time Gian Piero Gasperini came to Old Trafford, his Atalanta side had squandered a two goal lead.

At that stage, a repeat did not seem at all likely.



Roma were fitter, sharper, simply better, United shambolic.

Old Trafford was the Theatre of Screams, mainly directed at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers but often at the home team too.

Only a desperate foot by Yoro prevented Soule presenting Mora with a sitter as United were opened up like a tin of tomatoes once again, before Lammens denied Malen after he exposed Heaven’s hell and Soule was a fraction wide.

The half-time jeers were brutal. And deserved.

When Carlos Baleba burst through within 45 seconds of the restart only to ping his right hamstring, it felt like a perfect embodiment of United’s misery.



Likewise, as Fernandes was denied by debut-making keeper Devis Vasquez after Cunha’s tumble in the vicinity of Gianluca Mancini was bought by the ref and confirmed by VAR, there was shock.

But the video booth spotted Bryan Cristante had encroached before clearing and the United skipper took his second chance.

Within seconds, United looked to be set to level, as Bryan Mbeumo but saw his shot bounce off BOTH posts before being cleared.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now it was a siege, which looked to have been repelled.

Enter Cunha. Astonishing. Remarkable. Enough to keep Carrick in his job beyond Sunday? Maybe.

Sports.title: Barcelona 3 Aston Villa 0: Lamine Yamal and Raphinha ruin Unai Emery’s birthday as 100% record comes to an end
Sports.content:
Next

UNAI EMERY celebrated his 55th birthday but his team handed a gift to the wrong person.

Because one of the worst things a player can do in world football, particularly inside their own area, is to pass the ball square to Lamine Yamal.



Yet after just seven minutes, Joao Gomes panicked and did exactly that. He gifted the ball to the teenager with stardust in his boots and we all knew what the outcome was going to be.

On a miserable night in Barcelona, with Villa’s fans getting drenched, their team still gave a decent account of themselves although they were undone with second half goals from Raphinha.



Newcastle fell to pieces in a 7-2 loss here eight months ago but Villa are made of much stronger stuff.

So to be disappointed with a three-goal loss against the La Liga champions shows you exactly the progress Aston Villa are making under Emery.



They are an excellent team and remain in a brilliant Champions League position, something Villa fans could not have dreamed of a few years ago.

With three wins, they still look certain to reach the play-offs but they could still finish in the top eight to earn that automatic pass into the last 16.

Although he did not have to click into top gear, Yamal, despite taking a knock from Emi Buendia, was a joy to watch.

It is now 14 goals in the Champions League for Yamal, the most ever scored by a teenager, as he is now one ahead of Kylian Mbappe.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And he might have been beaten to the Ballon d’Or by Harry Kane the previous week but Yama is going to win the award on a few occasions.

He gave Villa right-back Ian Maatsen a difficult night, including the odd nutmeg which is never a great look for a defender.

And we will once again see the Spanish close up on November 15 when England visit the Metropolitano in Madrid in the Nations League.

The Nou Camp remains a work in progress and it is still a building site outside.

With the roof not due to be in place until next season, everyone got a good speaking – with the exception of Prince William in the posh seats.



Although those who did turn up did not have long to cheer a goal thanks to that suicidal bit of defending.

Keeper Zion Suzuki, who gifted Fulham a goal on Saturday, played a risky short pass to Gomes who had Pedri breathing down his neck.

Gomes lost his composure and played that pass straight to Yamal who would not have believed his luck. Even though Pau Torres was standing in front of him, Yamal had no trouble bending his shot into the left corner.



You would have expected Villa would have avoided doing anything similar but they could not deal with Barcelona’s aggressive press.

It was extraordinary that Suzuki once again passed to Gomes under pressure from Pedri and the same thing happened.

Villa lost possession but on this occasion, Suzuki redeemed himself to make a save to keep out Anthony Gordon’s shot.

In fairness to Villa, they refused to let their heads drop and had plenty of chances to level.

Matty Cash’s decent strike was deflected for a corner and Johan Manzambi had a couple of chances, scuffing one shot wide while hitting the second straight at Joan Garcia. Jackson also had a shot deflected for a corner when Villa attacked in a three versus two.



Yet Barca also scored seven minutes into the second half. Fermin Lopez played the ball into Raphinha just inside the area and he was then helped with that deflection.

Raphinha’s second, Barca’s third, pure class. Joao Cancelo had too much power for John McGinn who also struck the Scotsman in the face.

Cancelo jogged down the left and then played a delicious pass with the outside of his right boot for Raphinha to ghost past Torres to tuck the ball past Suzuki.



Unbelievably, Suzuki kept playing those silly passes out of defence and Barca were handed another chance although the Villa keeper kept out the shot from Fermin Lopez.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Leon Goretzka sent a header from a corner onto the outside of the post and a goal was the least Villa deserved, who will now go to Manchester United this weekend expecting to win.

The only worry for Villa is if United come calling for their manager but right now, there is no way he would want to leave. Emery would be utterly bonkers.

Sports.content:

MIKEL ARTETA bizarrely claimed he has a “massive library” of clips if referees start clamping down on shirt pulling.

The Arsenal chief’s comments come in the wake of his side’s 1-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday, when the Reds were denied a clear penalty.



Gunners full-back Jurrien Timber grabbed Alexander Isak’s shirt, but neither the referee or VAR pulled him up on it.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said he may have to tell his players to “dive” in the future to win spot-kicks.



But when asked about a possible crackdown on shirt pulls, Arteta said: “I have a lot of clips about shirt pulls and grabs.

“I have a massive library that we can talk about. We’re talking about one in particular.



“I have a massive library that we can throw there to remind everybody what every team is going through.”

This is not the first time this season that Arteta has revealed he has a dossier of evidence when it comes to officiating.

The Spaniard was booked during a 2-0 win over Everton last month for repeatedly leaving his technical area.

And when quizzed about it at the time, he said: “I do have to be careful.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“There are managers that 36 times in just ten minutes have left the touchline, no yellows.

“So I’m clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. Someone else has the record.

Sports.title: Burrage receives death threats and abuse after Chennai Open defeat
Sports.content:
Jodie Burrage has revealed online abuse and death threats; both Burrage and fellow British player Katie Boulter believe most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing

Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open

Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday.

Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months, went down to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat against India's Vaishnavi Adkar.

The 27-year-old, who reached a career-high ranking 85 in September 2023, published an Instagram story with some of the abuse received due to the defeat.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," Burrage said in the accompanying message.

German player Eva Lys tagged the WTA from her Instagram handle and asked: "When will something be done?"

Last July, Burrage urged gambling companies and social media companies to do more to tackle online trolls.

Speaking after her first-round defeat to American Caty McNally at Wimbledon, Burrage said she has had to stop herself from looking at her phone due to online abuse.

"I think it's very simple to have someone's ID connected to their account and that would, I think, quickly stop what people write and make them more accountable," Burrage said.

"I'm just guessing that they're gamblers; some of them say, 'You've lost me this amount of money' or whatever, so some of them are. I don't know, that's the only explanation I've got otherwise they are just very bad people.

"But yes, it's tough and today I'm trying not to look at my phone. It's not easy to deal with, but I do think there could be more being done."

A report from the Women's Tennis Association and International Tennis Federation revealed that 458 players were direct targets of abuse in 2024. The report, produced using an AI-led detection system developed by the Signify Group, found that 40% of the social media abuse came from frustrated gamblers, a figure that rose to 77% for direct abuse directed towards players' personal accounts.

Image: Katie Boulter blames gamblers who have lost money for the abuse

Katie Boulter also opened up about the level of abuse aimed at some players and said she and her family have received death threats last year.

Boulter believes much of the abuse comes from gamblers who have lost money and while she has learned how to better handle it over the years, incidents can raise genuine concerns for her safety.

"I think it just kind of shows how vulnerable we are. You really don't know if this person is on site. You really don't know if they're nearby or if they know where you live or anything like that," she said.

"At the very start of my career, it's probably something I took very personally [...] getting comments about the way you look."

"It becomes more apparent every single time you go on your phone."

The WTA's player board has previously condemned the abuse as "unacceptable" and said the impact can be "significant".

Sports.title: Stoke battle to victory at Blackburn
Sports.content:
Jack McGlynn scored an audacious free-kick as Stoke held off a late Blackburn comeback to win 2-1 in the Championship.

After weathering early Blackburn pressure, McGlynn caught everyone off guard in the 43rd minute, finding the net with a spectacular set piece from the left instead of the expected cross to notch his fourth of the campaign.

Substitute Moussa Baradji's own goal in the 68th minute gave the Potters a deserved cushion as they seemed set for a comfortable victory.

But Andri Gudjohnsen's tap-in halved the deficit in the 87th minute and the Icelandic forward thought he had equalised three minutes later when skilfully steering a header into the far corner but referee Andrew Kitchen penalised the striker for a push, much to the fury of the Rovers fans and coaching staff.

Despite the late scare, Stoke held on to make it eight wins in 11 and move level on goal difference with second-placed Birmingham.

Stoke's victory here last season owed much to Viktor Johansson's heroics and he was at it again within four minutes when he produced a stunning stop to tip Todd Cantwell's rasping 18-yard drive behind.

Johansson was needed again close to the half hour when Hayden Carter pounced on a loose ball and strode forward into the space to unleash a low drive that the Swede pushed wide for a corner.

Despite their dominance, Rovers fell behind just before the break thanks to an outrageous free-kick from McGlynn. Wide on the left, the American went for goal rather than sending in a cross everyone was expecting and while Balazs Toth got a hand to it, the referee checked his watch to indicate it was over the line.

Dapo Afolayan planted a header wide of the far post after meeting Jayden Fevrier's right-wing cross, as Rovers tried to respond.

Robert Bozenik spurned a glorious chance just after the hour when played through by Million Manhoef, but he could not slot beyond the outstretched Toth.

Stoke recycled possession, the ball fell to Ben Johnson on the edge of the area and his venomous strike deflected wide with Toth well beaten.

The visitors' pressure finally told in the 68th minute when Manhoef was given time and space to race through Blackburn's defence and though Toth pulled off a sharp save down to his left, substitute Yuri Ribeiro's attempted clearance hit fellow replacement Baradji and rebounded into the empty net.

Gudjohnsen handed Rovers a lifeline three minutes from time when Johansson failed to hold Sam Morsy's shot, pouncing for his ninth of the season and he thought he had helped Rovers to a great escape with a towering header three minutes later from Gady Beyuku's cross but it was controversially ruled out and Stoke held on.

Sports.title: Norwich thrash Derby to heap pressure on Eustace
Sports.content:
Norwich piled more pressure on Derby boss John Eustace after thrashing the Championship strugglers 4-0 at Pride Park.

On his 47th birthday, Eustace saw his side ripped apart by the pace and movement of the Canaries, who scored three times before the break.

Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich in complete control before substitute Jovon Makama wrapped up a third straight win for the visitors and condemned Derby to a fourth defeat in five games.

Derby have won only once this season and Friday night's home game with Bolton now looks like a huge one for Eustace.

They went into the game as only one of two teams without a home win in the Championship and they fell behind in the eighth minute. Jack Stacey crossed from the right and although Yongwa's header was saved, Musaba slammed the rebound into the roof of the net.

Musaba had a great chance to score his second in the 15th minute when Andre Brooks played him in but his low shot struck the legs of goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

Norwich looked like scoring every time they came forward and after Zetterstrom made a reflex save to deny Mathias Kvistgaarden, Maghoma made it two with a curling effort from the edge of the box in the 27th minute.

Boos rang out from the home fans and only the woodwork denied Norwich a third when Stacey's shot hit the inside of a post and was cleared off the line by Alex Mowatt.

It got even worse for Derby just before half-time when they were torn apart again and after Brooks fired the ball in from the right, Yongwa made no mistake from 12 yards.

The half-time whistle was met with another chorus of disapproval from the home fans and it was no surprise when Derby made three substitutions for the second half.

Derby at least had an effort on target with a Carlton Morris header forcing Daniel Grimshaw into a diving save and there was certainly more urgency about their play but Norwich were not finished.

Makama came to the party in the 66th minute with a rasping drive from the edge of the area which Zetterstrom could not keep out.

That was the signal for Derby fans to head for the exits and some of those who stayed joined in when Norwich fans taunted Eustace with chants of "sacked in the morning".

It was certainly a miserable night for Eustace and Derby, who even at this early stage look like a team fighting relegation.

Sports.title: Cunha completes wild Man Utd comeback win over Roma from two down
Sports.content:
Manchester United produced an extraordinary comeback from two down to beat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win in 10 games.

Michael Carrick looked on the brink when his disjointed team were completely undone for Matias Soule's opener and Donyell Malen soon made it two from the penalty spot. But Matheus Cunha won one of his own, scored two and was sent off in a wild contest.

United had been booed off at the break and when Carlos Baleba had to go off early in the second half with a hamstring injury it all looked dismal for United. But when Cunha won a penalty that Bruno Fernandes scored after a retake it altered the momentum.

Bryan Mbeumo struck both posts with one shot soon after and the noise inside Old Trafford was astonishing thereafter. Roma cleared one off the line and United had two more penalty shouts as the Italian side - unbeaten in Serie A - began to wobble badly.

Leonardo Balerdi's error proved it, his woeful clearance allowing Cunha to slot home the leveller. And it was the same player with a stunning near-post finish from Shea Lacey's pass who completed the comeback to the delight of the disbelieving crowd.

Cunha was sent off for a silly foul to ensure a tense finale but United held on for a first win in 54 days. Improbably, Carrick left the pitch not just to applause but having presided over a win in the Champions League. And a spirited one at that.

Analysis: A comeback from nowhere

Where on earth did that come from? Roma were two up and it could have been more against a United side whose spirit appeared as broken as their tactics in a first half that seemed like surrender. But strange things can still happen at the Theatre of Dreams.

It is difficult to overstate the incoherence of those opening minutes. Watching Fernandes throw his arms in the air in disgust at a Baleba pass late in the first half, it looked like a team in disarray and desperate to blame someone else for the situation.

United's tactical setup early on against Roma was arguably even worse than against Como when Fernandes criticised his manager. They were continually cut apart in the left-back position with Diogo Dalot up the pitch and Ayden Heaven exposed.

At that stage, thought turned to the balance of the squad and the quality of it, the confidence and the team spirit, the players, the coach and the ownership. None of that completely goes away after a chaotic 45 minutes but this was at least something.

It was a team telling the fans that they can show spirit, that they are not prepared to let it slide further without a fight, that they can still conjure quality from nowhere. The scenes at the end of the game showed that at this great club, sometimes, that can be enough.

Sports.title: Haas confirm Ocon will not race for team again this season
Sports.content:
Haas have confirmed Esteban Ocon will not race for the team again this season with Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara set to make his Formula 1 debut at this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Ferrari Academy driver Camara, who had already been announced to take Ocon's seat from the start of 2027, will become an F1 driver earlier than anticipated.

Frenchman Ocon was dropped midway through the last round in Mexico, with the American team not offering an explanation as to why.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jenson Button reacts to Esteban Ocon's social media statement after Ryo Hirakawa replaced him at the Mexico City Grand Prix

He was subsequently replaced by Ryo Hirakawa from Saturday onwards but the Japanese driver, who was 10th at the Mexico City Grand Prix, is racing in the World Endurance Championship this weekend in Italy.

Hirakawa impressively finished 10th to score a point on his F1 debut on Sunday following post-race penalties for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, plus Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto.

Haas announced last month that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad, with Brazilian youngster Camara signed as his replacement for 2027.

The Brazilian - current F2 leader - will step in to partner British driver Ollie Bearman at his home race with Ocon confirmed to have been removed for the rest of the season.

A Haas statement read: "TGR Haas F1 team can confirm that Esteban Ocon will no longer compete on its behalf in the 2026 FIA Formula 1 world championship."

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu refused to answer questions on what had happened with Ocon when he was live on Sky Sports on Saturday of the Mexico race.

The Japanese boss says the issue remains an "internal matter".

He said: "Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City - but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward.

"The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations.

"Looking ahead, we've chosen Rafael Camara to drive alongside Ollie Bearman at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix."

Haas have not confirmed who will drive at the final three scheduled races in Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Sports.title: Esteve hoping for Champions League debut – and Haaland reunion
Sports.content:
A reunion with Manchester City brings bad memories for the RB Leipzig defender Maxime Esteve. He scored two own goals at the Etihad Stadium last year. Not that he has advertised this to his new teammates. "Maybe they don't even know," he jokes.

It is an amusing statistic that this time last year, indeed until the final days of November, a dozen games into the Premier League season, Esteve had found the net for City more times than everyone bar Erling Haaland. "This is a secret. You don't have to say!"

The 24-year-old French centre-back left Burnley for Leipzig in the summer and the truth is that he is aching to face City again. He has been on the bench for their opening two Champions League games and is desperate to make his debut in the competition.

"Five years ago, when I was a young kid at Montpellier, my former club, I would have killed to be in this situation now, even if sometimes you do not have the playing time that you want," he explains. "It was always a dream to play for a Champions League club."

Image: Esteve made a big step forward in his career during his time at Burnley

Unlucky own goals aside - "and I remember the second was really, really unlucky", Esteve insists - he was brilliant for Burnley. Even in that game against City, his manager Scott Parker made a point of highlighting all his good work in the analysis afterwards.

"I had a meeting on the Monday with him. He told me, 'Max, this is nothing. This is really, really nothing.' Instead, he showed me the good things that I did in the game. Just for the confidence, it was good. It was a bad memory for me at the time but this is football."

Image: Phil Foden and Erling Haaland celebrate an own goal by Burnley's Esteve

Will there be more bad memories after coming up against Haaland again? Esteve acknowledges that Harry Kane has just been honoured with the Ballon d'Or but in his view nobody is better than Haaland. "The best striker I have played against," he says.

"I played just two games against him, but you can see that he is, I think, maybe the best striker in the world. For years, I think he will still be in this position. He is so powerful, so good at heading, so quick. All of the qualities to be a beast." So, how do you stop that?

It is not easy because the temptation is to get tight. "I remember when I played against him, he played with other players, maybe with Rayan Cherki, for example, in the small spaces, so we tried to stay around him." And yet, in a physical battle, it is just as tough.

"You can see as well the habit to sometimes just chip it to the back post and he comes really, really aggressive on you with a big header. He is really good in this box position against the defender, every time in a good position to just finish really good.

"I think he adapts his football against the opponent he is going to play. He did not really touch the ball during the game. He is not that active with the ball. But every time you have to be focused 100 per cent because you know that in one second he can score."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Erling Haaland was spotted dancing on the pitch after Man City's shoot-out win over Brighton

Esteve is unusually thoughtful and you sense that he welcomes detail in his coaching. For example, his video work on opposition strikers extends far beyond their shooting habits. He is fascinating when discussing how their speed dictates his movement.

"It helps you just for the confidence to say, OK, this guy is running at 36 kilometres [per hour] or is he running at 34 [kilometres per hour]? It is quite important because you might have to manage the line a little bit higher or this kind of thing. It is small details."

Maybe it is a product of working with a City legend in Vincent Kompany. The now Bayern Munich coach was in charge at Burnley during Esteve's first season in England. He sees similarities with his current coach, another former City defender in Martin Demichelis.

"It is quite funny. They still want to stay really fit. They play in training. You can see they are quite competitive. They don't want to lose. You can see it. It is still really important for them. They are quite young coaches so they have the new idea of football."

He adds: "We do not play the same football [as Kompany at Leipzig], but in terms of energy, time, work and professionalism, I am going to say they are quite similar. In terms of meetings, they are really perfectionists. They arrive early and they leave really late."

Image: Esteve has enjoyed a promising start to his career at RB Leipzig

That time-keeping is a feature of life in Germany. "They do not accept anyone being late!" But Esteve is having no problem adjusting. "The facilities, the food, the organisation, everything." The demands are something of a step up after relegation.

"The objective here is to qualify for the Champions League every season." For now, he just wants to play in it. "If I get this opportunity to play, I will be the most happy in the world, to be honest, because you want to realise your dream when you are a kid.

"It is time to integrate myself in the new league, in a new club, new culture as well. For sure, in terms of playing time, I would like to play more, but that is [true] for every player, to be honest. But it is a time for integration and I am here for a long time, I hope.

"I am really happy and really patient. When you come to a bigger club, there is more competition in your position and I totally get that. I just have to wait for my time." That time looks set to come against Man City, of all teams. Just no own goals, please…

Sports.title: Manchester United produce comeback for the ages as Cunha double floors Roma
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick enjoyed one of his finest nights as a Manchester United player in the Champions League against Roma, scoring twice in a 7-1 win in the quarter-final, second leg in 2007. The re-run here was all about his managerial survival at the club.

The situation looked impossibly grim for him at half-time. Amid an atmosphere of continued fan anger towards the United ownership, Carrick’s team had been implausibly bad. Roma took a 2-0 lead into the break and the truth was that the scoreline greatly flattered United.

What happened next was a fightback for the ages. For Carrick, it might even have topped 2007. United’s defending had been so loose, so generous. But they finally showed the other side to their game – the one about attacking punch; derring-do. They found a solution to their woes at the back. Keep the ball in the other half.

Matheus Cunha was the hero and it said plenty about the chaos of this game, the wildness of the emotions, that he ended up being sent off for a second yellow card in the 90th minute for a lunge at Leonardo Balerdi.

Before that, he had supplemented a Bruno Fernandes penalty – which the captain converted after a retake – with a touch and finish following an error from Balerdi. Cunha’s second goal, which proved to be the winner, was hammered in off the near post after a pass from the substitute, Shea Lacey. Cunha’s first touch to control was a beauty.

The United support sing about having seen it all. This was just extraordinary. Can it save Carrick? He will go into Sunday’s Premier League game at home against Aston Villa with renewed belief.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes hits his retaken penalty high into the net to start the United comeback. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The fragility of the United backline has been well documented. How the hierarchy decided that it did not need any reinforcements over the summer is beyond belief. With Luke Shaw still injured, Carrick was forced to persist with Diogo Dalot out of position at left-back.

Dalot pushed very high at the outset, which felt bold. It was plainly a demand from Carrick. Dalot’s positioning was pure folly on the opening Roma goal. The visitors transitioned quickly, far too quickly for United’s ponderous defence and when Rodrigo Mora looked up from the inside left, all he could see was Soulé in acres of space on the opposite channel. Where was Dalot? Mora played the pass. Soulé took a touch and swept past the exposed Senne Lammens.

Quick Guide Champions League roundup: PSG hit Villarreal for six Show Paris Saint-Germain set a new record as the quickest team to score four goals in the Champions League by powering into a 4-0 lead after 17 minutes against Villarreal on their way to a 6-0 win. João Neves started the goal-blitz before Desiré Doué, Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz quickly put the tie to bed. Ruiz struck his second to make it 5-0 soon after the interval and substitute David Boly completed the scoring as PSG extended their 100% Champions League start and moved three points clear at the top of the table. Since taking just two points from their first three Ligue 1 games this season, which included a 2-1 home defeat to Monaco, PSG have now won 10 successive games in all competitions. Inter were equally convincing, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip. Yann Bisseck curled in the opener from long range, Pio Esposito headed the second before ⁠halftime and Piotr Zielinski completed the scoring from ​distance after ​the restart. Sporting Lisbon beat Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, a day after parting ways with their head coach, Rui Borges. Under the reserve coach, Tiago Fernandes, the Portuguese giants picked up their third win in the Champions League this season, with Issa Doumbia scoring the decisive goal in the game at Stamford Bridge. Aleksey Batrakov scored two goals in quick succession to seal a 2-0 win for Galatasaray against Stuttgart. Batrakov opened the scoring in the 12th minute at Rams Park and struck again three minutes later. Lask won 4-0 against Slovan Bratislava and Bodø/Glimt drew 0-0 with Lille Stadiums across Europe fell silent before kickoff in memory of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, who died earlier on Tuesday. Agencies Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

United’s defending for the second goal was even worse. Leny Yoro turned and ran back towards his own goal as Roma advanced up the left, and when the move appeared to have broken down for them around the United box, there was Harry Maguire to gift it back to Soulé with a dreadful miskick. Soulé dropped his shoulder and shot; the ball hit Ayden Heaven’s hand and Malen converted from the spot. Again, Dalot had been high up the pitch.

The mutiny could be felt before kick-off; the sounds of it heard. There were the green and gold balloons of protest against the Glazers. The relentless chants against the club’s owners. When the clock showed 20 minutes and five seconds – or 2005; the year of the Glazer takeover – the Stretford End erupted in a planned move; hurling tennis balls down on to the pitch.

Moments earlier, a grisly Dalot error on the ball had almost led to Malen getting in for a third and the first half was just an ordeal for United. Roma were well organised in their 3-4-2-1 shape and they got in up the inside right time and again. They might have had many more before the interval; Mora, Malen and Soulé all went close.

United offered minimal resistance. They were so easy to play through. There was nervousness from them on the ball, heavy touches. A glaring lack of cohesion. What was the plan? When Bruno Fernandes had a half-chance on the edge of the box in the 43th minute, he could not sort out his feet and blazed high.
