Sports.title: IBF Reorders Lindolfo Delgado vs. Arthur Biyarslanov Talks
Sports.content:
The IBF made the correct call by keeping Lindolfo Delgado in contention for its vacant 140-pound championship after his withdrawal from the Riyadh event. Following a report from Darshan Desai, the sanctioning body ordered Delgado and Arthur Biyarslanov to reopen negotiations. While Biyarslanov certainly earned quicker clarity on the status of his bout, stripping Delgado of his title shot would have been an excessive penalty for prioritizing safety and preparation.

Delgado (24-0, 16 KOs) and Biyarslanov (21-0, 17 KOs) had been scheduled to meet on the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli undercard. Biyarslanov traveled to Saudi Arabia as planned. Delgado remained behind after his trainer, Robert Garcia, cited regional missile threats alongside a grueling travel schedule. Under that proposed itinerary, Delgado would have had barely two days on the ground to overcome jet lag and shed final pounds.

Biyarslanov voiced valid frustration after enduring twelve weeks of camp away from home, followed by seven days of silence in Riyadh. He put in the work, made the flight, and reasonably expected direct word on whether the contest remained intact. Delgado’s camp owed him that basic communication while sorting out logistical hurdles.

Still, traveling to Riyadh is not the same as arriving with proper runway to contest a world championship. Biyarslanov got into town early and settled into fight week. Garcia faced a delayed flight plan, extended ground travel, and a dangerously compressed weight cut. Just because one camp navigated the journey without incident does not invalidate the other side’s athletic and safety concerns.

Now, the ruling brings the two undefeated contenders back to the negotiating table for the title Richardson Hitchins vacated upon moving to 147 pounds. What remains is securing a firm location and date. Biyarslanov has already invested a full training camp and traveled across the globe. Before he launches another grueling camp, he deserves concrete details on where and when this matchup will actually happen.

Sports.title: Matchroom Is Wasting Teremoana Teremoana’s Prime
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana is nearly seven years older than Moses Itauma, but Matchroom is still handling him like a fragile prospect who just took up the sport. The Australian turns 29 in February, sits on 12 knockouts in 12 fights, and is doing nothing more than treading water.

Marching him out against Hemi Ahio on November 18 in Melbourne is pure filler, a safe exercise that teaches nobody anything.

Ahio has a right hand, sure, but he is a regional gatekeeper meant to be blown away. When Teremoana flattens him inside two rounds, Eddie Hearn will celebrate like something meaningful happened. It will not be.

Teremoana blew out Curtis Harper, Bowie Tupou, and DeAndre Savage in four rounds total. Stacking up quick knockouts against guys brought in to fall over proves nothing. Teremoana is running out of track to waste rounds on heavyweights who cannot throw back.

Matchroom should be throwing him in with fighters like Filip Hrgovic, Fabio Wardley, Joseph Parker, Frank Sanchez, or Bakhodir Jalolov. Parker has the ring knowledge to expose any flaw in Teremoana’s game. Sanchez would make him miss wildly, forcing him to adapt. Wardley would make him pay for every careless swing. Those bouts carry real risk, which is precisely what Teremoana needs if he expects to be taken seriously.

Jalolov is the real grudge match. The giant southpaw outpointed Teremoana at the Paris Olympics, and Teremoana has done little since then besides crush lower-tier opponents before breaking a sweat. A pro bout with Jalolov would settle whether Teremoana has actually grown into a genuine threat, or if he is simply a big puncher dominating weak competition.

Itauma is 21 and can afford easy nights while he matures. Teremoana has been a pro since 2020, turns 29 in months, and is burning up his peak years on glorified sparring sessions. Knocking out Ahio gets him to 13-0, but it does not tell the public whether he belongs with the elite. If Matchroom keeps feeding him soft touches for number 14, everyone will realize the promotional machine is just hiding him from real danger.

That Olympic background makes this entire situation impossible to defend. When an amateur competes on the world stage against elite international talent, he already knows how to box. He knows how to deal with different styles under immense pressure. Fighters with that kind of foundation are supposed to move quickly through the professional ranks. Instead, Teremoana is nearly twenty-nine years old, six years into his paid career, beating up club fighters who have zero business sharing a ring with him.

Eddie Hearn loves treating every signing like an unpolished project requiring years of gentle matchmaking. Matchroom protects records to manufacture shiny undefeated records, but that approach does Teremoana no favors. Heavyweights his size do not possess an infinite clock. Burning his athletic prime on showcase bouts against regional gatekeepers accomplishes nothing. Hearn gets cheap main events for overseas broadcasts while protecting his investment from suffering a loss.

The bigger issue rests directly on Teremoana. A heavyweight with genuine ambition never sits back quietly while his promoter dishes out safe opponents. He should be banging on Hearn’s door every week, demanding top fifteen names, forcing Matchroom to take the training wheels off completely. Elite punchers do not accept soft paydays. They push their handlers to secure bouts against legitimate contenders who possess the tools to punch back.

Settling for second-tier opposition reveals either a total lack of self-belief or satisfaction with being a protected house fighter. If he truly believed he belonged among the division elite, he would demand dangerous fights right now without hesitation.

Every time he signs to blast out an overmatched opponent in two rounds, he throws away months of his prime that he will never recover. If he refuses to force Matchroom into testing him against real competition, his career will end before anyone discovers how good he actually was.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Uses Online Backlash To Fuel Shane Mosley Jr. Clash
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley figures getting rinsed across social media might actually work in his favor. Losing his WBO middleweight strap threw his name directly into feeds belonging to fans who had never watched him box. Now, he plans on using Shane Mosley Jr. to make an impression that actually sticks.

“Winning caps it all off, 100 percent,” Bentley said during their Zuffa Boxing 12 faceoff on Sky Sports. “I mean, everyone’s saying my name. I wouldn’t know about flowers yet, ’cause right now I’m getting rinsed online, but that’s all cool.” Bentley pointed out that casual fans tuning in because of the drama finally get to watch him perform. He fully expects to stop Mosley inside the distance.

Bentley clashes with Mosley this Saturday at Copper Box Arena in London. It was the exact matchup Bentley pushed for before taking on mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernández. The WBO shut down his appeal, stripping his belt on the spot. While Bentley kept his spot on the card, the sanctioning drama created an instant buzz. The real casualty was the world title he could have carried into a massive unification clash.

That loss stings because Bentley still craves marquee matchups. He insists he technically remains the champion, keeping his sights locked on the middleweights signed to Zuffa. Carlos Adames got mentioned during the press festivities. Bentley made it clear he intends to hunt division leaders as a challenger, targeting the exact names he wanted during his title reign. Zuffa offers the platform, yet Saturday comes without any guarantees.

Mosley acknowledged Bentley lost his strap through boardroom politics rather than ring action, though he still expects to cruise to a points victory. Coming off a signature win against Serhii Bohachuk, Mosley wants the spotlight Bentley created. Invading London to steal a victory puts Mosley first in line for major fights under the promotional banner. Forcing Bentley into a messy boxing match could also ruin the knockout statement Bentley promised.

Bentley walked himself into a trap. Flattening an opponent who just upset Bohachuk forces the critics to shut their mouths after the WBO embarrassment. An emphatic stoppage forces Zuffa to open the checkbook for Adames. Scraping past Mosley on a dull decision does nothing for him, leaving him on the outside looking in with zero leverage. Internet trolls jumped on his neck the second the belt vanished. Saturday determines if Bentley backs up his mouth or becomes a punchline in his own backyard.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Walks Into Clarke Ambush At Copper Box
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith gets back in the ring against Cheavon Clarke on Saturday, November 7, at Copper Box Arena in London. The bout headlines Zuffa Boxing 12, putting the former WBO cruiserweight champion in front of a man holding an amateur victory over him from 2016.

Billam-Smith enters at 22-2 with 14 knockouts, aiming to hold his place near the front of the division. Clarke comes in at 12-2 with 9 knockouts, looking to make his previous success count on a major professional stage.

The preliminary bouts begin at 12 p.m. Eastern Time, which is 5 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time. The main card takes over at 2 p.m. Eastern, or 7 p.m. locally in the UK. The headline ring walks are expected around 5 p.m. Eastern and 10 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time, though that timing will shift depending on how quickly the supporting fights wrap up. Viewers in the United States and Canada can watch the card through Paramount Plus. Fans in the UK and Ireland can watch the main card on Sky Sports, with online streaming through NOW and the preliminary matches carried on Sky digital platforms.

The supporting lineup features Denzel Bentley taking on Shane Mosley Jr. in a ten round middleweight co-feature. Heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter meets Ivan Balaz on the main portion of the show, followed by a cruiserweight match between Lucas Roehrig and Connal McDonald, a middleweight bout featuring Sam Hickey against Amaury Massenaux, and Kayla Allen versus Julia Igel. The preliminary portion includes Zach Parker against Umar Dzambekov at light heavyweight, Masood Abdulah taking on Adan Palma, and the debut appearance of Vinnie Kemp.

Both main event fighters fought grueling bouts in June. Billam-Smith wore down Ryan Rozicki until Rozicki stayed on his stool after the seventh round. Clarke hit the canvas twice in the fourth round against Jack Massey, yet recovered to stop Massey three rounds later. Clarke owns the quicker hands over ten rounds, which means Billam-Smith cannot afford to spend long stretches following his opponent around the perimeter.

Billam-Smith must use his jab to establish distance, force Clarke toward the ropes, and work on the inside to sap Clarke of his bounce. Even if Billam-Smith lands clean early, Clarke has already shown he carries fight-ending power when wounded, meaning the former champion needs sharp discipline to avoid getting caught on the way in.

For Billam-Smith, he is entering that dangerous zone where a fighter’s style catches up with their shelf life, making this matchup against Clarke a massive upset potential.

Look at his recent stretch. Billam-Smith does not have easy nights. He does not box on the outside and slip shots; he relies on imposing physical will, eating three clean punches to land four of his own. By the final bell against Gilberto Ramirez, Brandon Glanton, and Ryan Rozicki, his face looked like ground beef. His skin splits if someone looks at him wrong, and the scar tissue around his eyes has become an open invitation for referees and ringside doctors to intervene.

When a pressure fighter like Billam-Smith, who absorbs heavy punishment, starts racking up rounds at 35 or 36, the decline rarely happens gradually. It happens off a cliff. The punch resistance cracks, the reflexes slow by half a second, and suddenly shots that used to get brushed off start rattling the frame.

Clarke is precisely the wrong stylistic matchup for an aging, battle-worn brawler to face in a ten-round fight. He has the amateur pedigree and hand speed to exploit Billam-Smith’s porous defense. Billam-Smith comes forward in straight lines with his chin up. Clarke has already proven in the amateurs that his hand speed gives Billam-Smith fits, and fast combinations against an opponent with compromised scar tissue is a recipe for severe cuts early.

Despite his advanced age, Clarke still possesses real power and resilience. Jack Massey dropped Clarke twice in the fourth round, and Clarke still showed the composure and engine to recover and stop Massey three rounds later. If Billam-Smith hurts Clarke, he cannot just swarm carelessly, because Clarke throws violent counters when trapped.

At this point, the schedule works entirely against Billam-Smith. At ten rounds instead of twelve, the distance favors the explosive, faster starter. Billam-Smith typically needs eight or nine rounds of grinding pressure to break a man down. In a ten-rounder, if Clarke banks four of the first six rounds behind speed and angles, Billam-Smith runs out of road and has to chase recklessly.

If Billam-Smith gets dragged into another trench war where he has to swallow flush shots to make Clarke work, this has all the ingredients of an ambush. Clarke has the speed, the confidence from their amateur history, and the firepower to hand the former champion a costly defeat.

Sports.title: Mannix Says Munguía and Melikuziev Have Reached Terms
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía and Bektemir Melikuziev have reportedly come to terms for a WBA super middleweight title fight. Munguía named his mandatory challenger after beating Nikita Zon by unanimous decision Saturday in Riyadh, but Sergio Mora still doubts he’ll take the fight.

“I think Munguía is going to stay away from him,” Mora said during his discussion with Chris Mannix. “Well, I think he’s going to fight him. I don’t think he’s going to give up his belt, and everything I’ve been told [is] that they’ve come to terms on the fight,” Mannix said on his channel. He gave no date for the defense.

Mora had already picked Melikuziev before the Zon fight. He sees a natural 168-pounder who uses his southpaw angles better than Zon and hits harder. Mannix brought up Melikuziev’s close fight with Darius Fulghum, when he needed a knockdown in the 12th. That’s a fair reason to hesitate over picking Bektemir, but Munguía gave him something specific to work on in Riyadh.

When Zon hurt Munguía in the sixth, the champion bent forward and pulled his gloves up around his ears. Zon kept hooking at the sides of the guard. Mora thought a straight punch or an uppercut could have brought Munguía’s head up and given referee Tony Weeks a reason to stop it. Both men backed Weeks for letting it continue. Munguía came back to hurt Zon in the same round.

What would worry me about Bektemir is what happens before Munguía gets to the ropes. Munguía likes to walk a man down and get close enough to work with both hands.

Every step in gives a southpaw with good feet a chance to move outside his lead foot and send a left hand through the middle. Munguía can come back from one bad minute, as he showed against Zon. Against Melikuziev, he may have to solve that left hand every time he tries to get his own offense going.

Sports.title: Could Rocky Marciano Take Away Larry Holmes’s Jab?
Sports.content:
Larry Holmes was one win away from matching Rocky Marciano’s 49–0 record when Michael Spinks took his heavyweight title in September 1985. After losing a close unanimous decision, Holmes had something to say about the champion whose record he’d come up short of tying. “Marciano couldn’t wear my jockstrap,” he said.

I thought Spinks earned that decision by taking the final round, and I gave Holmes the rematch, which Spinks won by split decision. But the crack about Marciano got me thinking about something Holmes did in the ring. He sometimes left his left arm extended between jabs to keep a shorter man at a distance. Most fighters would try to get around it. I think Marciano would have started punching it.

Rocky could come up from his crouch with a short uppercut into the elbow or dig a hook into the upper arm when Holmes covered up. He’d take some clean jabs getting close enough to do it. But if those punches made Holmes think twice about leaving the arm out, Marciano would have more room to step in. A punch that looked wasted in the fourth could buy him a shot at the ribs in the tenth.

Holmes could make that a slow and painful trade for Marciano. A quick jab and half a step back would leave Rocky reaching for an arm that was already gone. If Marciano tried to cover the extra ground by ducking in from too far away, Holmes could catch him with the right uppercut. Rocky might do good work once he got his head against Holmes’s chest and still spend most of the round trying to get there.

The danger for Holmes would come when he started pulling straight back with his hands down. Marciano was behind against Jersey Joe Walcott before knocking him out in the 13th to win the title. In the Ezzard Charles rematch, he scored an eighth-round stoppage with his nose badly split. Holmes could be well ahead after ten rounds and still have to watch where his left hand came back after every jab. If it dropped to his waist, Marciano could throw his right over it without having to get all the way inside.

I’d take Holmes by decision over 15 rounds. I can see Marciano hurting him late, especially if the work on the arm took some snap off the jab. But Holmes could win the first two minutes of a round from a distance and make Rocky spend most of the last minute closing it. I’d give Holmes more of those rounds than I’d give Marciano the kind where he got close early and kept him there.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Welcomes Oleksandr Usyk Fight
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith would welcome a fight with Oleksandr Usyk at cruiserweight, but it’s hard to see why Usyk would take it.

Billam-Smith faces Cheavon Clarke this Saturday in a fight that has generated little buzz. Even a strong win would leave him a long way from getting Usyk’s attention.

“Anyone would love to have that opportunity,” Billam-Smith said on talkSPORT when asked if he’d like to fight Usyk. He praised Usyk for what he accomplished in his first run at cruiserweight, including beating opponents in their own backyards. He also floated the possibility of Usyk fighting David Benavidez in May.

Benavidez is precisely why the Billam-Smith fight is so hard to picture. If Usyk can get Benavidez, there’s little reason to take a detour through Billam-Smith first. If he beats Benavidez, there’s even less reason to stick around for a fight that would be a much tougher sell.

Saudi backing could put a big purse on the table, but someone would have to be willing to take a hefty loss on the show. A former world champion settling an old score at the Copper Box is a decent Saturday main event. It would take a lot more than a win over Clarke to make Billam-Smith the opponent people want to see for one of Usyk’s last fights.

Billam-Smith tossing his name into the mix sounds like wishful thinking, because from a business standpoint, the numbers simply do not work. At cruiserweight, the appetite begins and ends with marquee matchups. Benavidez brings immense Mexican American star power and guaranteed crossover viewers. Jai Opetaia is viewed as the true elite at 200 pounds, a genuine pound-for-pound talent who can test Usyk athletically.

Those fights carry legitimate commercial intrigue and legacy value. Billam-Smith, by contrast, is a domestic UK ticket seller whose profile drops off steeply once you leave Britain. Expecting Saudi organizers to cut a massive check for an unheralded opponent when far bigger fights exist makes zero sense.

The winner of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua remains a gigantic stadium draw for Usyk regardless of previous records. Fans would gladly line up for an undisputed rubber match or a fresh chapter with Daniel Dubois before Usyk hangs up the gloves.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Ordered To Fight Michael Zerafa For Vacant WBO Belt
Sports.content:
Yoenli Hernández could have to go through a second purse bid just to get his first WBO title fight. The WBO has authorized negotiations between Hernández and Michael Zerafa for its vacant middleweight belt after stripping Denzel Bentley, whose mandatory defense against Hernández had already gone to bid.

Zerafa, ranked fourth by the WBO, moves ahead of two contenders who are unavailable. No. 2 Vito Mielnicki Jr. is unavailable, and No. 3 Tim Tszyu is under contract to face Erislandy Lara. WBO president Gustavo Olivieri said formal notice would follow. The fighters’ teams will have 20 days from the issuance of that order to reach a deal.

Hernández Has Already Been Through One Purse Bid

“The parties shall have 20 days from the issuance of the formal negotiation order to reach terms, pursuant to WBO Regulations or purse bid proceedings,” Olivieri said on X.

Warriors Boxing was the only bidder for Bentley’s mandatory defense and secured the promotional rights with a $200,000 offer on September 29. Bentley stood to receive $150,000, with the remaining $50,000 going to Hernández. Bentley had asked to fight Shane Mosley Jr. first and defend against Hernández afterward, but the WBO denied his appeal on October 22. He kept the Mosley fight, scheduled for November 7 in London as his Zuffa Boxing debut, and the WBO stripped him.

That first bid shows why the next 20 days matter. Hernández’s promoter did what the WBO process required and put up the money to stage the defense. Bentley still had a fight he preferred to take, and Hernández came out of the process with the same No. 1 ranking he had going in. A deal with Zerafa would spare him another round of bidding and give both camps a chance to settle where the fight takes place and what they’ll be paid.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) brings the bigger punch, but his last fight gave Zerafa something to study. Francisco Verón took him the distance in August and held him to a majority decision. For all the talk about why Bentley took the Mosley fight, that result matters more to Zerafa. There are rounds to win against Hernández if Zerafa can keep him from setting his feet and make him work to close the distance.

The opening for Zerafa came from the two names above him being unavailable. What he can do with it is another matter. Hernández has the power to make this a short night if Zerafa stands in front of him, but the Cuban still has to show he can take charge when an opponent makes him work deep into a fight. That’s what makes the pairing worth seeing once the teams get it signed.

Ghana News.title: Lebanon cocaine bust: Three foreign nationals arrested in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
Three foreign nationals — a Syrian, a Tunisian and a Lebanese — have been arrested in Ghana in connection with the seizure of 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine at the Rafic Hariri International Airport in Beirut, Lebanon.

The arrests form part of investigations into the movement of the consignment from Accra to Beirut and efforts to identify others suspected of involvement in the international drug trafficking network.

JoyNews sources said the suspects, comprising two men and a woman, were picked up in separate operations on Tuesday, November 3.

Two were arrested earlier in the day in Accra, while the third was apprehended at about 5 p.m.

They were arrested by the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) following intelligence shared by Lebanese law enforcement authorities.

The suspects are being investigated to establish the extent of their alleged involvement in the shipment and the wider trafficking network.

Cocaine concealed in luggage

The investigation follows the arrest of a Syrian national at Beirut’s Rafic Hariri International Airport on Saturday, October 31, after he arrived from Accra with cocaine concealed in two pieces of luggage.

Lebanese Customs authorities said officers discovered 40 packages containing a total of 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine during a search of the passenger’s luggage.

The drugs were reportedly concealed using sophisticated packaging and insulation materials intended to evade detection by scanning equipment. Electronic tracking devices were also found among the packages.

Lebanese authorities described the seizure as the largest drug bust in the history of the airport. Preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect had entered Lebanon through the Masnaa border crossing from Syria several weeks earlier before travelling to Accra and returning with the consignment.

The authorities said investigations were continuing to identify the intended recipient of the drugs and to trace those who had organised and facilitated the shipment.

NACOC has maintained that the arrest in Lebanon resulted from a coordinated controlled-delivery operation involving Ghanaian and Lebanese drug law enforcement agencies.

In a statement issued on November 1, the commission said the operation was intended to identify and apprehend individuals at both ends of the supply chain while gathering intelligence to dismantle the wider transnational criminal network.

It also said it was pursuing suspected accomplices in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Why a US-Russia showdown left Morocco celebrating
Ghana News.content:
Morocco has welcomed the end of a decades-long UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after a diplomatic showdown between the US and Russia left the Security Council unable to agree on its future.

The council failed on Friday to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (Minurso) after Russia vetoed a US-backed proposal. A rival Russian draft to extend the mission also failed to secure enough votes.

The decision raises questions about the future of Africa's longest territorial dispute and the fragile ceasefire between Morocco, which claims Western Sahara, and the Polisario Front, which has been fighting for the territory's independence for more than 50 years.

Here is what you need to know.

Why is Western Sahara disputed?

Western Sahara, on Africa's northwest coast, was a Spanish colony until 1975. It has significant phosphate reserves and valuable fishing grounds along its Atlantic coast.

As Spain prepared to withdraw, both Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory.

The International Court of Justice found historical ties of allegiance but no territorial sovereignty that overrode the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination.

Morocco's then King Hassan II responded by organising the Green March. On 6 November 1975, about 350,000 Moroccan civilians entered the territory in a mass demonstration intended to put pressure on Spain.

Days later, Spain signed the Madrid Accords with Morocco and Mauritania, agreeing to transfer administrative control. Morocco took the northern two-thirds and Mauritania the southern third. The agreement did not settle the sovereignty question.

The Polisario Front, an independence movement founded in 1973, opposed the deal. It saw it as replacing Spanish colonial rule with Moroccan and Mauritanian control.

Mauritania renounced its claim in 1979, but Morocco continued fighting Polisario.

Algeria became Polisario's main regional ally, providing military support and hosting its leadership and thousands of Sahrawi refugees in camps near the city of Tindouf.

The North African country says its position is based on the right to self-determination, while Morocco sees Western Sahara as an integral part of its territory.

Morocco and Algeria fought a brief border war in 1963 over disagreements about territory inherited from French colonial rule. Their relationship has remained tense, with Western Sahara at the centre of their dispute.

What was the UN's mission role?

After 16 years of fighting, Morocco and Polisario agreed to a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1991, with a sand wall, or berm, dividing the territory to keep the rival forces apart.

The UN established Minurso to monitor the ceasefire and organise a referendum on the territory's future. Sahrawis were meant to choose between independence and integration with Morocco.

The vote was scheduled for 1992 but never took place. The two sides could not agree on who was eligible to participate, and disputes over voter identification became a major obstacle.

In 2007, Morocco proposed autonomy, which would let Sahrawis manage their internal affairs while Rabat retained control over defence and foreign relations.

Thousands of Moroccans marched into Western Sahara in 1975 in what became known as the Green March

The Polisario Front and Algeria rejected the plan, insisting on a referendum that included independence as an option.

Years of UN-sponsored negotiations failed to produce a breakthrough.

The ceasefire broke down in November 2020, when Polisario said it was resuming armed struggle.

But after a long diplomatic campaign by Morocco, the UN Security Council voted in 2025 to back the autonomy plan as the "most feasible" solution for the disputed territory.

While most Sahrawis live in the part of Western Sahara controlled by Morocco, tens of thousands are estimated to be in refugee camps in Algeria.

What happened at the UN?

The US proposed extending Minurso's mandate for another year, but its draft went beyond the usual renewal.

It would have removed the word "referendum" from the mission's name and made Morocco's autonomy proposal the sole basis for further negotiations.

The draft received the support of 11 of the Security Council's 15 members, including France and the UK but Russia vetoed it, arguing that it was too favourable to Morocco.

Russia then proposed extending Minurso's mandate without changing its terms. That draft also failed, receiving only two votes in favour.

Minurso's mandate expired at the end of Saturday, 31 October. The UN said the following day that the mission had entered a liquidation period, with a reduced team overseeing the transfer of military equipment and other assets.

The UN mission has been in Western Sahara since 1991

UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination must be respected and warned of the risk of renewed hostilities.

The Polisario Front condemned the US proposal. Its representative, Sidi Omar, thanked Russia for vetoing it, saying it would "torpedo the foundations of the UN peace process" and threaten regional and international peace.

Morocco, meanwhile, said the mission's personnel and equipment should leave the territory in the coming days, arguing that the Security Council should no longer consider the Western Sahara issue.

Minurso had 155 military personnel and was expected to cost $62m (£46m) in the financial year beginning in June, according to a UN report.

Why is Morocco celebrating the end of the UN mission?

Morocco's royal palace welcomed the failure to renew Minurso's mandate.

In Laayoune, the territory's largest city, footage showed people celebrating, waving Moroccan flags and displaying portraits of King Mohammed VI.

"The decision is an opportunity for Rabat to challenge what it sees as an international mechanism that has failed to resolve the dispute," Issam Laaroussi, a Moroccan expert in international relations, tells the BBC.

He said Morocco now has more room to push its autonomy proposal and shift negotiations away from a referendum on independence toward autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty.

The decision does not, however, change Western Sahara's legal status or amount to international recognition of Moroccan sovereignty.

Western Sahara remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories, while the African Union officially recognises its independence, as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR).

But the decision comes after several countries backed Morocco's position, which in recent years has made securing international support for its claim central to its foreign policy.

In 2020, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of an agreement to establish diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israel.In 2024,

France also backed Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for resolving the dispute.

Thousands of Sahrawis live in refugee camps in Algeria

Morocco rejoined the African Union in 2017, more than three decades after leaving its predecessor, the Organisation of African Unity, in protest at the SADR's admission.

Since returning, Rabat has sought to build support for its position from within the organisation. At least 10 African countries have opened diplomatic missions in the territory in support of Rabat.

"Morocco is not necessarily seeking to abandon the UN process, but to change the framework for negotiations and draw greater support from regional organisations," says Laaroussi.

Addressing a special joint session of parliament on Monday, House of Representatives Speaker Ahmed Touizi hailed the end of Minurso as a victory for the country's diplomacy.

He said the country should now move from "managing the dispute to implementing its autonomy plan under Moroccan sovereignty, while pressing ahead with development projects in the territory."

Could this lead to a renewed war?

The fear is that Minurso's departure could lead to renewed fighting.

The mission has monitored military developments and helped reduce the risk of escalation.

Aid organisation Oxfam warned that losing its monitoring and de-escalation role could undermine stability, with serious consequences for civilians.

Laaroussi admits that the mission's departure could create security gaps.

"Minurso's departure does not create the original conflict, because the conflict is already there, but it could aggravate an already fragile security environment," he says.

The UN decision has also fuelled nationalist rhetoric online.

Several Moroccan users have shared AI-generated images of themselves in military uniform, declaring their readiness to fight for Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara.

In Morocco, Western Sahara is widely regarded as a national cause. Political parties that are often divided on other issues are united in supporting the country's claim to sovereignty over the territory.

Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita has said the end of the mission does not mean the end of the ceasefire, and that Rabat remains committed to it "within respect of its security and sovereignty."

Polisario has not said what it will do next.

Any resumption of fighting could well draw in Algeria, as tensions with Morocco remain high.

According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), both countries significantly increased military spending last year, with SIPRI citing their dispute over Western Sahara as a key driver.

Algeria spent an estimated $25.4bn, more than four time Morocco's $6.3bn.

Ghana News.title: Libya’s top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
Ghana News.content:
Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo.

The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings.

It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god.

Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name.

The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country.

It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza.

The ruling, known as a fatwa, is a religious opinion on a matter of Islamic law. Libya's Grand Mufti, Sadiq al-Gharyani, approved it.

The BBC has contacted Nike for comment.

The Dar al-Ifta is an influential religious institution based in Tripoli, in western Libya. The country is politically divided, with rival authorities and institutions operating in the east and west after years of conflict following the toppling of long-time leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

Although its religious rulings can carry considerable social influence, they are not necessarily government orders or legally enforceable.

Last year it ruled against wearing jewellery and watches bearing the logo of French luxury jewellery house Van Cleef & Arpels, arguing that its four-leaf clover design was associated with Christian beliefs and the pursuit of good luck, which it said contradicted Islamic teachings.

The latest fatwa does not announce a state ban on Nike products or specify penalties for people who continue to buy or wear them.

Social media reactions were mixed, with some users welcoming the ruling while others questioned its significance, calling it ironic or a distraction from more pressing issues.

The ruling comes amid wider debates over the rise of religious conservatism in public life in Libya.

In 2025, authorities in eastern Libya announced restrictions on rap music, theatre and dance performances, citing concerns that some lyrics and performances violated public morals and Islamic values.

Authorities later extended the measures to western Libya.

The Dar al-Ifta has also previously issued religious rulings against music, although there is no clear evidence that it was directly involved in the restrictions on performances.

Nike does not operate an official store in Libya; however, local sportswear retailers carry Nike-branded products.

Sportswear brands such as Nike and Adidas are popular across North Africa.

In Libya, as in other countries in the region, local markets also sell counterfeit versions of popular sportswear brands.

Ghana News.title: GES cautions teachers against paying money for automatic promotion
Ghana News.content:
Teacher

The Ghana Education Service (GES) has cautioned teachers participating in its ongoing promotion examination against paying money to individuals who claim they can secure them automatic promotion.

The warning follows reports received by management that some unscrupulous individuals are demanding money from candidates under the pretext of facilitating their promotion.

In a press release issued on Tuesday, November 3, the Service stressed that the promotion exercise was transparent and strictly merit-based, insisting that no payment or financial inducement was required or could guarantee a candidate's promotion.

Management, therefore, urged all eligible staff participating in the examination to disregard such demands and refrain from making payments to anyone in exchange for promises of promotion.

The Service also encouraged candidates to approach the examination with confidence, dedication and a positive attitude, while wishing them success in the exercise.

It further called on staff who encounter individuals soliciting money or have information about such fraudulent activities to report the matter to the police.

The GES reiterated that promotion would be determined solely by merit and the established procedures, warning candidates against falling victim to individuals seeking to exploit the exercise for financial gain.

Ghana News.title: ‘Yɛgye Yɛ Sika’ demo: NPP on ‘fishing expedition’ against Ablakwa – NDC
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) of targeting Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa because of his record in exposing alleged corruption.

The party described the NPP’s demands for accountability over the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa as a “fishing expedition”, arguing that the party is attempting to discredit the minister through repeated allegations.

Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Tuesday, November 3, following the NPP’s ‘Yɛgye Yɛ Sika’ demonstration, the National Deputy Communications Director of the NDC, Julius Kwame Anthony, said the opposition was determined to make an example of Mr Ablakwa to discourage others from challenging corruption.

“In fact, I have earlier described them as a group of people who are deep-necked into corruption and see all who have fought corruption in one way or the other as enemies to their cause.

"And they are very desperate to ensure that they make an example of such people so that nobody else will set such an example, the conduct of those people in the fight against corruption under their administration ever again. The Honourable Okudzeto Ablakwa is just being targeted by the NPP. They are on a fishing expedition,” he said.

The NPP staged the demonstration to demand accountability over the evacuation arrangements and called for the removal of Mr Ablakwa.

Mr Anthony accused the opposition of repeatedly making allegations against the minister in the hope that some would eventually gain public acceptance.

"They are on a fishing expedition. They are on a consistent mass slinging, throwing one, if it fails to throw another, with the hope that with time some of it would stick and that other people will watch it and fear that in the events that the people of this country are bedeviled with an NPP administration, they would fear going against that attitude of corruption, which characterized the previous NPP administration," he said.

He maintained that Mr Ablakwa, during his time in opposition, relied on what he described as credible evidence when raising concerns about alleged wrongdoing under the previous NPP administration.

He contrasted this with the NPP’s current demand for invoices relating to chartered flights used in the evacuation exercise, questioning why a political party should receive such documents directly from a state institution.

“I ask myself, at what point in the history of the Republic of Ghana do we have a situation where invoices of transactions of state institutions are sent to the headquarters of political parties? In this case, the NPP is demanding that we bring invoices of chartered flights to them at Asylum Down. At what point does accountability mean that?” he questioned.

He said that concerns about possible financial irregularities in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs should be investigated through the appropriate state institutions.

“If you want accountability and you want to check whether or not there are any infractions in the dealings of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, an audit properly conducted by the institutions of state designated to do so would bring those answers,” he said.

Ghana News.title: NPP questions Ablakwa’s figures in South Africa evacuation, demands independent audit
Ghana News.content:
The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has questioned the figures provided by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa, insisting that an independent audit is needed to establish the actual cost and number of people transported.

He rejected the minister’s decision to invite the Auditor-General to conduct a special audit of evacuation exercises dating back to 2017, arguing that the process should instead be handled by an independent audit firm whose findings would be made public.

Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Tuesday, November 3, the National Youth Organiser of the NPP, Abanga Fuseini Yakubu, said the party did not have confidence in an audit process initiated by the minister, who is at the centre of the controversy.

“What Okudzeto Ablakwa is doing, it is like you having an issue with me and inviting me into your court where you are the same judge in that court and you are going to determine the case. It doesn't make sense, and we don't believe in certain investigations,” he said.

The NPP youth organiser said his party wanted an independent audit of the entire evacuation exercise, with the findings published to the public.

He also raised questions about figures contained in a document released by the Foreign Affairs Ministry following a Right to Information request by the NPP Minority in Parliament.

According to him, the document indicated that 1,964 people were evacuated from South Africa to Ghana, while three chartered flights, each with a capacity of about 300 passengers, were used.

He questioned how the remaining passengers were transported and demanded details of the commercial flights allegedly used, including ticket costs, passenger manifests, seat numbers, and payment vouchers.

"The charter flight carries 300 people, which he chartered three flights. So 300 times three adds up to 900. So leaving the rest of the people on the plane. And that is how we want to know whether those people came with a commercial flight, whether they came with cars or bicycles, how much did he pay for each ticket, each flight, and which seat numbers, the vouchers, the passenger manifest.

"These are legitimate concerns that we are asking for. And we are also asking for the publication of the receipt that he paid for the $750,000 for the charter flight. Because in the commercial market, those ordinarily would not cost more than $150,000 to $300,000."

On concerns raised about commercial flight records, including the identification of only 247 passengers against the minister's reported figure of more than 1,000, Mr Yakubu said the NPP was seeking documentary evidence to establish the actual number of passengers transported.

He maintained that the party's concerns were not politically motivated, citing JoyNews' investigations into the evacuation arrangements as evidence that the questions raised deserved attention.

“I can refer Joy News. The guys who did that wonderful job, I don't believe they are politicians. They only say what they see. And the New Patriotic Party Minority in Parliament are on the same page with what Joy FM did,” he said.

He questioned why the minister and members of the NDC would dismiss the NPP's concerns on political grounds when, in his view, the media investigation had also raised questions about the exercise.

Ghana News.title: MoFA, DMT sign MoU for 21,000-tonne grain storage facility in Wa
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with DMT Collateral Management Limited for the construction of a 21,000-tonne grain storage facility in Wa in the Upper West Region.

The agreement, signed on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at the Ministry in Accra, forms part of efforts under the government's Feed Ghana Programme to expand the country's grain storage capacity, minimise post-harvest losses and strengthen national food security.

The facility is expected to serve as a Food Security Hub, providing strategic grain reserves to support the country during periods of food shortages and other emergencies.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, commended DMT Collateral Management Limited and the Danish Embassy for their role in facilitating the project.

He reaffirmed the Ministry's commitment to supporting the successful implementation of the facility.

The Chief Executive Officer of DMT Collateral Management Limited, Paul Sannie Minlah, said the project would incorporate an emergency grain reserve system known as the Hospital Bin, designed to ensure the availability of food stocks during periods of national need.

The project will be supported by an export credit of approximately €4.8 million facilitated by the Danish Embassy, alongside an additional investment of about €5 million.

Beyond improving grain storage, the facility is also expected to create training opportunities for National Service personnel, members of the Feed Ghana Brigades and Ghanaian technicians.

The training will focus on silo operations, grain handling and maintenance to build local technical capacity and support the efficient management of the facility.

The project is expected to be completed and commissioned by August 2027.

President John Mahama joined other Commonwealth leaders at the opening ceremony of the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda.

President Mahama has also welcomed UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s acknowledgement of the atrocities committed during the slave trade and the British government’s openness to a formal apology and structured dialogue on reparatory justice.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Raphinha, Lamal fire Barcelona to 3-0 Champions League win over Aston Villa
World.content:
Barca took early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued fine goal-scoring form with a second-half brace.

Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the football competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goal-scoring form with a second-half brace.

Barca bounced back after defeat to champions Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top-eight league phase berth.

Manager Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half, but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died of a cardiac arrest on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second-division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

“Yes, it was [a good win]; I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don’t want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus – may he rest in peace,” Raphinha told Movistar.

“This can happen to anyone; it’s very tough … you’re going to play a game, and the same thing can happen to you…

“From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family.”

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.



The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high, and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst.

However, Villa reacted strongly, and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort.

Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball.

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing.

Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner.

Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot.

The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions.

Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games.

Elsewhere on Tuesday, Bayern ‌Munich and PSG underlined their Champions ⁠League title ⁠credentials with victories over Atletico Madrid and Villarreal respectively, while Manchester United came ⁠from two goals down to snatch a dramatic win over AS Roma.

Bayern broke down a stubborn Atletico ⁠side in Madrid as second-half goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer secured victory, while PSG set a record as the fastest team to score four goals in ‌a Champions League match on their way to a 6-0 victory.

At Old Trafford, Matheus Cunha struck twice in quick succession after the break as United overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Roma 3-2, the comeback following protests by home supporters.

World.title: Texans vote in most expensive Senate race in US history
World.content:
Over half a billion dollars have been spent on the Talarico-Paxton race for US Senate, which has been dominated by voter affordability concerns.

Share Texans vote in most expensive Senate race in US history on social media

Houston, Texas, the US – Texas voters have begun casting ballots in a consequential US Senate race that has already become the most expensive in United States history.

All told, at least $573.2m had been poured into support for both Republican candidate Ken Paxton and Democratic candidate James Talarico ahead of the Tuesday, November 3 vote.

The figure has included at least $212m to support Paxton from billionaire Elon Musk, whose SpaceX company is based in southern Texas.

The sum made voters of varying political persuasions queasy as they cast their ballots in a race that has been defined by affordability issues.

“That kind of money is being spent on the wrong stuff,” said Rico Sanchez, a 40-year-old union sheet metal worker who voted for Democrats based on the sky-high cost of living.

“It’s about control,” he said.

Kasey Blanco, a 21-year-old who split his ballot, voting for Republican Governor Greg Abbott and Democratic US Senate candidate Talarico, echoed the sentiment.

“It’s kind of scary,” he said. “You see the extent that a lot of these politicians are trying to get into the game and distort the view.”

Political power “should be from the people, by the people”, Blanco said.

The record spending has included both funds raised by the campaigns, as well as outside spending.

Talarico has outpaced Paxton in campaign funding, raising $155m to Paxton’s $40m. Federal law limits fundraising from individual donors, who must identify themselves.

Separately, a huge amount of money has poured in via political action committees called super PACs, which can spend an unlimited amount in support of a candidate but cannot directly coordinate with campaigns.



Paxton has been the largest beneficiary of such spending, including $168m from Musk to the Senate Leadership Fund, which has gone almost completely to supporting the Republican candidate, according to a New York Times analysis.

The newspaper estimated that Musk, who briefly and controversially led US President Donald Trump’s federal cost-cutting panel, the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), had spent at least $212m on Paxton, noting it was likely an undercount due to so-called “dark money” spending. Trump’s MAGA Inc PAC has spent at least $10m to support Paxton.

The Lone Star Rising PAC, meanwhile, has spent at least $21m on Talarico.

‘Pouring all that money’

With national eyes on Texas, both US Senate candidates gave their closing pitches late Monday.

Talarico seized on Paxton’s past corruption allegations as Texas attorney general, drawing attention to Musk’s spending spree as evidence of prioritising big money interests over everyday voters.

His campaign has regularly referenced the “Friday Night Lights” television show, the story of an underdog American football team.

A Talarico victory would represent the first time a Democrat has won statewide office in Texas since 1994, with the party long hoping to “turn Texas blue”.

“We’re going to do something extraordinary,” Talarico said from San Antonio. “We’re going to do something historic. We’re going to shock the billionaires, shock the world, when we take back Texas.”

Paxton has portrayed Talarico as antithetical to the ideals of Texas, which has been dominated by Republicans for three decades. The state’s low-tax, low-regulation model, mixed with conservative social policies, has long given it special significance in Republican mythos.

Paxton’s campaign has repeatedly referenced the 1836 Texas Revolution, an uprising against then-Mexican control.

“We’ve never been this close to losing everything that we hold dear – our jobs, our livelihoods, our way of life in Texas,” he said at an event in Collin County. “If Texas falls, we don’t have another Texas to move to.”

Casting her ballot on Tuesday, 46-year-old Texas voter Monique Orellana said she was uncomfortable with Musk’s spending.

“He’s pouring all that money out here, trying to get whatever he’s trying to get,” she told Al Jazeera.

Regardless of party, she wanted elected officials to do their job and represent the people.

“I would vote for Republicans if I felt they were gonna do what they said they were gonna do. Right now I’m not feeling it,” she said.

“Trump said he wasn’t going to start a war, and he did anyway. And he said he was going to fix the price of groceries on day one. They went up anyway,” she said.



Voter Luis Plazas, 58, said he was not as concerned about the election spending, but wanted to see the economy improve and a pivot on Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

Still, he said, he voted Republican down the ballot, a decision he said was motivated by his religious beliefs.

“I’m a Christian, so I believe in family values, and it seems like Republicans are more inclined to that,” he said.

“I’m not really happy with the contenders or who I voted for, but my main concern right now is conservative values.”

World.title: French officials eye social media’s role in promoting unrest.
World.content:
Pinned

Hundreds of thousands of protesters took to the streets in cities across France again on Saturday, the latest expression of national grievance that has led to clashes between protesters and the police and kept the country on edge.

As dusk fell and official rallies wound down, unauthorized marches splintered off in Paris, stoking fresh fears of chaos as night approached.

Adding to those fears: Halloween, which falls on Saturday. The French authorities, citing calls on social media for people to revolt that encouraged them to wear masks and costumes, warned that the risk of a new outbreak of violence was high.

In Paris, tensions began flaring between protesters and the police in the late afternoon, as officers fired tear gas at people who refused to disperse. The Paris police estimated that 70,000 people marched in the demonstration, compared with 110,000 last Saturday. After the main demonstration ended, hundreds of protesters, many masked and clad in black, formed an unauthorized procession in eastern Paris.

The interior ministry estimated that nationwide, 320,000 people demonstrated, compared with 410,000 last week. Protesters and the police also clashed in Marseille, Lyon, Toulouse, and Rennes.

Corentin Schnell, a 19-year-old engineering student, took part in the unauthorized march in Paris because, he said, he was angered by accounts of the police using tear gas and stun grenades against protesters in past weeks. “I’ve come to demonstrate and to try to provide medical care — to limit the damage, regardless of which side it’s on,” he said.

Earlier in the week, France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, promised to deploy 70,000 police officers, matching the numbers on Oct. 24. That operation helped keep a lid on outbreaks of arson and looting, although then, too, there were clashes as the police tried to disperse the crowds in the evening.

There was ample fuel for a repeat of those combustible scenes. Students, who are returning to school on Monday after a two-week break, were not mollified by the government’s initial response to their demands. The Education Ministry agreed to cap some class sizes, offer low-interest loans to rebuild school buildings and phase out an unpopular online college admissions platform.

The students vowed to go on protesting. Their two-month-old movement has grown to include university students, public workers and veterans of the “yellow vest” movement that convulsed France from 2018 to 2020.

The authorities have said they are most worried about trouble breaking out after nightfall.

“We are seeing numerous calls to gather coming from the far left, the radicalized extreme left, and from certain radicalized ‘yellow vests’ websites, which are urging people to attend rallies or public gatherings starting at 8 p.m. in many cities across France,” Mr. Nuñez said at a news conference.

Some of the messages were violent, Mr. Nuñez said, calling for “revolution” and “insurrection.” Those gatherings will be forbidden, and any attempt to gather despite the ban will lead to arrests, he said.

Demonstrators have been encouraged on social media to turn up wearing Halloween costumes. Mr. Nuñez warned that it was a criminal offense to conceal one’s face during a demonstration that disrupted public order.

Here’s what else to know.
