Social media: French officials are increasingly concerned about social media’s role in attracting people and inciting violent behavior. Speculation that the government considered temporarily suspending several popular sites drew a denial from President Emmanuel Macron himself. Read more ›

Far-right activists: While the government has blamed far-left activists for much of the mayhem, officials confirmed that bands of young men with links to the far right have also infiltrated the demonstrations. They use the pretext of protecting shop owners but often clash with far-left groups.

Widening movement: The nationwide unrest in France began with a handful of student demonstrations at high schools in suburban Paris last month. Read more ›

Giulia Imbert contributed reporting.

World.title: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
World.content:
Puente announced his decision at the end of a lengthy congressional session on Tuesday evening in which he had outlined new rail safety measures and been grilled by the opposition.

He also said: "I am not only stepping down from my position as minister of transport, but... I am also withdrawing my name from the lists for the early legislative elections."

Puente's position immediately came under scrutiny after the 28 October crash.

The main opposition, the conservative People's Party (PP) and the far-right Vox, were both calling for his resignation - as were some of the government's allies.

They argued that the minister should take responsibility for a high-speed rail system that many Spaniards now regard as unsafe and whose credibility even Socialist Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez admitted was "broken".

The opposition also criticised Puente for appearing to blame human error for the crash, claiming the minister was trying to deflect the blame from his own failings.

But, having said he was going to remain in his post just a few days ago, his resignation appears to have taken many by surprise.

The rail accident and Puente's decision have come at a crucial moment in the Spanish political calendar, with early general elections on 29 November.

Many observers see the accident as a massive electoral setback to the Socialist-led government that will make it impossible for SÃ¡nchez to defy the polls and win the election.

Puente's predicament presented him and the prime minister with a dilemma - refusing to resign might look insensitive in the wake of the accident and stepping down could look like acknowledging he and the government were at fault.

In the end, Puente opted for the second option, insisting his decision had been driven by "political dignity".

Many Spaniards will now ask whether Puente's successors will manage to restore faith in the country's railway system.

World.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
World.content:
Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats.

Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC.

The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing. Authorities have also searched planes in Poland, Spain and Bulgaria.

While officially there is no link between them, authorities from various countries will be co-operating to assess whether this was a co-ordinated attack, designed to disrupt airspace.

The UK government described today's incidents as "malicious hoax threats".

In a statement it said it had "one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we've seen today".

Aviation security expert Paul Mason said bomb threats on passenger planes "don't happen that frequently", which made the latest incidents "unusual".

"It sounds like they've been made in a credible manner across a broad range of airlines," Mason told BBC Radio 5 Live. "That would suggest to me that it's been a very deliberate act by a typical actor rather than a load of coincidental, malicious calls."

He said "there are a lot of processes" that the onboard crew and people on the ground must go through "to validate the credibility of the threat".

A flight may be asked to divert if the credibility of a threat "is of a certain level", Mason added, and in some cases the onboard crew may not even be advised on what the ground operators were dealing with.

World.title: Binance says fake job interviews used as part of $6.3bn crypto hack
World.content:
Hackers who stole a record $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) from Binance used fake job interviews and a compromised internal AI tool, the firm has revealed.

Initial findings published by the company, which operates the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said hackers gained access to its systems through "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign".

It said they used a range of techniques such as malicious software downloads to compromise the computers of Binance engineers and gain control over tools to drain its wallet of billions of dollars worth of crypto.

Binance called it a "serious and highly sophisticated security incident" and apologised, saying "this should not have happened".

In a post on X, external, Binance said hackers targeted its engineers using social engineering techniques.

These see hackers use approaches such as phishing to trick people into parting with sensitive or personal details, that can then be used to try and access their accounts.

Binance said as part of the hack, one of its engineers was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives.

It said the perpetrators used "more advanced and deceptive" methods to build trust with him, such as sharing social media accounts that contained personal images.

The engineer in question was instructed to download malware masquerading as an "assignment" during a second interview, that deployed malicious code with "obfuscation techniques" evading detection.

Binance said hackers then leveraged the engineer's compromised computer and a compromised internal AI tool in October to gain control over two other engineers' laptops, and execute the next steps of the attack.

The incident led Binance to suspend withdrawals for customers globally, meaning users could not get their cryptocurrency out of the platform until the service was restored on Sunday.

Customers withdrew billions of dollars worth of assets after it reopened.

"We apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry," it said.

The company added it had taken a range of steps following the incident, including working with law enforcement to trace and freeze affected assets.

It said it had also set aside more than 100% of the funds needed to cover the loss, noting 98% of the token assets impacted had been "replenished" as of Saturday.

The record $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) attack is thought to be the largest crypto hack to date.

World.title: NTSB says crucial plane parts found three miles from Florida crash site
World.content:
"Knowing that it was lost is a very important piece of evidence in terms of pointing us towards other things to investigate," he said.

Chapman said officials were still working out whether losing the left elevator caused the plane to nosedive or whether the part fell off because "forces on the aircraft caused that to separate".

He said the part of the plane that controls upward and downward movement may not have been "effective" at the speed the plane was travelling.

The Learjet 60 was bound for the Bahamas from Austin, Texas, when it nosedived into a multi-lane highway and exploded on impact.

In air traffic control audio recordings, someone in the cockpit can be heard reporting "moderate turbulence" and that the crew was "managing the ice".

They are then heard saying the plane was "picking up precipitation" and "we need to climb". Moments later, the same voice said the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft (3,048m) per minute.

An emergency was declared and the pilots can be heard yelling "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground".

NTSB plans to investigate the role weather played in the crash. Officials were struggling to access the wreckage due to the huge crater created by the jet on a road in Palm Beach.

Chapman said on Tuesday that the force of the impact severely damaged the wreckage.

Seven passengers died on board, named in a joint statement as tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife, Helen Sharp, and their two children - Emma, four, and Charlie, two - as well as friends of the family Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and Anita Maria Cetina, a nanny.

The pilot was named in media reports as 55-year-old Jeffrey Gregory. Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, who earned her pilot's licence when she was 17, was reported to be the co-pilot.

World.title: Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
World.content:
Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo.

The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings.

It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god.

Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name.

The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country.

It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza.

The ruling, known as a fatwa, is a religious opinion on a matter of Islamic law. It was approved by Libya's Grand Mufti, Sadiq al-Gharyani.

The BBC has contacted Nike for comment.

The Dar al-Ifta is an influential religious institution based in Tripoli, in western Libya. The country is politically divided, with rival authorities and institutions operating in the east and west after years of conflict following the toppling of long-time leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

Although its religious rulings can carry considerable social influence, they are not necessarily government orders or legally enforceable.

Last year it ruled against wearing jewellery and watches bearing the logo of French luxury jewellery house Van Cleef & Arpels, arguing that its four-leaf clover design was associated with Christian beliefs and the pursuit of good luck, which it said contradicted Islamic teachings.

The latest fatwa does not announce a state ban on Nike products or specify penalties for people who continue to buy or wear them.

Social media reactions were mixed, with some users welcoming the ruling, while others questioned its significance, describing it as ironic or a distraction from more pressing issues.

The ruling comes amid wider debates over the rise of religious conservatism in public life in Libya.

In 2025, authorities in eastern Libya announced restrictions on rap music, theatre and dance performances, citing concerns that some lyrics and performances violated public morals and Islamic values.

The measures were subsequently extended to western Libya.

The Dar al-Ifta has also previously issued religious rulings against music, although there is no clear evidence that it was directly involved in the restrictions on performances.

Nike does not operate an official store in Libya, however Nike-branded products are available through local sportswear retailers.

Sportswear brands such as Nike and Adidas are popular across North Africa.

In Libya, as in other countries in the region, counterfeit versions of popular sportswear brands are also sold in local markets.

World.title: Europe on alert after supermarket freezers hit by cyber-attacks in 10 countries
World.content:
The European Union has raised concerns about the attacks, which come three weeks after a cyber-attack disrupted as many as 700 French grocery stores, causing food losses estimated at tens of millions of euros.

The security of refrigeration systems as well as other devices that can be monitored remotely has heightened concerns about government-backed hybrid attacks.

The EU's food and agriculture commissioner, Christophe Hansen, said the bloc was taking the incidents very seriously and warned of further disruption in the future.

Commission spokesman Thomas Regnier was careful not to attribute blame, but said: "These incidents of course show once again how cyber-attacks can disrupt essential services and affect citizens' daily lives."

"These are not isolated incidents and of course we have to be collectively resilient and prepared for such cyber incidents."

In Italy, Giorgia Meloni's government called a meeting with intelligence chiefs, but said the impact was "currently very limited" and most of the food distribution chain had up-to-date security systems able to fend off such attacks.

At least four Co-op supermarkets in Sicily and one business in Tuscany were affected, according to the national cybersecurity agency.

Meloni's office said those businesses affected were "mostly still equipped with obsolete security systems, with interfaces directly exposed to the internet and inadequate authentication mechanisms".

Belgian supermarkets were among those hardest-hit, with dozens of stores reporting refrigeration failures. Federal prosecutors have opened an investigation.

World.title: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
World.content:
Russian strikes on Ukraine â including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital â have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others over the last 24 hours.

At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.

He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".

Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added.

The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said.

Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.

Nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha as residents were gathering to receive humanitarian aid at a distribution centre, authorities said. Local media reported that when the attack began, people took refuge underground but the roof collapsed, trapping many underneath.

"The scale of the tragedy is difficult to comprehend," regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.

Russia's defense ministry said the attack had targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen.

However, there was no credible evidence that the site was being used by the Ukrainian military and there were no major military or industrial facilities in the settlement of Komyshuvakha, reports BBC News Russian defence correspondent Ilya Abishev.

The village is to the south-east of the city of Zaporizhzhia, which has come under constant Russian bombardment.

According to Abishev, Komyshuvakha is of high military importance as part of Ukraine's defensive and transport network on the approaches to the regional capital.

But the UN's human rights monitoring mission said the distribution of humanitarian aid at the local school had been highly publicised and the attack "seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law", external.

World.title: US strikes Iranian island ahead of midterm elections
World.content:
The US has carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials have told CBS, the BBC's US partner.

The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing on a US aircraft.

Iranian state news agency Irna reported explosions on Qeshm on Monday. The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.

The US military has not commented on the strikes, which came as mediators stepped up their efforts to prevent a return to all-out war after the US midterm elections on Tuesday.

Trump has been facing falling polling numbers and pressure from within his Republican Party to end the war, which began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in February.

Earlier on Monday, the president told reporters that he was in "no rush" to ramp up strikes on Iran.

"One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially," he told news outlet Axios. "They have no money, no gasoline and their people are getting very tired of it."

He also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme, in an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms.

This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump added.

There has been mounting speculation in the last few days that the US may resume significant strikes in Iran again after the midterms. But asked by a reporter on Monday if that was the case, Trump said "no".

Meanwhile, the Associated Press cited two regional officials as saying that, during a weekend phone call, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had pushed Trump for another wave of strikes on Iran following the midterms.

World.title: Ogun reconstitutes Awujale Interregnum Council, names Adesanya Chairman, Okunowo Secretary
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has announced the reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), reaffirming its legal authority to oversee the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale.

The decision follows the reported withdrawal of some members of the council, established by the state government in August 2025, amid disagreements over the emergence of a group reportedly known as Adele Oba Awujale.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat, the government said the withdrawal of some members did not invalidate the council, which remained the only legally recognised administrative body empowered to manage the affairs of Ijebuland during the interregnum.

The government clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal.

Addressing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale group, the government declared that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy legislation in Ogun State.

According to the statement, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Obas and Chiefs Law of Ogun State 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the management of the Awujale stool.

It further explained that the Chiefs Law of 1957, which some former members reportedly relied upon to justify the emergence of the group, was a pre-independence legislation that no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The government also cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya (the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode) against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others, as judicial affirmation of the legality and authority of the AIAC.

It noted that all members of the council were parties to the suit and had consented to the judgment, which acknowledged the legality, validity and authority of the administrative body established by the state government to oversee the administrative and traditional responsibilities of Ijebu-Ode pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale.

The government further recalled that the court affirmed that where there was a conflict between the responsibilities of the administrative body and the traditional functions of the Olisa, the authority of the administrative body would take precedence.

It stressed that the judgment had not been appealed and remained binding on the parties.

While acknowledging the right of individual members to withdraw from the council, the government maintained that such decisions could not confer legal authority on another body to assume the responsibilities of the AIAC.

It consequently warned members of the public against engaging in official transactions or administrative dealings with individuals who had withdrawn from the council in their purported capacity as members of an alternative administrative body.

The government also urged the former members to refrain from actions capable of contravening the law or undermining the peace and stability of Ijebuland.

To ensure continuity in the administration of Ijebuland during the interregnum, the government announced the reconstitution of the council with the following members:

1. Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Olisa of Ijebu-Ode – Chairman.

2. Chief Chris Okunowo, Bobasuwa – Secretary.

3. Professor Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso – Member.

4. Chief Stephen O Bakare, Babalaje – Member.

5. Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun – Member.

The government said the reconstituted council would continue to discharge the legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities of the AIAC until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned.

It reaffirmed its commitment to upholding the rule of law, respecting established traditional institutions and ensuring a peaceful and transparent process in the succession to the vacant Awujale stool.

World.title: ADC warns Sokoto govt, vows to hold governor responsible for intimidation, violence against opposition
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has warned Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu that it will hold him responsible for any violence against opposition members as the party prepares to launch its presidential campaign in the state on Wednesday.

The warning came on Tuesday, a day after the state government sealed an ADC campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto, citing a property ownership dispute and security concerns.

In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC accused the state government of political intimidation and demanded an end to interference with its activities.

“The Sokoto State Government must understand that governing a state does not confer ownership,” the statement said. “No governor has the power to decide which party can campaign, which candidate can speak, or which political choices the people of Sokoto are allowed to consider.”

The party warned that public officials who obstruct lawful political activities should be prepared to face legal consequences.

Dispute over campaign activities

Commissioner for Lands and Housing Nasiru Dantsoho said government records showed that the sealed property belonged to Savannah Bank, with no documented transfer of ownership.

He said the government had written to the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) for clarification and would keep the premises sealed pending a response.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Dantsoho also cited a disturbance involving political supporters near the property as a reason for the closure.

Aminu Abdullahi, spokesperson for ADC governorship candidate Manir Dan’iya, alleged that the government demanded ₦30 million for a venue for the campaign launch.

He said the party agreed to the amount but was not provided with payment details. PREMIUM TIMES has not independently confirmed the alleged demand or obtained a government response to it.

The office closure followed an alleged attack on Mr Dan’iya’s convoy near Sokoto airport on 30 October.

The governorship candidate accused personnel linked to state security outfits of obstructing his convoy and damaging his vehicle. The All Progressives Congress (APC) disputed allegations of politically motivated violence, while police said they were investigating the incident.

Separately on Tuesday, Atiku Abubakar accused the State Security Service of recruiting protesters to disrupt Wednesday’s campaign launch.

He alleged that the protesters were being mobilised to create disorder that could justify a curfew and stop the event. This newspaper has not independently established the allegation. The SSS had not responded to earlier enquiries at the time of that report.

The ADC said it would proceed with the launch despite the dispute.

“Let there be no misunderstanding. The ADC will campaign in Sokoto State. We will not be intimidated, obstructed or pushed out of any part of Nigeria,” the party said.

It urged its supporters to remain peaceful and called on security agencies to protect the rights of all political parties.

World.title: Enugu govt empowers 520 vulnerable persons with grinding machines
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has empowered 520 vulnerable persons across the 260 wards of the state with grinding machines to improve their economic well-being and reduce poverty.

The beneficiaries, drawn from the 17 council areas, received the machines during an empowerment programme organised by the state Ministry of Human Development and Poverty Eradication in Enugu on Tuesday.

Distributing the machines on behalf of Governor Peter Mbah, the Secretary to the Enugu State Government (SSG), Chidiebere Onyia, said the intervention was part of the administration’s commitment to human capital development and poverty eradication.

Mr Onyia said the administration had, from inception, set a target of reducing the state’s poverty headcount index from 58 per cent to zero.

He described the distribution as one of several interventions designed to support vulnerable persons and improve their economic independence.

The SSG said the state government did not only build roads, schools and hospitals but also support the poor in the state.

According to him, the beneficiaries were selected based on clearly defined socio-economic indicators to ensure that the intervention reached genuine vulnerable households.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“What you are experiencing today is just one of the interventions put in place to ensure that vulnerable persons develop skills and use the equipment for productive economic activities.

“The aim is to enable them to generate income and have more disposable revenue to improve their quality of life,” said Mr Onyia, a professor.

He said the government had also established a monitoring mechanism through the Ministry of Budget and Planning to track the use of the equipment and ensure that beneficiaries put them to productive purposes.

He cautioned the beneficiaries against selling the machines, stressing that the equipment was provided to promote self-sufficiency and not for resale.

The SSG added that the empowerment programme would be sustained, noting that beneficiaries would also be supported with agricultural inputs, digital skills training and other interventions across relevant sectors.

He said the government would continue to use data to plan, monitor and evaluate its interventions to ensure that they produced measurable results.

How beneficiaries were selected

In her welcome address, the state Commissioner for Human Development and Poverty Eradication, Benedette Okoli, said the distribution was organised to commemorate the 2026 International Day of the Poor.

Ms Okoli said the 520 machines were allocated to two vulnerable persons from each of the 260 political wards across the state’s 17 local government areas.

She said the programme was made possible through the approval of Governor Mbah, whose administration remained committed to improving the welfare of poor and vulnerable citizens.

According to her, the grinding machines are not merely equipment but economic empowerment tools that will enable beneficiaries to engage in productive activities, generate income and support their families.

The commissioner said the beneficiaries were selected from the Enugu State Social Register of the Poor and Vulnerable, prepared by the State Operations Coordinating Unit (SOCU).

She explained that the selection process was transparent and free from political considerations, favouritism or personal connections.

She assured them that the ministry would work with relevant stakeholders to monitor the programme and provide the necessary support to ensure lasting benefits.

Also speaking, the State Coordinator of SOCU, Joy-Blossom Eneh, represented by the Head of Monitoring and Evaluation, Christopher Nnam, expressed appreciation to the governor for supporting the use of the state’s social register to identify vulnerable households.

Mrs Eneh said the social register had provided an evidence-based approach to identifying beneficiaries and ensuring that government interventions reached those who genuinely needed assistance.

She said the unit had captured 586 beneficiaries, including indigent persons and petty traders, for various government interventions.

She described the empowerment programme as evidence that the governor’s commitment to using the social register was yielding tangible results.

One of the beneficiaries, Ndidamaka Ejiri from Igboetiti Local Government Area, while responding on behalf of others, expressed gratitude to the state government.

Mrs Ejiri said the machine would, no doubt, significantly improve their family’s income.

“I thank Governor Peter Mbah for this gesture. Coming 2027, my vote belongs to him, and I promise to put the equipment into productive use to help myself and my family,” she said.

(NAN)

World.title: Police probe teenager’s corpse found in Cross River community
World.content:
The Police Command in Cross River State has begun an investigation following the discovery of the beheaded body of an unidentified teenager in Yahe River, Yala Local Government Area of the state.

The victim, believed to be about 16 years old, was discovered dead in the river on Tuesday, 27 October, with his head severed from his body.

Sunday Eitokpah, the police spokesperson in Cross River, disclosed this in a statement on Monday in Calabar.

Mr Eitokpah, an assistant superintendent of police, said the incident was reported at about 5:30 p.m. by the Officer-in-Charge of Yahe Outstation, Ekurbe Abi, an assistant superintendent of police, which led to the recovery of the body from the river.

He said bloodstains were observed at the scene, raising concerns about the circumstances surrounding the teenager’s death.

According to him, the corpse was subjected to medical examination and subsequently deposited in the mortuary, while efforts are ongoing to establish the identity of the deceased.

The Commissioner of Police in Cross River, Ajo Ordue, has directed a thorough investigation to ensure that anyone found responsible is brought to justice, according to the statement.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ordue appealed to residents of Yahe and neighbouring communities to report any missing person matching the deceased’s description or provide credible information that could assist the investigation.

He urged members of the public with useful information to contact the nearest police station or the command control room.

He assured residents that further developments would be communicated as the investigation progresses.

(NAN)

World.title: We can’t find enough private jets to hire for our campaigns – Akpabio
World.content:
Nigeria’s Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, has said he and other politicians preparing for the 2027 general elections are finding it difficult to hire private jets to travel between locations for their campaigns.

Mr Akpabio attributed the difficulty to the inability of private airline operators in Nigeria to adequately meet the demand for air travels.

He made the remarks during plenary on Tuesday when lawmakers were debating a motion seeking to enforce the Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA) between Nigeria and China.

The motion, sponsored by Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North), urged the Bola Tinubu administration to renegotiate the agreement to allow Nigerian airlines to operate direct flights to China.

Using the festive season, particularly in December, to illustrate the pressure on the country’s aviation sector, Mr Akpabio urged the federal government to address the challenges facing domestic airline operators.

“Watch December and the confusion. Even the private airlines cannot handle it. Common campaigns, we cannot see even private jets to hire. We should at least be able to urge the federal government to look into that to alleviate the plight of airlines,” he said.

Mr Akpabio also recalled when the country operated a national carrier, Nigerian Airways, which he said transported pilgrims from Nigeria to Saudi Arabia for religious pilgrimage.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the airline once had between 32 and 40 aircraft, which operated flights to different destinations, and questioned how the country’s aviation industry had deteriorated to its current state.

“We used to have a plane in those days carrying people to Saudi Arabia and all that. At the time, Nigerian Airways had about 32 planes on ground, about 40, going from one place to the other. So, how did we get here?” he asked.

The senate president maintained that Nigeria needed a national carrier capable of flying the country’s flag.

Politician flying private jets

The use of private jets by Nigerian politicians and top government officials has become a common feature of political campaigns and official travels, despite the enormous cost of chartering such aircraft.

During election campaigns, particularly presidential elections, candidates and their political parties often spend millions of naira hiring private jets to move between states and attend rallies, campaign events and political meetings within tight schedules.

Presidential candidates, in particular, rely on chartered aircraft to cover multiple locations across the country, given the demands of nationwide campaigns and the need to travel with their aides, security personnel and campaign teams. The cost of such flights varies depending on the aircraft type, distance, duration of hire and other operational considerations.

Online reports estimated that private jet charter rates in Nigeria range from $5,000 to $7,000 (from about ₦6.6 million to ₦9.3 million) per flight hour, depending on the aircraft type, capacity, route and operating conditions. This means that politicians could spend between $30,000 and $42,000 (about ₦38.8 million to ₦55.7 million) on a four-to-six-hour trip.

The trend is not limited to presidential candidates. Governors, federal lawmakers, ministers and other senior government officials also use privately owned or chartered aircraft for domestic and international journeys, often referencing tight schedules, security considerations and the convenience of travelling without relying on commercial flight schedules. Some top officials also have access to government-owned aircraft or presidential fleet services for official engagements.

The practice also extends to international travels. Public records and previous reports have documented the use of chartered private aircraft by senior government officials on overseas trips. For instance, former President Goodluck Jonathan told a UK court in 2026 that he approved the use of private jets by former Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke for some foreign trips.

World.title: OgunLNG, Deep Sea Port triggering fresh investor rush, says Abiodun
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has disclosed that the planned $7 billion Gateway Deep Sea Port and the proposed $10 billion Ogun Liquefied Natural Gas (OgunLNG) project are attracting fresh waves of investors to the state, positioning it for a new phase of industrial expansion and economic growth.

The governor said the strategic investments, alongside the proposed Ogun Blue Marine and Special Economic Zone and the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway being constructed by the Federal Government, were opening up unprecedented economic opportunities and generating growing interest among local and international investors.

Abiodun made this known on Tuesday in Ijebu-Ode during the town hall meeting on the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) and the 2027 Budget, organised by the Ministry of Budget and Planning.

He described the planned Deep Sea Port as a defining legacy project of his administration, noting that the agreements recently signed in Paris with DP World would attract approximately $7 billion in private-sector investment into Ogun State.

According to him, the agreements cover the development of the Gateway Deep Sea Port and the Ogun Blue Marine and Special Economic Zone, which are expected to transform the state’s maritime, logistics, manufacturing and industrial landscape.

“In September, I had the privilege of travelling to Paris to sign a landmark agreement that will be the biggest legacy of my administration, and that agreement is for the construction of the Ogun Deep Sea Port.

“That day, we signed two agreements: one for the Deep Sea Port and the other for the Ogun Blue Marine and Special Processing Zone. These combined agreements translate to an investment of about $7 billion of private capital, with no government investment,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor added that the proposed $10 billion OgunLNG project, being developed with the involvement of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC), would further strengthen the state’s investment prospects, while the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would enhance connectivity and open up new economic corridors.

He said the convergence of these major projects had significantly increased investors’ interest in Ogun, with the state witnessing growing pressure from prospective investors seeking to establish businesses and take advantage of the emerging opportunities.

Abiodun noted that his administration’s investment in infrastructure, human capital development and the provision of an enabling business environment since 2019 had laid the foundation for the state’s growing economic profile.

Reviewing his administration’s achievements, the governor disclosed that over 1,700 kilometres of roads had been constructed or rehabilitated across the state, with substantial interventions also undertaken in healthcare, education, agriculture, electricity and security.

He listed the Gateway Medical Centre of Excellence, the rehabilitation of more than 1,600 public schools, the recruitment of over 6,000 teachers and support for thousands of farmers among the major interventions undertaken by his administration.

On electricity, Abiodun disclosed that power plants had been installed in Abeokuta, while similar facilities would be established in Ijebu-Ode and Remo to improve electricity supply, stimulate commercial activities and support industrial development across the state.

He specifically highlighted the administration’s interventions in Ijebu Division, including the reconstruction and rehabilitation of roads in Oru, Awa, Ilaporu, Ago-Iwoye, Eruwon and Atan, among other communities.

In Ijebu-Ode, he said, the government had constructed 26 roads, reflecting its commitment to improving connectivity and opening up communities to economic opportunities.

The governor described the town hall meeting as particularly significant, being the last of such budget consultations to be held by his administration, and an opportunity for residents to make meaningful contributions to the priorities and direction of the 2027 fiscal plan.

He said the budget would be anchored on the state’s 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, with emphasis on realistic spending, the completion of ongoing projects, the delivery of essential services and investments that would generate sustainable economic growth.

“My responsibility is to present a realistic and transparent budget that will complete all ongoing projects and provide essential services,” he said.

Abiodun expressed appreciation to the people of Ogun State for their cooperation and support over the past seven years, assuring them that his administration would remain focused on delivering its commitments until the end of its tenure.

He further stressed the importance of sustaining government policies and programmes beyond his administration, noting that development should be a continuous process rather than one tied to a particular government.

The governor urged traditional rulers, community leaders, religious organisations, professional bodies and other stakeholders to actively participate in the budget preparation process by identifying the specific developmental needs of their communities and offering practical recommendations.

He assured participants that submissions made at the meeting would be carefully considered in the preparation of the 2027 budget.

Abiodun, however, explained that proposals that could not be accommodated in the 2027 fiscal document would be documented as an annexure and transmitted to the incoming administration to ensure that legitimate community needs and development priorities were not lost in the transition.

He reiterated his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, equitable development and the creation of economic opportunities that would improve the living conditions of residents across the state.

Earlier in his opening remarks, the Chief Economic Adviser and Commissioner for Finance, Mr Dapo Okubadejo, said the government’s development agenda was centred on infrastructure provision, improved access to essential services and the creation of an enabling environment for economic activities and individual prosperity.

Okubadejo described governance as a shared responsibility and urged residents to partner with the government in ensuring that the state’s resources were deployed to areas where they would deliver the greatest benefits to the people.

World.title: Toluwanisings’ wife, father, associates sign peace undertaking over burial dispute’ — Police
World.content:
The Oyo State Police Command has stepped in to settle the disagreement between the family and associates of the late Nigerian singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji over where to bury him.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the singer’s family opposed plans by his wife, Elizabeth, and associates to bury him in a cemetery, insisting that his remains should instead be laid to rest at his residence.

The disagreement attracted widespread attention on social media, with the family threatening to exhume his body if the parties buried him in a cemetery.

The family also demanded that the authorities establish the circumstances surrounding his death before proceeding with the burial, citing suspicions of foul play.

Peace deal

The police spokesperson, Ayanlade Olayinka, disclosed the intervention in a statement on Tuesday, explaining that the command acted after the disagreement generated allegations of conspiracy, defamation and conduct capable of breaching public peace.

According to Mr Olayinka, the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received reports about the dispute over the proposed burial arrangements, which escalated into heated exchanges across various public communication platforms.

He said: “In view of the potential implications of the disagreement for public peace and order, the Commissioner of Police, exercising his statutory responsibilities under Section 4 of the Police Act and other relevant provisions of the law, directed that all parties be invited to the Command Headquarters, Eleyele, Ibadan, for an intervention aimed at preventing further escalation and facilitating an amicable resolution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Consequently, at the conclusion of the engagement held today, 3rd November 2026, all parties, comprising the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunmi Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as the deceased’s personal assistant and other representatives, entered into and signed a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police.”

Undertaking

Mr Olayinka further disclosed that the parties had resolved to maintain peace and ensure good conduct.

He said they also pledged to avoid anything that could trigger unrest and discontinue public exchanges, interviews and discussions that might escalate tensions surrounding the singer’s death and other related issues.

“Furthermore, the parties expressly undertook to discontinue the dissemination of information, narratives, allegations and publications relating to the matter through social media platforms, print media, radio, blogs and other communication channels, including publications made through their respective proxies, agents, associates and representatives”, he said.

Mr Olayinka further disclosed that Toluwani’s family, wife and associates resolved to refrain from granting interviews or providing access to individuals and media platforms seeking to publicise further accounts of the dispute.

He added that all parties agreed to caution their representatives and associates against making or circulating statements, sponsoring publications or amplifying content that could revive the disagreement or jeopardise the peace agreement.

“In reinforcing the terms of the undertaking, the Commissioner of Police warned that the agreement must be respected by all parties and extended to their proxies, agents, associates and representatives.

“He cautioned that no individual should take advantage of the unfortunate circumstances surrounding the singer’s demise to instigate hostility, promote unsubstantiated allegations or engage in conduct capable of disrupting public peace. Any person whose actions constitute an offence under applicable laws will be arrested and prosecuted accordingly.”

Bloggers and media

Additionally, Mr Olayinka urged members of the public, bloggers, media practitioners and other interested parties to act responsibly and honour the agreement reached by both parties.

He warned media organisations and bloggers against circulating unverified reports or content that could trigger fresh tensions.

“All concerned are advised to respect the commitments made by the parties, as any conduct independently amounting to a criminal offence will be addressed in accordance with the law.”

He assured Nigerians that the command would continue to protect lives and property, tackle criminal activities and preserve public order across the state.

Mr Olayinka appealed to all parties to respect their agreements and pursue a peaceful resolution through lawful channels.

This newspaper reported that the “Kabiyesi Olorun Ayo” crooner died after he slumped at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State, on 15 October.

World.title: 2027: Now that Governor Alex Otti has declared, By Ferdinand Ekeoma
World.content:
Now that Governor Alex Otti has declared, these are the pictures that will campaign for him. These pictures speak eloquently about what is happening on Obohia Road.

These are real explanations captured in pictures. They are not promises, neither are they stories. They are not folktales, and not fantasies. They are facts you can touch, roads you can drive on.

This was how Port Harcourt Road was dealt with. This was how Ohanku Road was rescued. This is how Obohia and Omuma Roads are presently being dealt with. This is the same onslaught being unleashed on Uratta Road and Old Express Road.

For decades, these roads were synonymous with pain, flood, and abandonment. Today, they are symbols of recovery, commerce, and dignity. Go to Port Harcourt Road and see a six-lane artery with an underground tunnel drainage system. Go to Ohanku and see a road that has brought relief to thousands of traders and residents. Go to Obohia and Omuma and see history being rewritten in real time.

As campaigns gradually gather momentum, we shall be showing our people these modest but monumental interventions — their economic impact, how they have revived Aba, restored pride to Umuahia, reconnected rural communities, created jobs, and how our Governor intends to sustain this momentum of transformation across Abia.

Dear peace-loving Abians, join us in telling these stories. Do not yield to the temptations and provocations of Children of Anger and abandon the real issues, which are governance and development.

Ignore hate speech, divisive tantrums and distractions — they are the weapons of the weak. Defeat distortions and falsehoods with facts and figures. Let achievements speak where propaganda shouts.

Indeed, help is here at last.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

*Ferdinand Ekeoma is the Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to Governor Alex Otti of Abia State.

World.title: 2027: Opposition criticism won’t weaken Tinubu’s Northern support — Illiyasu Kwankwaso
World.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

An influential member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Musa Illiyasu Kwankwaso, has dismissed opposition criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, insisting that it would not weaken the President’s support base in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Kwankwaso said supporters of Tinubu in the North remained committed to his re-election bid despite sustained criticism from opposition politicians.

He stated this on Tuesday while hosting journalists in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital, where he described Tinubu as the right candidate for the 2027 presidential election.

“There is no panic and no going back in our support for Tinubu. The criticisms coming from the opposition will not stop us from voting for him in the North,” he said.

The APC chieftain described the opposition’s criticism as part of political manoeuvring ahead of the 2027 elections, arguing that political rhetoric alone would not diminish what he characterised as the President’s growing support across the region.

According to him, northern voters are increasingly concerned about issues directly affecting their lives, including economic recovery, security, infrastructure development, employment and national stability.

He maintained that the administration’s policies, programmes and achievements since assuming office had strengthened confidence among its supporters, although he did not provide specific indicators to substantiate the claim.

Kwankwaso said supporters of the President would intensify grassroots mobilisation across northern communities to communicate the administration’s policies and highlight what they consider its achievements.

He urged APC members not to be distracted by opposition narratives but to concentrate on strengthening party structures and maintaining regular engagement with voters ahead of the elections.

The APC stalwart expressed confidence that the political coalition backing Tinubu would remain united and focused, adding that supporters were prepared to defend the administration’s record and seek a fresh mandate based on its performance.

He called on Tinubu’s supporters across northern Nigeria to remain committed, describing the 2027 elections as an opportunity to sustain ongoing government policies and programmes and give the President more time to consolidate his administration’s development agenda.

World.title: 2027: Akume’s allies disown Alia’s campaign council as Benue APC supremacy war deepens
World.content:
Akume-Alia

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

A fresh supremacy battle has erupted in the Benue State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, following the rejection of about 500-man campaign council for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Hyacinth Alia by the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, a political mobilisation platform associated with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume.

The disagreement followed Monday’s announcement by the APC State Organising Secretary, James Ornguga, of a joint campaign council for Tinubu and Alia ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also fixed Thursday, November 5, for the inauguration of the council in Makurdi, with a supplementary list expected to be released later.

However, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, in a disclaimer issued Tuesday and signed by its Director-General, Chief Akange Audu, disowned the purported campaign structure, alleging that the names of its conveners, members and political candidates had been included without their authorisation.

The Alliance specifically faulted the inclusion of its conveners, Senator Jack Tilley-Gyado, and Elder Simon Shango, as well as its candidates for the National Assembly and Benue State House of Assembly, in the list of the purported Alia campaign council.

It stated, “for the avoidance of doubt, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 categorically dissociates itself from the said publication and disowns any claim or suggestion that the individuals mentioned therein are associated with, or constitute members of, the purported Alia Campaign structure.”

The group further questioned the political arrangement that reportedly placed Governor Alia as chairman of the campaign council while listing Akume, whom it described as the founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, as merely a member.

According to the Alliance, “We find it particularly contentious that a purported Alia Campaign structure would designate Governor Hyacinth Alia as its Chairman while listing the Founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, Sen. George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, merely as a member.”

The Akume-aligned group alleged that “since the APC secured victory in the 2023 general elections, the party’s established leadership and structures have, in practical terms, been sidelined by the Alia administration. This has contributed to the divisions and disagreements currently affecting the party in the state.”

Despite rejecting the campaign council, the group insisted that “the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 remains committed to its stated mandate of mobilising support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

“Our political engagement also extends to supporting APC candidates for the National Assembly and the Benue State House of Assembly who emerge from the list and leadership direction recognised by our leader, Sen. George Akume.”

The Alliance also took a swipe at the Alia-led administration, saying “we remain concerned about the hardship experienced by the people of Benue State under the present administration of Governor Hyacinth Alia. We believe that the 2027 political process should provide an opportunity for constructive engagement on governance, accountability, party unity and the welfare of our people.

“The Alliance is an independent and clearly structured political mobilisation platform. Its identity, leadership and membership cannot be appropriated, manipulated or misrepresented through unauthorised publications.

“We therefore urge APC State, Local Government, Ward Executives, stakeholders, members and the general public to disregard the purported publication.”

World.title: Youth Forum backs Audi, warns against removal campaign
World.content:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The Patriotic Nigeria Youth Forum (PNYF) has passed a vote of confidence on the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, warning that campaigns for his removal could undermine ongoing reforms and efforts to protect the nation’s critical infrastructure.

The forum said leadership continuity was important to consolidating the gains recorded by the Corps in professionalism, operational capacity and institutional development.

National Coordinator of PNYF, Comrade Olamide Odumosu, stated the position during the forum’s 2026 National Youth Day celebration, held under the theme, “Reimagining the Nigerian Youth: Leadership, Innovation and a Greater Nation.”

Odumosu specifically cautioned individuals and groups, including Mr Deji Adeyanju, reportedly campaigning for Audi’s removal, urging them to support their concerns with verifiable evidence rather than engage in activities capable of distracting the security agency from its statutory responsibilities.

He said decisions concerning the leadership of a strategic security institution should be guided by measurable performance, facts and the national interest.

According to him, the NSCDC has recorded improvements under Audi, particularly in protecting critical national assets, including oil and gas facilities, electricity installations, telecommunications infrastructure and other strategic public facilities.

“Before our eyes, the NSCDC under Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi has undergone remarkable transformation. The Corps has moved beyond its previous limitations and is increasingly demonstrating the professionalism, discipline and operational capacity expected of a modern security institution,” he said.

Odumosu added that Audi had demonstrated an understanding of institutional development and the strategic importance of protecting infrastructure vital to Nigeria’s economic stability and national security.

“These achievements deserve recognition and encouragement,” he said.

The forum maintained that sustained leadership could help consolidate ongoing reforms, particularly as the protection of critical infrastructure remained central to the country’s security and economic development.

It urged those dissatisfied with the Commandant-General’s leadership to channel their grievances through constructive engagement and evidence-based criticism rather than campaigns it said could generate unnecessary distractions.

Odumosu also expressed support for President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, describing the protection of critical national assets as an important component of efforts to strengthen national security and stimulate economic growth.

He called on Nigerians, particularly young people, to support security agencies and recognise the contributions of personnel working to protect lives, property and essential infrastructure.

Forum seeks greater investment in youths

Beyond the debate over the NSCDC leadership, the forum called on the Federal Government and private sector to increase investment in skills development, entrepreneurship and employment opportunities for young Nigerians.

Odumosu identified unemployment, poverty, inadequate access to quality education, insecurity and limited economic opportunities as major challenges confronting the country’s youth.

He urged the government to prioritise digital skills, artificial intelligence, vocational education, research, entrepreneurship and greater youth participation in governance.

The PNYF coordinator also challenged private companies to expand opportunities for young people through employment, internships, mentorship schemes, innovation grants and enterprise development programmes.

“Investing in young people is not charity; it is an investment in Nigeria’s economic growth, stability and prosperity,” he said.

He stressed that addressing the challenges facing young Nigerians required sustained collaboration among government institutions, businesses and civil society organisations.

Odumosu reaffirmed the forum’s commitment to promoting responsible citizenship, leadership development, patriotism, innovation and national unity.

He also urged young Nigerians to embrace peaceful democratic participation, respect for the rule of law and active involvement in national development, saying the country’s future depended significantly on their contributions towards building a secure and prosperous nation.

World.title: Rising feed costs threaten poultry, livestock farming in 3 states
World.content:
Farmers in Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states have warned that rising feed costs, expensive day-old chicks and poor market prices threaten livestock production and livelihoods.

They said the situation had forced some operators to reduce production, sell their animals at losses or abandon farming altogether.

The farmers spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Tuesday during a nationwide survey in Minna.

They identified high feed costs, which account for 70 to 80 per cent of poultry production expenses, as their biggest challenge.

They called for subsidised feed ingredients, affordable financing, improved access to essential inputs and local feed mills to reduce production costs.

In Kogi, a poultry farmer and retired Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security director, Mr Dare Olukaiyeja, said feeding accounted for 80 per cent of his production costs.

Olukaiyeja, who keeps 250 birds, said a crate of eggs currently sold for about N6,200 amid declining consumer purchasing power.

Similarly, Mr Shola Adeyi, a Lokoja-based farmer with a 1,000-bird capacity, said feed prices had increased by N2,000 to N3,000 per bag almost monthly since January.

He said starter, finisher and layer feeds sold for N22,500, N22,000 and N16,000 respectively, while day-old chicks cost about N2,200 each.

Adeyi identified unreliable electricity, extreme heat and high bird mortality as additional challenges confronting poultry farmers.

He said some operators had abandoned the business because they could not afford alternative power sources.

He said eggs sold for between N6,000 and N6,500 per crate, while broilers fetched N4,500 to N5,000 per kilogramme.

According to him, the prices barely covered production costs, necessitating long-term subsidised or interest-free loans and effective market regulation.

Another farmer, Mr Malik Ajayi, said day-old chick and feed prices usually increased during Sallah, Easter and Christmas.

Ajayi, who rears broilers, cockerels and foreign turkeys, said he recently bought three cartons of day-old chicks for N352,500.

He attributed some price fluctuations to possible exploitation by large-scale producers and urged the government to introduce effective price regulation.

Ajayi, who keeps 150 broilers, 50 cockerels and 15 foreign turkeys, said some farmers sold their birds cheaply to avoid prolonged feeding costs.

He added that frozen poultry dealers also faced high electricity and preservation expenses.

Mrs Oluwaseyi Fadaka, another Lokoja-based farmer, said a bag of feed now cost about N22,000, with her 40 Noiler birds consuming one regularly.

She said rising feeding costs were eroding profits, forcing farmers to sell at losses or abandon the business.

Fadaka said some smallholders were exploring organic feeding alternatives but needed government support through subsidised feed and affordable, quality inputs.

Responding, the Kogi Government said it was implementing interventions through the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support Project (L-PRES).

The State Project Coordinator, Mr Abdulkabir Otaru, said the World Bank-supported project targeted productivity, commercialisation and resilience across livestock value chains.

He said the project recently supported 500 women and youths across the state’s 21 local government areas with poultry inputs and equipment.

Beneficiaries also received day-old chicks, feed, drugs, vaccines and N100,000 each for logistics support.

The Commissioner for Livestock Development, Dr Olufemi Bolarin, said the ministry was collaborating with L-PRES and stakeholders on sustainable solutions.

He said improved poultry breeds, including resilient, dual-purpose SASSO chickens, were being introduced to strengthen food security and farmers’ incomes.

Stakeholders called for subsidised maize and soya beans, local feed ingredient production and solar power support to reduce bird mortality.

In Niger, poultry farmers and feed dealers said rising feed, chick and transportation costs were threatening the sustainability of poultry businesses.

A NAN survey at Firduas Agrovet, a poultry feed and day-old chick dealership in Minna, revealed significant increases in poultry input prices.

The dealers attributed the increases largely to rising transportation costs, saying some feed prices had risen by about 40 per cent over the previous year.

They said a bag of layer feed, previously sold for N7,500 to N8,000, now cost about N15,000.

Broiler feed, formerly sold for approximately N18,000, had increased to N24,000, they added.

A day-old broiler chick sold for N2,200, while a layer chick cost about N3,500, with festive demand influencing prices.

The dealers said N500,000, which previously could sustain about 500 birds, could now cater for only approximately 100.

A poultry farmer, Mr Bala Ibrahim, said rising production costs and unstable market prices were making it difficult to sustain businesses.

He said feed constituted a significant proportion of production expenses, while fluctuating chick prices complicated financial planning.

Ibrahim said some operators had reduced their flock sizes, while others struggled to remain in business.

He said poultry sales frequently failed to cover feeding, medication, labour, transportation and other production expenses.

He urged the Niger government to reduce production costs and improve farmers’ access to affordable feed and essential inputs.

Responding, the Permanent Secretary, Niger Ministry for Livestock, Mr Jonathan Wasa, said the government planned to revive and upgrade the Tagwai feed mill.

He said the initiative was intended to improve local feed availability and reduce the financial pressure on livestock farmers.

Wasa said the ministry was collaborating with Niger Foods to facilitate the supply of raw materials for feed production.

He explained that feed transported from Kaduna and Ilorin was expensive because of additional transportation and distribution costs.

Establishing local feed production, he said, would reduce dependence on external supplies and improve accessibility.

Wasa said Niger had abundant raw materials for feed production, adding that the government was working to harness the resources.

He expressed optimism that upgrading the Tagwai facility would improve feed availability and reduce production costs when operations began.

He said the intervention would strengthen the livestock value chain and create opportunities for farmers and agricultural input suppliers.

In Nasarawa, livestock farmers also blamed rising feed costs and poor market prices for declining profitability and farm closures.

The farmers spoke to NAN in Lafia, citing rising maize and soya bean prices without corresponding increases in poultry product prices.

A poultry farmer, Mr Musa Ibrahim, said feed accounted for about 70 per cent of production expenses.

“The cost of feed constitutes about 70 per cent of production. We are buying feed at exorbitant prices but selling at a loss because consumers cannot afford high prices.

“Many of our members have closed their farms. If nothing is done urgently, poultry and livestock farming will collapse in the state,” he said.

Mrs Sarah Audu, a livestock farmer from Akwanga, said high feed costs had forced her to reduce her flock from 2,000 birds to 500.

She urged the state and federal governments to provide subsidised feed ingredients and establish feed mills.

Similarly, Alhaji Suleiman Danlami, a cattle fattener in Keffi, decried poor animal prices in spite of rising production costs.

“During festive periods we expect to make profit, but now even at Sallah and Christmas, prices are poor. Transportation cost is high, feed is high, but market price is low,” he said.

The farmers warned that without urgent interventions to reduce production costs and improve market conditions, more smallholder operators could abandon livestock farming.

They urged governments to strengthen local feed ingredient production, establish feed mills and provide affordable financing to sustain production and improve food security.

World.title: JP Morgan’s Nigeria expansion to boost foreign investment — IMPI
World.content:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The Independent Media and Policy Initiative (IMPI) has said the planned expansion of global financial giant JP Morgan Chase into Nigeria’s merchant banking sector could attract fresh foreign investments, improve corporate financing and strengthen the country’s access to international capital markets.

The policy think tank said the American financial institution’s application for a national merchant banking licence was a significant endorsement of Nigeria’s investment prospects and could encourage more multinational corporations to commit long-term capital to the country.

In a policy statement signed by its Chairman, Dr Omoniyi Akinsiju, IMPI said the proposed expansion could reshape Nigeria’s corporate finance landscape by making it easier for businesses to access funding, structure large-scale projects and manage risks associated with cross-border investments.

According to the group, JP Morgan’s transition from a representative office to a fully licensed merchant bank would enable it to deepen its involvement in trade finance, corporate lending, cross-border underwriting and other sophisticated financial transactions.

It said the development could be particularly beneficial to capital-intensive sectors such as energy, telecommunications and manufacturing, where high borrowing costs and complex financing arrangements had continued to constrain investments.

“JP Morgan Chase’s move to secure a national merchant banking licence in Nigeria marks a significant shift in West Africa’s corporate finance landscape,” IMPI said.

The group added that the proposed operations could help multinational companies structure investments more efficiently through direct access to cross-border trade facilities, commodity hedging instruments and syndicated financing involving domestic and international markets.

It said the availability of such services could reduce delays and additional costs businesses often encounter when relying on multiple financial intermediaries to execute major projects.

IMPI also argued that Nigeria’s sovereign and corporate borrowers could benefit from stronger links to international capital markets, while the presence of a major global financial institution could reinforce confidence among foreign pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and private equity investors.

However, the think tank cautioned that JP Morgan’s proposed entry would not automatically translate into increased foreign direct investment, stressing that the broader benefits would depend on prevailing investment conditions and the consistency of economic policies.

Tinubu’s reforms and investor confidence

The policy group attributed renewed international interest in Nigeria to the economic policy direction of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly the foreign exchange market reforms and removal of petrol subsidy introduced in 2023.

It acknowledged that the reforms initially triggered inflationary pressures and currency depreciation but argued that they had helped reshape the country’s external financial position and renew international investor interest.

“Our analysis found that the near four years of the federal administration mark a record of consistent current account surpluses, underpinned by an aggressive strategy to not only drive FDI but also link it to domestic macroeconomic stability with a medium- to long-term microeconomic impact,” the statement said.

IMPI maintained that the reforms represented a structural shift from policies that previously distorted market signals towards a system intended to improve price discovery, strengthen external balances and attract sustainable investments.

It said the emerging challenge was to convert renewed international interest and short-term capital inflows into investments that would expand productive capacity, create jobs and strengthen the real economy.

From portfolio inflows to long-term investments

The think tank also identified a potential shift in Nigeria’s foreign investment profile, arguing that the country could gradually move away from excessive dependence on foreign portfolio investments towards more sustainable foreign direct investments.

It explained that portfolio investors had been attracted by high yields on government securities and other short-term financial instruments, while the Central Bank of Nigeria’s monetary and foreign exchange policies sought to address currency pressures and rebuild investor confidence.

It noted that the surge in portfolio inflows had helped boost Nigeria’s foreign reserves to more than $55 billion, although the high interest rates associated with the strategy had also increased borrowing costs for domestic businesses.

“For nearly two years, foreign capital prioritised government debt and Treasury bills (FPI) over physical infrastructure (FDI) because short-term paper yielded safely above 25 per cent,” IMPI said.

The group argued that as inflation moderates and yields on fixed-income securities decline, investors could become more interested in longer-term opportunities, including infrastructure concessions, industrial projects and direct equity investments.

It added that the declining attractiveness of short-term financial instruments could encourage institutional investors and cross-border private equity firms to redirect some of their funds towards productive assets.

“For our standpoint, as inflation begins to moderate, the focus is shifting towards converting these temporary portfolio flows into permanent, factory-to-market FDI,” the statement added.

IMPI said JP Morgan’s proposed merchant banking operations could facilitate this transition by providing the financing structures and risk-management instruments required to execute large-scale investments.

It argued that international investors required more than favourable policy announcements before committing capital to physical projects, noting that predictable financing arrangements, credible risk-sharing mechanisms and access to institutions capable of handling complex transactions were equally important.

The group said the presence of a globally influential financial institution could help bridge that gap by connecting Nigerian businesses and projects with international capital providers.

It added that improved access to corporate finance could support investments in energy infrastructure, telecommunications and industrial production, while making it easier for Nigerian companies to participate in international trade.

However, IMPI said the broader impact would depend on the consistency of economic reforms, the evolution of borrowing costs and the ability of businesses to translate improved financing opportunities into viable projects.

It maintained that JP Morgan’s proposed expansion should be viewed not merely as the arrival of another financial institution, but as an opportunity to deepen Nigeria’s integration into global investment networks.

The group said the ultimate test would be whether renewed investor attention translated into factories, infrastructure, expanded production and jobs rather than remaining concentrated in short-term financial instruments.

For Nigeria, it added, the opportunity lay in converting improving investor sentiment into sustained capital formation capable of supporting long-term economic growth.

World.title: Champions League: Man United rise from the dust to shock Roma 3-2
World.content:
Manchester United’s Brazilian striker #10 Matheus Cunha celebrates after scoring their second goal during the UEFA Champions League, league phase football match between Manchester United and Roma at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on November 3, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP)

Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford.

The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen.

But Matheus Cunha’s struck twice after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had given United hope to end a nine-game winless run in all competitions.

The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance.

Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of previous trips to Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse.

Gian Piero Gasperini’s lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining.

The Italians have now lost on all five visits to the Theatre of Dreams, most notably when Carrick scored twice in a 7-1 thrashing in the Champions League quarter-finals 19 years ago.

Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez’s foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international.

It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes.

Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora’s pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes.

Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Soule’s shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven.

Malen converted the resulting penalty for his 12th goal of the season.

The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United’s unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club.

United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box.

Yet, Carrick’s luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini.

Fernandes’s first spot-kick was saved by Roma’s third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors.

The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback.

Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts and Roma captain Bryan Cristante had to hack clear off the line as the visitors rode their luck.

However, Leonardo Balerdi’s swipe at fresh air deep inside his own box gifted Cunha the simplest task to tap in an equaliser seven minutes from time.

Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration.
