Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time.

The 10 men held on to breathe new life into United’s Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como.

Whether it proves to be a turning point or just another stay of execution for Carrick remains to be seen.

World.title: Atiku’s claim: DSS denies plotting Sokoto protest, orders probe
World.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) has denied allegations that it planned to organise protests in Sokoto State, describing the claim by former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as inconsistent with its operations.

The Service, however, said its Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation in deference to the former vice president.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Deputy Director, Public Relations and Strategic Communications, Favour Dozie, the DSS said its operatives deployed to protect the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Mannir Daniya, evacuated him to safety when he was attacked on October 31, 2026.

According to the Service, Daniya escaped unhurt during the incident, while two DSS operatives were assaulted and were still receiving treatment in hospital as of the time of the statement.

The DSS said the governorship candidate personally contacted the State Director of the Service in Sokoto to express appreciation for the intervention and subsequently requested additional security reinforcement.

The Service also cited its arrest and prosecution of Monday Udeme Steven in Rivers State on March 2, 2026, for allegedly threatening to attack the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi.

It said Steven was prosecuted before a Federal High Court in Rivers State and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment.

The DSS said its operations to protect politicians across party lines contradicted Atiku’s allegation, which it argued could demoralise its operatives risking their lives in the line of duty.

Read Also: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally in Sokoto

It nevertheless said the Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation out of respect for the former vice president.

The Service also recalled a similar allegation by African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, that it was involved in an attack on him in Ekiti State.

It said it appreciated the police for their swift investigation and preliminary report on the incident, which identified an altercation as its cause and led to the arrest of 11 suspects.

The DSS added that it would await the outcome of the police investigation and would not dissipate further energy on the matter.

The Service reaffirmed its commitment to accountability under its current Director-General.

World.title: 2027: Ogun indigenes rally behind Adebutu, reaffirm ‘Ogun for Ogun’ agenda
World.content:
.pledge grassroots mobilisation as PDP candidate takes campaign to communities

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

Indigenes of Ogun State have reaffirmed their commitment to protecting the state’s political heritage, declaring support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ movement ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The residents made the pledge during separate engagements at the ward-to-ward campaign tours of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, across the state’s local government areas.

The campaign tour, which has taken Adebutu and Kolapo to various communities in recent weeks, is aimed at mobilising grassroots support for the PDP candidates and presenting their seven-point development agenda, tagged ITURA DE, to the electorate.

At the different ward meetings, residents, community leaders, market women, farmers and youths turned out to welcome the candidates, with several communities receiving them with colourful displays and enthusiastic celebrations.

The engagements also provided opportunities for residents to interact directly with the candidates, raise concerns about their communities and outline their expectations from the next administration.

Among the major issues raised were the poor condition of rural roads, unemployment, inadequate agricultural support and the need for improved infrastructure and access to modern farming equipment.

Several stakeholders pledged to mobilise support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, arguing that the state’s leadership should reflect the interests, heritage and aspirations of its indigenes.

At Alagada Ward in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a market leader, Mrs Folasade Ogunye, said her support for the movement was informed by the belief that indigenous leadership would better understand the challenges confronting grassroots communities.

She lamented the poor condition of roads leading to markets and the limited employment opportunities available to young people, insisting that residents needed a leader who understood their everyday struggles.

“We, the women of Obafemi/Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad, and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and understands our struggles.

“We believe that someone with a genuine connection to the people will better appreciate our challenges. That is why we have pledged to go from house to house to mobilise support for this mandate. It is about our pride and the future of Ogun indigenes,” she said.

In a related development, some residents said to be former members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at Alapakooni community in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area publicly renounced their allegiance to the party.

The defectors reportedly set bunches of APC brooms ablaze to symbolise their departure from the party, citing dissatisfaction with its political leadership and questions surrounding the identity of its governorship candidate.

A community youth coordinator in Alapakooni Ward, Tunde Akinola, said their decision to align with Adebutu was motivated by their desire for leadership they could identify with and hold accountable.

“We decided to join this ward meeting today with our incoming governor, Adebutu, because we love our state and cannot trade its future on the altar of politics.

“We want to follow someone we know, someone who understands our people and has the capacity to deliver on his promises,” Akinola said.

Similarly, a community stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, Deji Bamidele, said farmers in the area were eager for a government that would prioritise agricultural development through mechanisation and improved access to farming inputs.

He lamented that many farmers still depended on rudimentary implements despite the increasing need to boost food production.

“In this community, farming is our life, but we have been left with cutlasses while farmers in other states are benefiting from tractors and modern equipment.

“When Adebutu explained the ITURA DE agenda and how agriculture would be mechanised, we saw hope. We are committing our farmers’ cooperative, which has more than 300 members, to the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ cause because we want our agricultural potential properly harnessed,” he said.

At Owode Ward 3, also in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a retired teacher, Alhaja Sariyu Bankole, described the movement as an opportunity to preserve the state’s political heritage.

According to her, Ogun State has produced several distinguished leaders whose legacies should inspire the emergence of leadership that understands the history and aspirations of its people.

“We cannot mortgage our heritage. Ogun State is the home of great leaders, and we must ensure that whoever governs us understands our history and respects the people.

“I have spoken to my former students and their parents in this ward about the need to participate actively in the election. We must make our voices count and work towards the future we desire,” she said.

In Sagamu Local Government Area, a youth leader, Comrade Bayo Oduwole, said young people were determined to play a more active role in determining the political future of the state.

Speaking at Ward 10, Oduwole maintained that the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ campaign should be driven by competence, accountability and a genuine understanding of the state’s needs.

“The courageous indigenes of this state have called on us not to surrender our future, and we agree with the need for leadership that understands our people and their aspirations.

“We know Adebutu’s family history here and are familiar with the contributions associated with his family. We also recognise the compassion shown by Iya Sunnah. We will mobilise our youths through voter education and door-to-door campaigns to secure victory,” he said.

Responding to the expressions of support, Adebutu described the ward-to-ward engagements as an opportunity to understand the needs of communities and build a development agenda around them.

He said the ITURA DE agenda was designed to address the socio-economic challenges facing the state, with particular attention to infrastructure, agriculture, employment generation and improved living standards.

“This tour has shown me that our people are yearning for homegrown leadership that understands their challenges and is prepared to address them.

“The ITURA DE agenda is not just a slogan; it is a social contract to restore dignity, fix our roads, empower our farmers, create jobs for our youths and return Ogun State to its rightful place.

“We are not just campaigning; we are listening to the people, understanding their concerns and taking note of their expectations. We will deliver on our promises,” Adebutu said.

Also speaking, the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, assured residents that a government led by the party would prioritise inclusive governance and ensure that grassroots communities were adequately represented in policy decisions.

She particularly highlighted the importance of women, children, education and primary healthcare in the proposed administration’s development plans.

“What we have witnessed in the wards we have visited is genuine concern and love for Ogun State. The people want a government that listens to them and responds to their needs.

“As a mother and a daughter of this soil, I assure you that our government will prioritise women, children, education and primary healthcare.

“We will not disappoint the people. This ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is about building a state where every community, irrespective of its location or social standing, has a sense of belonging and benefits from good governance,” Kolapo said.

The PDP candidates maintained that their ongoing grassroots engagements would continue across the state as they seek to consolidate support and present their policy proposals ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

World.title: OKOROCHA’S VENDETTA GAMBLE WITH IMO APC
World.content:
By Declan Emelumba

The frenzy with which Senator Rochas Okorocha has been celebrating his pyrrhic victory at the Federal High Court, Abuja, over the Imo West senatorial primary of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has more than confirmed that the judgment was premeditated. As loquacious as ever, Okorocha has gone to town to thank those who facilitated that travesty of justice. His mention of help from high places, and his speedy embrace of the so-called Rainbow Coalition without any contact with the APC at the grassroots, have given him and his co-conspirators away. But Nigerians are not fooled. Many have recalled the old saying: the witch cried in the night, and the child died at dawn.

One sharp observation came from Sam Amadi, a lawyer, rights activist and politician from Imo State, who is no fan of Governor Hope Uzodimma. In a Facebook post the day after the judgment, Amadi wrote: “Hope Uzodimma may be guilty of many things. But it does not mean he is guilty of everything.” He pointed to the footage of Uzodimma voting on the primaries election day, with his wife by his side and a large crowd of APC members behind him. Then he threw down a simple challenge: “Let us see the evidence of Okorocha’s primary election.”

That may sound academic in a courtroom, but it confirms what APC members in Ideato South, Okorocha’s home, and across Imo State have said all along: he was an absentee aspirant who neither campaigned nor took part in the primary. His son Amen, who swore to the affidavit used to procure this phantom judgment, is not even known to the party.

As Jesus said of Judas, it was written that the Son of Man would be betrayed, but woe unto the man who betrays him. Chief Sam Mbakwe spoke in the same manner about the vexed abandoned property issue, under which Ndigbo were dispossessed of their property in Rivers State. He said that whenever that infamy was mentioned, the man who chaired the Abandoned Properties Implementation Committee, David Mark, would be remembered on the wrong side of history. In like manner, whenever controversial Federal High Court judgments are mentioned, the name of Justice Obiora Egwuatu will be remembered. That he set aside Supreme Court rulings duly cited before him to hand a questionable victory to Okorocha seals his place in the hall of infamy.

What is baffling is the way Okorocha has been moving from one media house to another, gloating over this so-called victory, vilifying the governor and speaking as if the judgment were the final word. Unless he knows something that is not written in the Electoral Act or the Constitution, or unless those pulling his strings have given their puppet overwhelming assurances, Uzodimma retains the right to appeal this judgment all the way to the Supreme Court. Okorocha’s faith in a judgment that cannot stand the test of the law is curious, especially as the Imo APC has already disowned him.

On Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, the very day of the judgment, Okorocha declared: “Hope has never won an election in his life.” The record says otherwise. Uzodimma won the Imo West Senate seat twice and sat in the 7th and 8th Senates. In the 2023 governorship election, he polled 540,308 votes against 71,503 for the PDP and 64,081 for the Labour Party. INEC’s returning officer, Prof. Abayomi Fasina, declared him winner and returned him elected. Now contrast that with Okorocha’s own route to the Senate in 2019. Announcing the Imo West result, the returning officer, Prof. Innocent Ibeawuchi, told the nation: “I declared this thing before under duress; I’m still under duress declaring this one.” INEC initially refused Okorocha a certificate of return. So which of the two men has never truly won an election?

On the same programme, Okorocha said: “There’s no single project initiated by Hope and finished by Hope.” He should ask his own people. The road Okorocha built to his village collapsed, cutting his community off from the rest of Imo and subjecting his people to untold hardship. Three governors, Okorocha included, could not fix the Orlu–Mgbee–Akokwa–Uga federal road, the only accessible route to his village. Uzodimma rebuilt it from end to end, together with the Umuchima Bridge linking Orlu and Ideato, which Okorocha failed to build in all his years as governor and senator. The Auxiliary Bishop of Orlu, Most Rev. Thomas Ifeanyichukwu Obiatuegwu, publicly praised the project and thanked the governor. The road and bridge Okorocha’s own people now use were delivered by the man he mocks.

He went further: “He can’t beat my record. He can’t even get close to it. Not one, one hundredth of my record.” Every Imo person knows that Okorocha’s so-called projects fell into ruin even before he left office. The International Conference Centre, a stone’s throw from Government House, lost its roof, and its ceiling caved in. The Mother and Child Hospital on Douglas Road, Owerri, was left to mechanics, hoodlums and reptiles; it is not fit to be called a poultry farm, let alone a hospital. Chukwuma Nwoha Road, Dick Tiger Road and other urban roads had become swampy bush paths until Uzodimma rebuilt them. And in the name of urban renewal, Okorocha savagely destroyed the piped water system he inherited. It is hard to believe that the Imo of today is the same Imo that Okorocha spent eight years spoiling and pillaging. That old Imo was truly nothing to write home about.

Acting like a bull in a china shop, Okorocha accuses Uzodimma of humiliation and intimidation. That bears the mark of envy and an outsized grudge, which only facts can heal. He has not told Nigerians why security agencies arrested his son-in-law, Uche Nwosu. He has not told Nigerians that the EFCC secured forfeiture orders on properties traced to him, his wife and his daughter. He has not explained the Royal Spring Palm Estate on Akachi Road, Owerri: government land developed and claimed as private property by his wife, Nkechi. He has not explained how Eastern Palm University, built with public funds, came to be claimed as his own until the Uzodimma government recovered it and renamed it K.O. Mbadiwe University. Nor has he mentioned the state panel that found he used soldiers and hoodlums to seize the land of Alvan Ikoku Federal College of Education and demolish 101 staff buildings. He speaks today as a free man only because Uzodimma, against wise counsel, refused to prosecute him and his family for widespread corruption. Okorocha ought to be answering for his record, not comparing it with Uzodimma’s.

Indeed, he already has charges to answer. A Senior Magistrate Court in Abuja has issued a bench warrant against Okorocha and his son Amen, on charges of criminal conspiracy, forgery, perjury and false documents over the primary results he paraded. The police confirmed that they arrested him at the REIZ Continental Hotel in Abuja on 12 October and released him on bail. Yet on live television he insisted: “Never was I arrested.” A man who can obtain a dubious court order while facing forgery charges, and then deny an arrest the police have confirmed, is capable of anything. Is this the character the APC wants to fly its flag at next year’s senatorial election?

Like the proverbial nza bird that eats its fill and then challenges its chi to a wrestling match, Okorocha has stepped back onto his familiar terrain of deceit. He now claims that his name on the ballot guarantees Tinubu’s victory in Imo, while “Hope cannot carry Imo. Cannot carry South East.” The figures tell a different story. In 2015, as a first-term governor seeking re-election and the de facto leader of the APC in Imo, Okorocha delivered Muhammadu Buhari 133,253 votes, about 19 per cent, well short of the 25 per cent he now brags about. Only in 2019, after Uzodimma joined the APC, did Buhari cross the mark, with 140,463 votes, or about 27 per cent. Instructively, most of the votes came from Oru East local government, Uzodimma’s home, where Buhari secured over 90% of the votes cast.

In 2023, when an Igbo son was on the presidential ballot and Ndigbo were emotional about his candidacy, Tinubu polled 66,406 votes in Imo, about 14 per cent and his best result anywhere in the South-East. He got 8,914 votes in Abia, 5,111 in Anambra and 4,772 in Enugu. And where was Okorocha, the self-acclaimed founder of the party? By his own admission on Arise Television, he preferred Peter Obi.

This self-righteous man, who claims to be a victim and prances around Abuja without touching base at home, has labelled Uzodimma greedy. I will not dignify his beer-parlour gossip about what the governor wants. Let us instead examine the facts in the public domain. In December 2014, as a sitting governor, Okorocha contested the APC presidential primary and polled 624 votes. When he lost, he went back home and secured a second term as governor. In 2019, still a sitting governor, he ran for the Senate while sponsoring his son-in-law to succeed him. In 2022, as a senator, he contested the APC presidential primary against Tinubu and scored zero. If that is not greed, what is?

When Uzodimma defeated his son-in-law for the APC governorship ticket, Okorocha moved Nwosu to another party and worked against the APC. Adams Oshiomhole, then national chairman of the APC, called him “an embarrassment to APC” and accused him of trying “to create a dynasty” in Imo. So why is Uzodimma’s senatorial ambition a mortal sin in Okorocha’s eyes? It is the case of the man with a log in his own eye shouting about the speck in another’s.

Okorocha knows he cannot win a councillorship election in his hometown of Ogboko. In September, councillors from Ideato North and Ideato South held a special plenary on the Umuchima Bridge, endorsed Uzodimma for the Imo West Senate seat and barred Okorocha from using roads and bridges he never built. The man who calls himself the Abraham of the APC is today represented in the House of Representatives by an opposition lawmaker, Ikenga Ugochinyere. So much for his electoral value.

These basic facts should guide those goading Okorocha into this political gamble, in which he has sold his soul to betrayal rather than repent of the atrocities of his eight-year imperial reign in Imo State. The APC and its leaders must not allow this perfidy to stand. The party’s fate in Orlu Zone hangs in the balance. Its fate in Imo State also hangs in the balance. Rochas Okorocha is deficient in honour and integrity, carries no electoral value in the state, and has lent himself to the destruction of the APC’s pillar in the South-East.

Emelumba is Imo state Commissioner for Information, Public Orientation and Strategy

World.title: Unhealthy Rivalry Should Not Be Mistaken for Legislative Independence, Says Group
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Arewa Revival Project (ARP) has emphasised that unhealthy rivalry, needless confrontation and persistent disagreements with the executive arm of government should not be misconstrued as signs of legislative independence.

The group spoke out against former lawmakers’ negative criticism of the President of the Senate and the National Assembly.

The former legislators had reportedly alleged that the Senate, under the leadership of Senator Godswill Akpabio, was an extension of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Presidential Villa.

According to a statement by the Project Coordinator, Hon. Muttaka Ahmed Ibrahim, true legislative independence is demonstrated through principled decision-making, responsible representation and a commitment to democratic values, not through needless power struggles or unhealthy competition.

The group noted that while legislative autonomy is essential to a functioning democracy, it must be exercised responsibly, guided by constitutional principles, mutual respect and the collective interest of the people.

Legislative independence, he said, should promote constructive engagement, effective oversight and accountability, rather than foster division, institutional hostility or personal antagonism.

According to the organisation, the constitution does not require the National Assembly to oppose every presidential proposal to demonstrate its independence, stressing that effective democratic governance requires institutional cooperation without undermining constitutional responsibilities.

It noted that the legislature’s primary responsibilities include lawmaking, appropriation, oversight and the protection of the constitutional order.

The organisation also defended Akpabio’s leadership, stating that his performance should be assessed fairly through the Senate’s legislative activities, institutional responsibilities and leadership record.

While acknowledging that the Senate President and the National Assembly must remain open to public scrutiny, ARP cautioned against reducing the office of the Senate President to political ridicule because of partisan disagreements.

The group further called on the former lawmaker to present specific evidence if he had concerns about legislative misconduct, compromised oversight, financial impropriety or constitutional violations.

ARP acknowledged that a credible opposition was essential to democracy but maintained that opposition activities should focus on accountability, exposing wrongdoing, offering policy alternatives and defending citizens’ interests.

ARP reaffirmed its commitment to responsible governance, national unity, democratic stability and the Renewed Hope Agenda, while calling for accountability across all public institutions.

World.title: DSS DG Frees Four Suspected IPOB Members, Approves N20m Compensation
World.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) has released four suspects arrested over alleged membership of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and approved an initial payment of N20 million as compensation to them.

The Director-General of the Service, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, approved N5 million for each of the four suspects after they were cleared of the allegations.

Security sources disclosed that the suspects, identified as Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry, were arrested in May 2022 in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State.

According to one of the sources, investigations established that the suspects had been misled into believing they would receive monthly payments of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme.

“The Agency established that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme, not knowing that they were being lured by a group of IPOB members who are now facing trial,” the source said.

The source explained that the four suspects were victims of a recruitment scheme allegedly orchestrated by members of the proscribed group, some of whom are currently facing trial.

While receiving the released suspects, their counsel, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, commended the DSS for its efforts towards safeguarding national security.

The law firm particularly praised Ajayi for what it described as his genuine commitment to upholding human rights.

Furthermore, he noted the high level of hygiene and professionalism within the Service, being the best he has witnessed in over 20 years of interacting with DSS personnel. He reiterated his earlier public statement that President Tinubu made the right choice in appointing Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi as DSS DG.

Expressing gratitude to the DSS boss, Emele Uduma Ibe who spoke on behalf of others, described the day as the happiest of his life, noting that the experience had taught him a valuable lesson which he would share with others. He offered prayers for God’s continued blessings upon the DSS boss and the management of the Service.

The release and compensation represent another restitution exercise by the DSS under Ajayi’s leadership, aimed at addressing cases involving individuals cleared of allegations following investigations.

Recall that upon assuming office in 2024, the DG ordered a review of over 300 inherited terrorism cases. Currently, the DSS panel has been able to decongest its facility to about 100 after thorough investigations, paying over a billion naira in compensation.

The DSS boss awarded N20 million and covered the medical bills of a Jos based businessman, who was shot erroneously by service personnel in Plateau State. Chineze Ozoadibe was also compensated with N10 million after she was wrongfully arrested, Sunday Ifedi who was also compensated with 10 million naira after investigation cleared him of ties with IPOB, likewise Kenneth Okechukwu Nwafor was also paid N5 million after investigation absolved him of IPOB allegations.

This is aside other numerous cases that the DSS has handled quietly which never made news outside the Agency, the source said..

“Like other compensated suspects, the DSS will also offer psychological, medical support to these four in addition the initial amount given. I’m confident the DSS will also help further reintegration into the society,” revealed a source.

The DG- DSS in a recent maiden media interview admitted that, as humans, the DSS is prone to mistakes. However, where there is injury, Mr Ajayi said there must be remedy.

“Where we admit our mistakes, we offer compensation, and seek ways to improve operations in tandem with the rule of law.”

World.title: Atiku Decries Intimidation of ADC Members, Denial of Using Public Facilities for Campaigns in Sokoto
World.content:
*Vows to address rally in Sokoto Wednesday

*PDP chairmen petition IG over harassment by APC govs

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Former Vice President and the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar has decried the violence and political intimidation of members of his party in Sokoto State by the state government as well as refusal of the use of public facilities for rallies and campaigns.

He vowed that irrespective of the actions of security agencies and the state government denial of public facilities for campaigns and rallies that he will address a rally in Sokoto State in Wednesday.

He also accused the leadership of the Department of State Security of recruiting thugs to obstruct ADC campaigns in Sokoto State

This is coming as the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP States chairmen has petitioned Police Inspector General over Intimidation and Harassment by APC Governors

Addressing a press conference Tuesday in Abuja, the former vice president said, “I address you today with a heavy but resolute heart. What is unfolding in Sokoto is not ordinary political competition. It is a calculated campaign to frustrate the African Democratic Congress, obstruct our campaign and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose.”

According to Atiku, “Public facilities that should be available to every political party for legitimate campaign activities have been blocked. Logistical support has been withheld. These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field.

“More disturbing still, the information available to us is that the leadership of the Department of State Services is recruiting people to stage protests in Sokoto. The objective is to create disorder, give the APC controlled state government a pretext to impose a curfew and prevent our campaign take off from holding as scheduled.

“We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade.”

He continued, “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis. I call on every officer involved to stop immediately and return to the constitutional duty of impartial service.”, Atiku stated

Blaming the current administration for this breach of peace, Atiku said, “For three and a half years, the Tinubu administration has devoted too much energy to weakening credible opposition and too little to solving the problems facing Nigerians. It has pursued a politics of absorption and intimidation, while drawing former opposition figures into the APC and narrowing the space for political competition. The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one party state in all but name.

“The government is afraid of the people’s verdict. It has unleashed a crushing cost of living crisis and now appears determined to frustrate Nigerians’ democratic right to choose a different path. Food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials have become unaffordable for millions. Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive. That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.

“I will make life affordable again. We will support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. We will pursue a targeted production subsidy tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, so that support reaches consumers through measurable relief while also strengthening domestic industry. Nigerians deserve policies that put food on the table, restore opportunity and make daily life manageable again.

“The APC has still not recovered from the abysmal failure of its last rally in Kaduna. It should have taken that as a warning that Nigerians are withdrawing their confidence. Instead, it has chosen intimidation and obstruction. These are the last kicks of a dying horse. The more this government tries to silence the people, the clearer it becomes that it has already lost their confidence”, he said .

The ADC Presidential candidate said that “The 2027 general election will be a defining moment in our democratic history. This is more than a contest between parties or candidates. It is a choice between a government that has shown indifference to people’s suffering and Nigerians who have endured enough and want their votes to count.

“The ADC will resist every gimmick, administrative roadblock and underhand manoeuvre designed to exclude the opposition or impose a one party reality on Nigeria. We will not be intimidated into silence or irrelevance. Our campaign will proceed, and I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state.

“I call on the people of Sokoto to remain calm and peaceful. Do not allow anyone to provoke you or turn a political gathering into a security crisis. I also urge the security agencies to protect commuters, residents and rally participants without favour. The authorities must ensure that our rally can hold peacefully and without interference.”

According to Atiku, “To the voters of Nigeria, remain resolute. Stand your ground. Democratic freedom is not a gift from any government. It is your right. Do not allow anyone to intimidate you or checkmate your will.

“As the Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress, I give you my word: I will lead this campaign and I will not abandon the field. We will confront every attempt to restrict democratic participation with firmness, organisation and faith in the Nigerian people.

“The ADC will stand with officers who refuse to be used against democracy and who remain faithful to the Constitution. Those who choose to betray their duty and collude in the suppression of political freedom will be held accountable under the law.

“Nigeria belongs to its people, not to any party or temporary occupant of power. We will defend that truth and the people’s right to choose.

Meanwhile , the chairman of the PDP states chairman’s forum, Austin Nwachukwu said at a meeting with the party’s National Working Committee, NWC at the PDP National Secretariat that the APC governors are intimidating and harassing members of the party in their states

According to Nwachukwu, “l just want to use opportunity to also bring to the notice of our National Working Committee that some states in the country, especially where we don’t have APC governors, are very antagonistic to our candidates and members.

“We have painstakingly produced very good candidates for the forthcoming elections and this is not going well with the governors of some states.

“For example, last week, the forum leadership was forced to go to Ebonyi State to address a draconian issue that have been brewing there, where intimidation, harassment, arrest, killings have become the order of the day, under the watch of the governor of Ebonyi state, His Excellency, Governor Nwifuru.

“We made a presentation, and with me here is a copy of the petition that we’re unfolding to the Inspector General of Police today, and to other relevant security agencies, the killings and harassment of our candidates and governorship candidate, especially in various states of the country, must stop.”, the chairman of the PDP states chairmen forum stated

He said that “the forum will not take it lightly anymore if any of our candidates are harassed, intimidated, or killed because of mere elections. It’s a contest. Winner must emerge.

“So on that notes, my colleagues, on the National Working Committee, I want to welcome all of us to this meeting and wish us a very happy deliberations. Thank you.

Thank you very much, Chairman”, Nwachukwu stated

The national chairman of the party, Abdulrahman Mohammed assured that the party will look into their petition.

He also assured the states chairmen of the party that the PDP is very much in the party as all their candidates have been recognised by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC

He boasted that the party nominated candidates at all levels that are capable of winning any election.

World.title: DSS Says Sowore’s Bid to Make Its Lawyer Witness in Alleged Cyberbullying Trial Dilatory, Judge Fixes Ruling for Nov 9
World.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS), on Tuesday, told the Federal High Court in Abuja that the bid by African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, to turn its lead counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, into his witness, is the politician’s ploy to delay his trial for allegedly cyberbullying President Bola Tinubu.

The DSS told the court that the subpoena Sowore issued on its lead counsel was in bad faith and strange in law and in criminal trial. Under Section 192 of the Evidence Act, stated the lawyer, no legal practitioner is permitted to disclose any communication made to him in the course of his engagement unless with the consent of his client.

The DSS added that Sowore’s subpoena was an abuse of court process calculated to annoy and irritate its lead counsel.

The submission by the DSS came as the trial judge, Justice Mohammed Garba Umar, fixed November 9, to deliver ruling on Sowore’s

application.

The judge fixed the date after taking arguments for and against the application by counsel on both sides.

At Tuesday’s proceedings, Kenneth Cyril-Ita, who represented the DSS, asked the court to set aside the subpoena issued against Kehinde, SAN, by Sowore seeking to turn the DSS lead lawyer into a witness in the trial.

Sowore, through his lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide Fusika, SAN, had served a subpoena on the DSS lead counsel to appear in court to give evidence in respect of the trial of the defendant for allegedly cyberbullying President Tinubu.

In his motion on notice against the execution of the subpoena, Cyril-Ita told the Court that the evidence sought to be given through the subpoena witness is irrelevant to Sowore’s alleged cyberbullying trial. Contrary to Sowore’s claim, the DSS lawyer said there was no application before the Court to suspend or adjourn the trial till 2027.

“By not setting aside the subpoena, the Court is being invited to deprive the Federal Republic of Nigeria, a counsel of its choice in the prosecution of the matter as counsel cannot be a witness and counsel at the same time in the same matter,” he stated.

“The evidence of whether the Complainant will ask for adjournment or not in the matter as shown in the publication sought to be tendered is a matter allegedly caught by section 83(3) of the Evidence Act,” he continued.

He, therefore, urged Justice Umar to set aside the subpoena and direct Sowore to continue his defence in the charges against him.

In his argument, Ruben Adakole, who represented Sowore, asked the Court to uphold the subpoena against the DSS lead counsel as requested by the defendant to make him his witness.

Thereafter, Justice Umar adjourned to November 9, to deliver his decision on the matter.

World.title: 2027: Obi Warns Govs Against Electoral Manipulation, Says Nigerians Will Resist Rigging
World.content:
• Accuses governors of prioritising political survival over performance

• Insists leadership must be earned through service, not intimidation

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Peter Obi Media Office has warned state governors against alleged attempts to manipulate the 2027 general election, declaring that Nigerians will resist any process that undermines the credibility of the polls.

The media office, which accused some governors of allegedly working behind the scenes to compromise the democratic process, said political leaders should focus on presenting their records of performance rather than seeking to retain power through electoral manipulation.

It maintained that any electoral process that failed to meet the standards of freedom, fairness and transparency would be rejected by Nigerians, who, it said, were determined to exercise their democratic rights.

In a statement issued Tuesday by its spokesman, Indris Zekeri Jnr, the Peter Obi Media Office said governors should recognise that political leadership is a privilege earned through service and not an entitlement to be retained through deceit, intimidation or interference with elections.

The statement, titled, ‘Nigerians Will Choose the Best Product in the Marketplace,’ accused some governors of becoming increasingly desperate as the 2027 general election approaches.

“Instead of presenting their records of service, performance and achievements, they are turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging,” the statement alleged.

It warned that attempts to undermine the democratic process would not permanently suppress the will of the electorate, insisting that Nigerians had become increasingly determined to reject leaders they considered undeserving of another mandate.

Part of the statement read: “The 2027 election will be a defining moment for our nation. Nigerians are resolved to reclaim their country through the power of their votes.

“Let it be known that no degree of rigging, intimidation or political manoeuvring can permanently silence the will of the people.”

The media office further argued that political leaders should be judged by their records and capacity to address the country’s challenges rather than their ability to deploy political influence to retain power.

It also reiterated its position that Peter Obi remained a preferred choice among Nigerians, citing what it described as his commitment to competence, character, compassion and responsible leadership.

According to the statement, Obi represents an alternative leadership proposition capable of addressing Nigeria’s challenges and restoring national dignity, prosperity and hope.

The media office urged political officeholders to respect the sovereignty of the electorate, stressing that the authority to determine who governs the country ultimately rests with the people.

It added that Nigerians were prepared to defend their votes in the 2027 elections, warning that electoral manipulation, intimidation and political manoeuvring would not override their democratic aspirations.

“The mandate rests with the people. Nigeria must function again, and it will be OK,” the statement added.

World.title: SON Unveils Cylinder Recirculation Scheme to Curtail Spread of Unsafe Units
World.content:
* Targets 43m certified units

The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) has launched the National Cylinder Recirculation Programme (NCRP) to curtail the spread of unsafe, expired and substandard liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders across the country.

Unveiled at the Nigerian Alliance for Clean Cooking (NACC) Conference 2026 in Abuja, the N2.27 trillion national initiative sets out a coordinated regulatory framework to register, inspect, track and recirculate LPG cylinders across all six geopolitical zones.

The programme targets the deployment of at least 43 million certified cylinders and the establishment of 42 Authorized Requalification Facilities (ARFs) nationwide to replace unsafe units currently in circulation.

Under the new system, every cylinder will be onboarded onto a central National Cylinder Registry and assigned a unique QR code, enabling regulators and industry participants to trace each unit from manufacture through distribution, inspection, and maintenance.

Cylinders returned through approved retail channels will undergo testing at ARFs, where units meeting national quality standards will re-enter the market, while defective ones will be impounded for corrective action or safe disposal.

Delivering the keynote address, Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, represented by the ministry’s Director of Weights and Measures, Dr. Salim Mohammed, described the rollout as a transformative investment in public safety, industrial growth and skilled job creation aimed at establishing long-term stability in the LPG sector.

“This programme is more than a regulatory initiative; it is a transformative N2.27 trillion national investment in safety, industrialization and human development. By deploying at least 43 million certified cylinders and establishing 42 requalification centres nationwide, we are creating thousands of skilled jobs and laying the foundation for long-term sector planning,” she said.

During a panel session on expanding clean cooking access, industry leaders and regulatory officials highlighted the operational requirements needed to scale the framework.

Mr. Sabo Ahmed Barau, representing the Executive Director of Health, Safety, and Community Relations at the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), stressed that regulatory oversight will cover all stages from bulk storage to last-mile delivery to safeguard Nigerian households.

Addressing investment needs, Managing Director of FuelTree, Dr. ‘Bekeme Olowola, represented by the company’s Chief Technologist, Mr. Femi Oye, stated that verifiable empirical data through digital tracking is essential for unlocking commercial equity, grants and specialized climate financing.

On distribution, Founder of Falcon Corporation and Century One, Prof. Joseph Aigbedion, noted that primary storage infrastructure must be linked with arterial, community-level distribution clusters to reach families effectively.

CEO of Cook-Blue and Chiffinity Intelligence Consult, Princess Odiaka, highlighted the role of composite cylinders and community-based models in widening access, citing a “Trash-to-Cook” initiative in rural households.

She said: “Through our ‘Trash-to-Cook’ initiative, rural women exchange recyclable household waste to pay for clean gas refills. By turning discarded waste into currency, we address affordability, clean up the environment, and deliver clean cooking as an accessible service right to their doorsteps.”

SON is executing the NCRP in collaboration with government agencies and industry partners, including the NMDPRA, the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), and the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs.

Following its domestic launch, Nigeria plans to present its digital safety and traceability framework to the international community at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

World.title: 2027: Indigenes Vow to Defend ‘Ogun for Ogun’ Mandate, As Adebutu, Deputy Tour Wards
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta

Indigenes of Ogun State have restated their resolve to protect their heritage and ensure that the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate of prominent stakeholders in the state is actualised in the 2027 governorship election in the state.

They made this pledge in their separate remarks during the ward-to-ward tours embarked upon by the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, declaring their support for the candidates ahead of the poll.

Adebutu and Kolapo have in the past weeks been touring wards across all the local government areas in Ogun, mobilising indigenes and intimating them with their seven-point agenda tagged: ‘ITURA DE.’

Many grassroots dwellers who were meeting Adebutu and Kolapo for the first time were excited to receive the candidates to their communities as they welcomed them with fanfare.

Indigenes also had the opportunity of having town hall discussions with the PDP candidates where they enumerated the challenges they are facing in their various communities.

They urged Adebutu to fix their deplorable roads and assist farmers with seedlings and modern agricultural equipment to enable them to produce food in large quantity for the state.

Speaking at different ward engagements, stakeholders resolved to mobilise support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate, stressing that: “It will be a slap on our dear state if a stranger is allowed to rule over us.”

At Alagada Ward, Obafemi Owode LGA, Mrs. Folasade Ogunye, a market leader, said she was backing the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ movement because indigenes understand the pains of the grassroots.

She said: “We, the women of Obafemi Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and our struggles.

“Apart from that, it would be a disservice to the memory of our heroes for an outsider to dictate the fortune of our people. That is why we have pledged to go from house to house to secure this mandate. It is about our pride as Ogun indigenes.”

At Alapakooni community in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of the state, some members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), set some bunches of brooms ablaze, saying they decided to dump the party because they could not continue to support a candidate who has not been able to state his true identity.

Tunde Akinola, a community youth coordinator at Alapakooni Ward, said: “We decided to join this ward meeting today with our incoming governor Adebutu because we love our state and can’t trade it on the altar of politics. We want to follow the person we know and that will deliver.”

A stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, identified as Deji Bamidele, said: “In this community, farming is our life but we have been left with cutlasses while other states use tractors. When Adebutu explained ITURA DE and how agriculture will be mechanised, we saw hope.

“We are committing our farmers’ cooperative of over 300 members to this ‘Ogun for Ogun’ cause to ensure our land is governed by our own.”

At Owode Ward 3, Obafemi Owode LGA, Alhaja Sariyu Bankole, a retired teacher, said her commitment was driven by the need to protect Ogun’s political legacy.

“We cannot mortgage our heritage. Ogun State is the home of great leaders. Allowing non-indigenes to take over will erase our history. I have told all my former students and their parents in this ward that we must vote for our own. That is our covenant,” she stated.

Similarly, in Ward 10, Sagamu LGA, Comrade Bayo Oduwole, a youth leader, said the youth were tired of being spectators.

“Courageous indigenes of this state have said we should not allow strangers to rule over us and we agree completely. The ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is not about tribalism, it is about competence and belonging. We know Adebutu’s family history here. We know all that they have done. We know how compassionate Iya Sunnah has been. We will mobilise our youth with voter education and door-to-door campaigns to ensure victory,” he said.

In his response, Adebutu thanked the indigenes for their warm reception and reaffirmed his commitment to the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate.

“This tour has shown me that our people are yearning for true homegrown leadership. The ITURA DE agenda is not just a slogan, it is a social contract to restore dignity, fix our roads, empower our farmers, create jobs for our youth and return Ogun State to true glory. We are not just campaigning, we are listening, and we will deliver,” he said.

Also speaking, the Ogun PDP deputy governorship candidate, Yemi Kolapo, assured residents that their administration would be inclusive and grassroots-driven.

She said: “What we have seen in all the wards we have visited is genuine love for Ogun State. As a mother and a daughter of this soil, I assure you that our government will prioritise women, children, education and primary healthcare. We will not disappoint you. This ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is a mandate for all of us to save our state from dangerous intrusion.”

World.title: [Watch] Livid Leon Schuster: ‘You’re p*ssing me off!’
World.content:
Leon Schuster has managed to pull off another epic prank, this time on his interviewer, Leanne Manas.

The veteran comedy actor and comedian sat down with the Morning Live presenter to discuss everything from his health to relationships, and even his scariest prank!

WATCH: LEON SCHUSTER PRANKS LEANNE MANAS

In a snippet from the interview, which takes place in Leon Schuster’s house, Leanne Manas asks the veteran star about his response to being accused of using blackface in his candid camera films, which spanned several decades.



The 75-year-old appeared visibly agitated at the question, responding: “That is a sensitive question and I dont want to answer that

“You have affronted me now, and it p*sses me off, I thought we were going to get along.

Now flustered and losing his cool, Schuster added: “Don’t ask me about stuff like that,please! Don’t do that again, beauce I will walk out of this interview

“You don’t do that to me, not in my own house!

The You Must Be Joking star eventually broke from his character, casually announcing: “You’ve been Shucks’d!”

Leanne Manas – almost in tears at the prank – later shared that she had experienced heart palpitations and rush of emotions during Schuster’s pretend confrontation.



She posted: “When I sat down with the legendary Leon Schuster and the conversation took an unexpected turn, my mind started racing. I was trying to work out how to bring things back on track before it all went too far!

She added: “What happened next caught me completely off guard”.

Watch the full interview below…

‘I’LL DIE A PRANKSTER!’

During his interview with Leanne Manas, Leon Schuster added that he had no ill intent behind his candid camera pranks, some of which have courted controversy for its portrayal of “blackface”.

He shared: “I’m a prankster, and I’ll die a prankster. It’s all part of the culture of this land”

“It’s important you know your audience. I try to give the people what they want. I’m so sorry I can’t make one final candid-camera movie. But one more clap and my neck will break”.

He added: “I want to be remembered as that okie from the Free State who stood firmly on the ground, who didnt a swollen head, and who contributed somehow to unify our nation through my movies”.

World.title: ‘Kaizer Chiefs is bigger than Fernando Da Cruz’
World.content:
There are growing concerns that the Chiefs job is too big for Fernando Da Cruz. Photo: Kaizer Chiefs Facebook

Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz is under serious pressure after a dismal start to the campaign. Is he a good fit?

What are Da Cruz’s strengths as a coach?

Before his appointment, Da Cruz was known for his emphasis on tactical discipline and defensive structure. So far, the new boss has been insistent on a system using three central defenders, two wing-backs and a midfield pivot. The 3421 allows the front three to be more flexible. Injuries to regular central midfielders Lebo Maboe and Siphesihle Ndlovu were not ideal

A Marcelo Bielsa STUDENT

Fernando Da Cruz worked alongside legendary Argentinian Marcelo Bielsa at Lille. Da Cruz had three stints with the French outfit in several roles, namely, as a scout, caretaker manager and head coach of the B side, where he nurtured talents such as Idrissa Gueye, Lucas Digne, Victor Osimhen, and Eden Hazard.



Da Cruz has been good to his word, but it hasn’t been good enough

Mfundo Vilakazi has been handed 746 minutes. Only veterans Brandon Petersen, Inacio Miguel and Lebo Maboe have played more than the youngster. 20-year-old Luke Baartman has played 480 minutes, while 22-year-old Wandile Duba is proving his worth and winning the trust of the boss, playing 476 minutes so far. 22-year-old Mdu Shabalala has 442 minutes of playing time so far, but Langelihle Phili’s debut season with the club has been cruelly interrupted by a serious ankle injury. It’s clear that the youngsters are being trusted.

Chiefs are out of the title race

Kaizer Chiefs are already 12 points adrift of leaders Sundowns, and their season is only nine matches old. What conclusions can we draw here? Are the players at Da Cruz’s disposal simply not good enough, or is he not getting the most out of a talented young group?

World.title: ‘Here we are’: Ayanda Borotho unveils latest venture, YaNala Auras!
World.content:
Actress and entrepreneur Ayanda Borotho has peeled back another layer of her business ventures by launching YaNala Auras.

The former Isibaya actress recently introduced her brand on Instagram, paired with the tagline: “Healing auras by Nomafu.”

The luxurious brand offers an array of aromatic products crafted to bring warmth and healing to both living spaces and the body. Its range includes diffusers, soaps, luxury candles, scented bath salts, and linen mists.



AYANDA BOROTHO UNVEILS LATEST CREATION, YANALA AURAS

Ayanda has been forthcoming with information which is aimed at enhancing the customer experience.

She shared a detailed price list and a WhatsApp number for customers wishing to place orders from YaNala Auras.

She also shared the six signature scents that customers can choose from: Nala Star, Zaidi Eternal, Sala Whisper, Maisha Blossoms, Aliye Flora, and Raha Sun, offering multiple options from the brand’s catalogue.

‘HERE WE ARE IN CHAPTER YANALA’

In a personal Instagram post, Ayanda explained that she has been working tirelessly to bring YaNala Auras to life.

However, fear of failure almost engulfed her, as she had originally intended to launch the brand in August 2026.

She also revealed how the name YaNala Auras came about, adding that her faith was the catalyst behind forging ahead with the venture.



“I’ve been silently, tenaciously working on this baby. I intended to launch in August, but I chickened out. I was absolutely fearful of failure,” she began.

“And that’s the honest truth. But then I remembered I wrote a book because I was God-led. I yielded.

Here too, I yielded. And my soul remembered what it’s like to be carried,” she added.

“To trust not in the process but in the processor. So here we are in chapter YaNala, a combination of Yahweh (Divine God) and Nala (Abundance, also my name),” she wrote.

FLAIR FOR INTERIOR DECOR AND SUPPORT FOR BLACK-OWNED BUSINESSES

Over the years, Ayanda has often shown support for black-owned businesses in South Africa. Now, she finds herself on the receiving end of that support, thanking those who have shown interest in YaNala Auras.

In June 2026, Ayanda praised the impressive service of Dreamy Furniture, a black-owned business in Johannesburg that manufactures in luxury couches and headboards.

She had bought couches for her living room, which elevated the look and feel of her home’s interior.

World.title: How teacher salaries in Botswana compare with South Africa
World.content:
Teachers in South Africa and Botswana earn different salaries. Image: Pexels

Teachers in South Africa and Botswana earn different salaries, with qualifications, experience and job grades playing an important role in determining their monthly earnings.

The two neighbouring countries have different public-sector salary structures, but advertised salary scales provide an interesting comparison of what educators can earn.

South Africa’s 2026 teacher salary scales show that educators’ earnings vary significantly depending on their qualifications and experience.



According to salary information published by BusinessTech, the lowest salary notch is R169,707 annually, equivalent to approximately R14 142 per month.

However, qualified teachers with a Relative Education Qualification Value (REQV) of 14 to 17 start at R366 051 annually, translating to approximately R30 504 per month.

Experienced teachers in this category can earn up to R794 151 annually, or about R66 179 per month.



How much do teachers earn in Botswana?

In Botswana, advertised temporary teaching positions provide an indication of salaries available to educators entering the public education system.

A recent recruitment notice for temporary primary and secondary school teachers listed salaries between P108 444 and P123 420 annually for the C4 grade.

This translates to monthly earnings of approximately P9 037 to P10 285.



Teachers appointed under the C3 grade can earn between P127 092 and P150 852 annually, equivalent to approximately P10 591 to P12 571 per month.

Using an indicative exchange rate of P1 to R1.163 on 3 November 2026, the C4 salary range translates to approximately R126 114 to R143 540 annually.

The C3 range is equivalent to approximately R147 808 to R175 441 annually.



South Africa vs Botswana: Who pays teachers more?

The available figures suggest that qualified South African teachers earn more than those advertised in Botswana’s temporary teaching recruitment notice.

For instance, a South African teacher starting in the REQV 14–17 category earns approximately R30 504 monthly, compared with about R14 617 for a Botswana C3 teacher at the bottom of the advertised salary range.

However, the comparison is not a direct like-for-like assessment because the two countries use different grading systems, and the Botswana figures relate specifically to temporary appointments.



Teachers’ actual earnings also depend on qualifications, years of service, responsibilities and applicable benefits.

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns become the first Carling Knockout semi-finalists

World.title: Authorities investigating bird deaths at Johannesburg’s Zoo Lake
World.content:
Carcasses of Egyptian geese and other waterbirds were discovered at Johannesburg's Zoo Lake this past weekend. Images via Canva @Daniel Mminele/@Aayesha-bebe Mayet

An investigation has been launched following the discovery of dead geese and other birds at Zoo Lake in Johannesburg.

As confirmed by the Zoo Lake Users Committee, the carcasses of more than 20 waterbirds – including Egyptian geese – were discovered at Zoo Lake on Sunday, 1 November 2026.

This prompted concerned park visitors and residents to raise the alarm.



JOHANNESBURG DEPARTMENTS INVESTIGATE

As of Monday, 2 November, Johannesburg City Parks and Zoo’s (JCPZ’s) Environmental Conservation team collected and removed the dead birds from the lake.

To establish the cause of death, veterinarians from the Johannesburg Zoo will conduct post-mortem examinations on selected carcasses.

Meanwhile, teams from JCPZ Conservation and Operations, the City’s Environment and Infrastructure Services Department and Johannesburg Water have collected water samples from the site.

POSSIBLE CAUSE OF DEATH

The JCPZ surmise that seasonal avian botulism, a disease fatal to birds, might have caused these birds’ deaths.

“Seasonal avian botulism is among the suspected causes, particularly during the current hot conditions,” said the JCPZ, per a media statement. “Warmer water and decomposing organic matter can create conditions favourable for the production of toxins that affect waterbirds.”

So far, avian botulism has not yet been confirmed, as they await the veterinary findings and water-quality testing results.



“Water-quality testing falls within the environmental oversight function of [the Environment and Infrastructure Services Department],” the JCPZ continued. “While testing provides information about conditions at the time of sampling, it cannot, on its own, predict every wildlife mortality incident. The timing of the deaths, preceding conditions and any available warning signs still need to be established through the investigation.”

JOHANNESBURG RESIDENTS ADVISED TO EXERCISE CAUTION

With the investigation underway, JCPZ reminds residents that the city’s urban dams and lakes are man-made and receive stormwater run-off. This can carry pollutants, litter and organic waste.

Hence, the appearance of clear water shouldn’t be taken as a guarantee that it’s safe to swim in or fish from.

For the sake of precaution, you are strongly encouraged to:

Refrain from swimming in these water bodies or consuming fish caught in them.

Keep children and pets away from dead or visibly distressed wildlife.

Avoid handling dead birds or fish.

Report dead birds, distressed waterbirds and fish kills to emi@jhbcityparks.com. Ensure that you provide the exact location and photographs where possible.

In other news, the SAHRC has raised concerns about corruption linked to water tanker contracts in Gauteng.

World.title: Ekurhuleni power battle: Can the MK Party weaken ANC support?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - With just a few hours to go before election day, the country's metros are under the spotlight.

In Ekurhuleni, ongoing water challenges and other service delivery concerns are among the issues the community is facing.

The latest eNCA MarkData poll shows both the ANC and DA stand a chance of winning the municipality: 31,2% of respondents said they will vote for the DA, while 29,4% chose the ANC.

But other movements could shape control of the metro, including local government election newcomers, the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP).

READ | eNCA MarkData | eThekwini election projections point to major political shift

eNCA Elections Analyst Wayne Sussman believes areas like Katlehong could have a say.

In 2021, the ANC won almost 50% of the vote in ward 52, while the IFP came second with 19%.

Sussman cites hostel communities as the driving force behind this IFP performance.

The political landscape shifted in the 2024 general elections when the MK Party emerged, securing 26% of the vote, while the ANC dropped to 38%.

“Tomorrow, we are going to be watching wards like this to see if uMkhonto weSizwe can create history and win wards off the ANC in townships like Katlehong,” he said.

The Brakpan area was also not left behind as Sussman dissected the political landscape in Ekurhuleni.

“There are about five roadhouses there. This is the area where the Freedom Front Plus did the best in Ekurhuleni in 2021. The DA got over 60% of the vote, and the Freedom Front 17%.” “The Freedom Front scored quite well in the eNCA MarkData poll. And we watch in wards like this, because generally, the ANC has to keep parties like uMkhonto weSizwe, EFF and, to some extent, the IFP, at bay. The DA has to deal with parties like the Freedom Front Plus and the PA,” he explained.

World.title: Lottery licence back to square one after court ruling
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Trade, Industry and Competition Minister, Parks Tau, has to go back to the starting blocks regarding the National Lottery licence.

The licence to run the Lotto was awarded to Sizekhaya Holdings in May last year.

But the High Court in Pretoria has set aside that decision.

The ruling reopens the battle for one of South Africa's most lucrative licences.

READ | High Court sets aside awarding of Lotto licence to Sizekhaya Holdings

The challenge was brought by two unsuccessful bidders, Ithuba Lottery and the Ringeta Consortium.

In his ruling, Judge Norman Davis, found several flaws in the awarding process, including that Tau had taken advice from a new committee which had run a parallel process to that of the evaluation committee.

The judge suspended the declaration of invalidity for 12 months to not disruption lotto operations which are run by Sizekhaya for now.

World.title: SA Explained | Political Branding: Can Campaign Stunts And Slogans Win Voter Trust? | 03 November 2026
World.content:
The Pothole Has Become a Political Message. But Who Is Accountable for Fixing It?

A flooded road, an overflowing sewer or a dry household tap once represented a local service-delivery problem. Increasingly, these failures also provide the raw material for political campaigns. They can be photographed, filmed, shared and transformed into instantly recognisable symbols of municipal government.

The attraction is understandable. A politician standing beside a neglected road does not need a lengthy speech to explain why infrastructure matters. The image does much of the work. It offers a visible problem, identifies a location and invites the public to consider who should be held responsible. In an election campaign crowded with slogans and promises, that kind of simplicity is powerful.

Yet there is an important distinction between drawing attention to a failure and explaining how it will be corrected. The first requires a camera and a compelling moment. The second requires an understanding of municipal budgets, maintenance programmes, procurement, engineering capacity and the institutions responsible for delivery.

South Africa's municipal problems are also too substantial to be reduced to campaign spectacle. In its 2024–25 local government audit outcomes, the Auditor-General reported that only 39 of the country's 257 municipalities obtained clean audits. It also found continuing weaknesses in financial management, compliance and performance reporting, while metropolitan audit outcomes had regressed over the municipal term.

These findings do not establish that every municipality delivers poor services, nor does a clean audit automatically guarantee functioning infrastructure. They do, however, demonstrate why public accountability must extend beyond individual incidents to the systems that determine whether municipalities can deliver consistently.

The distinction becomes especially important when opposition politicians expose failures under an incumbent administration. Such scrutiny can serve a legitimate democratic purpose. Residents benefit when infrastructure problems that have been ignored receive attention, when officials are asked to explain delays and when promises are compared with actual progress.

But the same standard of scrutiny should apply to the politician offering an alternative. Identifying a pothole is not a road-maintenance strategy. Showing a broken water pipe is not a funded infrastructure programme. A credible public explanation should identify the responsible authority, the likely cause, the proposed remedy, the resources required and the timeframe against which progress can be assessed.

Incumbents face a different but equally demanding test. They may inherit neglected infrastructure, deteriorating finances or longstanding administrative weaknesses. These circumstances can help explain why a problem exists, but they do not eliminate responsibility for managing it. A useful response should make the history clear while showing what the current administration has done, what remains unresolved and when residents can expect measurable improvement.

Reputation strategist Tshepo Matseba offered a useful formulation in a conversation with eNCA's Naledi Moleo: "a brand is a promise fulfilled". Applied to municipal government, the phrase raises a practical question. What evidence should residents expect before accepting that a political promise has been honoured?

The answer cannot depend entirely on public relations. A repaired road, a functioning wastewater system or a reliable water supply requires more than a successful media response. It requires capable officials, credible financial information, maintenance planning, oversight and follow-through. Those processes are less visually appealing than a viral video, but they are what allow improvements to continue after the cameras leave.

The most valuable political content may therefore be the kind that creates lasting public scrutiny. A photograph of a flooded street should lead to questions about drainage maintenance, spending and responsibility. A viral clip about broken infrastructure should invite examination of previous repair commitments and current delivery plans. Public attention becomes more useful when it is connected to evidence that residents can revisit.

Campaign advertising can tell a compelling story about what a party intends to do. Municipal performance provides a record of what governing institutions have actually managed to achieve. Neither should be judged solely by a slogan or a single dramatic incident.

When the posters come down, the roads, taps and public services remain. That is where accountability becomes measurable, and where political promises must finally confront the ordinary demands of governing.

References

· Auditor-General of South Africa. Consolidated Report on Local Government Audit Outcomes 2024–25. https://mfma-2025.agsa.co.za/

· Auditor-General of South Africa. Audit Outcomes Overview, 2024–25. https://mfma-2025.agsa.co.za/pages/audit-outcomes-overview

· SA Explained. Naledi Moleo in conversation with Tshepo Matseba, recorded 2 November 2026. Source: SAX_02NOV_Naledi_Tshepo_2026_LGE_transcript.txt.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 1 Cent | 03 Number 2026
World.content:
The Illusion of the Pump: Why Complex Pricing Ecosystems Defy Common Sense

Few economic indicators touch daily routines quite as intimately as the monthly fuel price adjustment. For millions of commuters, logistics operators, and households, the announcement is an anxious ritual. When the adjustment lands on a microscopic one-cent reduction, public reaction oscillates between dark humour and quiet frustration. A single cent offers negligible comfort against the backdrop of broader cost-of-living pressures. Yet focusing purely on the final digit at the pump misses a far more intricate economic narrative happening beneath the surface.

Fuel pricing operates within a tightly regulated ecosystem governed by international petroleum costs, currency volatility, and domestic tax structures. When global crude markets surge due to geopolitical instability, local consumers brace for punishing hikes. In theory, recent state interventions through temporary fuel levy discounts were designed to cushion these systemic blows. However, the final price at the retail level rarely reflects a straightforward subtraction.

The missing link in the equation is the complex adjustment mechanism known as the slate levy. Designed to absorb cumulative under-recoveries in the oil industry over time, the slate levy acts as a financial shock absorber. When international pricing pressures create discrepancies between what fuel costs oil companies and what consumers pay, the slate adjusts. Consequently, substantial state-led relief measures can be entirely neutralized in a single month by a corresponding spike in the slate balance.

This dynamic highlights a broader truth about modern economic management. Systems exposed to multiple external variables rarely yield linear results. A policy designed to provide relief can be swallowed whole by structural pricing mechanisms operating downstream. For consumers and businesses alike, navigating these fluctuations requires looking past the immediate headline figure. True financial resilience relies on understanding the invisible gears turning behind the scenes, long before the fuel ever reaches the nozzle.

World.title: eNCA News Bite | IEC warns of election misinformation, Trump cuts AGOA and diesel prices fall | 03 November 2026
World.content:
Stay informed, fast, with ⁠News Bite⁠, your daily update on South Africa and the world, presented by Marcelle Gordon.

On the eve of the ⁠local government elections⁠, ⁠IEC⁠ chief Sy Mamabolo warns political parties against spreading baseless fraud claims online. Wednesday voting runs from 7am to 9pm. Gauteng police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni details election security. In Ngcobo, two women are arrested for allegedly posing as IEC officials for voting material.

Home Affairs extends its hours, but some 370,000 IDs remain uncollected. Temporary identity certificates are available, but a Randburg glitch frustrates applicants. Democracy Development Programme's Sphamandla Mhlongo questions councillor accountability after voting.

The ⁠Trump administration⁠ moves to remove South Africa from ⁠AGOA⁠ from January, with its decision sent to Congress. ⁠Trade Minister Parks Tau⁠ says the US has raised new concerns despite Pretoria's concessions.

⁠Cosatu's Matthew Parks⁠ urges continued talks to protect exporters and jobs.

A power failure at ⁠Rand Water's⁠ Mapleton pumping station in Boksburg disrupts supplies to ⁠Tshwane⁠, ⁠Ekurhuleni ⁠and three other municipalities. No power-restoration time has been provided.

After ⁠taxi clashes ⁠kill at least ⁠12 people⁠, ⁠Cape Town⁠ rivals ⁠CATA and CODETA⁠ agree to a ceasefire and independent mediation, after earlier failed agreements.

⁠Americans ⁠vote in midterm elections that could reshape ⁠President Donald Trump's ⁠power in Congress for his final two years. Analyst Daniel Silke explains the stakes.
