Speaking at the event, NHAI chairman Santosh Yadav said the initiative is crucial considering that non-availability of soil can hold up embankment works and delay completion of highways. He said one-year of delay in under construction highway projects in Bihar is estimated to lead to around Rs 2,000 cr in civil cost escalation and around Rs 2,800 cr loss in toll remittance.

World.title: U.S. Midterm Elections 2026 LIVE: Trump says midterm results will be ‘better than you think’
World.content:
Polls opened on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) in the U.S. midterm elections, starting with Vermont and several other East Coast States, including New York, New Jersey, Virginia and Kentucky. The vote will decide how much power President Donald Trump has for the rest of his term. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 States are up for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote.

Also read: U.S. Midterm Election night agenda: When polls close and when to expect results

Mr. Trump’s Republican Party controls both chambers of Congress. Democrats need to flip enough seats to win a majority in at least one, which would limit what Mr. Trump can pass in the second half of his presidency. Pollsters expect tough Senate contests for Republicans in Iowa, Kansas and Ohio, while Texas and Michigan are expected to lean towards Democrats.

Also read: Trump’s Republicans scramble to stop Democratic midterms wave

Early voting is on pace to eclipse that of the last midterms, and Democrats appear more enthusiastic than Republicans in opinion polls. On the final day of campaigning, Mr. Trump called the country “booming.” The Supreme Court rejected his push to have thousands of disputed mail-in ballots in California set aside, and Michigan’s Senate race was shaken when Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over her party’s nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

World.title: Driver who ran over officer still absconding as M.P. Police expand search across State
World.content:
A day after running over a police officer in Madhya Pradesh’s Dewas district, the driver accused remains at large on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) even as the police expand their search with multiple teams working across the State, including in districts bordering Gujarat, officials said.

Special DG Upendra Jain told The Hindu that while arresting the driver is a priority, various teams are also looking for the other three accused of an interstate illicit liquor racket.

Inspector Dilip Puri, in charge of Dewas’s Khategaon police station, had died in the wee hours of Monday (November 2, 2026) after he was allegedly mowed down by a truck carrying illicit liquor to Gujarat that he had stopped for checking. A constable was also injured in the incident and the accused driver had been identified as Gajendra Rawat, a resident of Alirajpur district.

Mr. Rawat had fled the scene by crossing over a road divider and abandoned the truck after some distance to escape. The police had seized about 1,800 litres of illicit liquor hidden in the truck.

Following the death, the police had uncovered an inter-state bootlegging network illegally supplying liquor from Harda district to Alirajpur and further smuggling it across the State border into Gujarat.

Three persons, including key accused Rahul Jaiswal who allegedly ran the entire racket from Harda, his associate Vijay Rao in Indore and the truck owner Kairam Singh Changod, a resident of Alirajpur, have been arrested in the case so far, while search is on for three of Mr. Rahul’s alleged business partners and Mr. Rawat.

The police have said that Mr. Rahul has admitted to be a Congress functionary in Dewas. The Opposition party, that has launched scathing attacks on the BJP government over illicit liquor trade over the past few weeks, is yet to respond to Mr. Rahul’s arrest.

“The main person on the supply side was Rahul Jaiswal and on the execution side, it was Kairam Singh and this driver. We have two of them in custody. We have teams working in various districts, including border areas like Alirajpur where they would smuggle liquor into Gujarat from. The remaining people will be arrested soon,” he said.

Mr. Jain also said that the accused would avoid crossing the truck into Gujarat and supply liquor in small quantities from the border areas of Alirajpur and sell in the neighbouring State.

“They [Mr. Rawat and Mr. Changod] would stock the illicit liquor with them in Alirajpur and then smuggle it into Gujarat on motorbike or other smaller vehicles through porous border in forest areas to avoid checking on state borders,” he added.

The police are yet to make an estimate of the total amount of liquor smuggled from Harda.

“Our priority at the moment is arresting all persons. The specific amount is not relevant at this point because it does not change the offence and what we seized from the truck was anyway a large amount,” he added.

Meanwhile, the Dewas Police have also arrested Madhya Pradesh Congress spokesperson Anand Kasliwal in connection with a separate ongoing investigation into a counterfeit liquor manufacturing and selling racket, that allegedly has claimed 13 lives in Dewas in October.

Mr. Anand’s son, Aman Kasliwal, an Indore-based businessman, had been arrested on October 28 for allegedly selling chemicals used to make the fake liquor. Mr. Aman was among the 11 persons arrested in the case for manufacturing and selling the liquor in Dewas’s villages.

Officers said that Mr. Anand was arrested for allegedly tempering with evidence and sale records at his son’s shop.

Mr. Anand had earlier, in a statement, claimed innocence for his son saying that his company had legally sold paint thinner with proper billing and denying any connection with those involved in manufacturing counterfeit liquor.

World.title: When will 14 State-run universities get Vice-Chancellors and Syndicates, Madras High Court asks T.N. government
World.content:
Taking serious note of as many as 14 State-run universities functioning without Vice-Chancellors/Syndicates for the last three to four years, the Madras High Court on Tuesday called for an explanation from Tamil Nadu government as to when normalcy would be restored in all those educational institutions.

Justice N. Anand Venkatesh requested Advocate General Vijay Narayan to appear on behalf of the Higher Education Secretary, whom the judge impleaded suo motu in a batch of applications pending before him, and explain the reason for the absence of Vice-Chancellors/Syndicates on November 17, 2026.

The judge was seized of a batch of eight sub applications filed by the retired employees of Annamalai University to reopen their contempt of court petitions filed against the university Registrar since their pension had not been disbursed yet. In response, the Registrar said, the process was under way and sought time.

Senior counsel R. Singaravelan, representing the applicants, told the court that the Registrar was facing practical difficulties in administering the institution since it did not have a Vice-Chancellor or a Syndicate and was being run by a Convenor Committee headed by the Higher Education Secretary.

After recording his submission, the judge said, he dealt with yet another major issue where the retirement benefits of 500 former employees of the University of Madras got settled after a prolonged pressure exerted by the court. Anna University too was facing a similar issue.

“The common thread that runs through these Universities is the functioning of the Universities without Vice-Chancellors and properly-constituted Syndicate and their present functioning with the assistance of temporary Registrars and Convenor Committees,” the judge highlighted.

He went on to state: “The Convenor Committee headed by the IAS Officer, at the best can only be a temporary arrangement and it is virtually impossible for this Committee to run the Universities and administer the Colleges falling under the purview of those Universities.”

Lamenting that this status was continuing for three to four years, the judge said: “It has a direct impact on the functioning of the educational institutions. If the State government does not take immediate steps to set right this anomaly, it will directly impact the higher education in Tamil Nadu.”

Wanting to find a solution to the problem, the judge suo motu impleaded the Higher Education Secretary as one of the respondents and directed the officer to apprise the court of the steps taken by the government so far to restore normalcy in all the 14 State universities which were suffering without a regular administrative setup.

World.title: 7,000 kg of unhygienic, foul-smelling khoya seized, destroyed: Delhi CMO
World.content:
The Food Safety Department of the Delhi government carried out an inspection at Mori Gate Khoya Market on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) and seized and destroyed about 7,000 kg of unhygienic and foul-smelling khoya, taking the total quantity of khoya destroyed by the department so far to 10,660 kg, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said.

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government would not compromise on public health, and ensuring that people have access to safe and quality food during the festive season is one of the government’s foremost responsibilities. “Those involved in food adulteration, regardless of how influential they may be, will be brought within the ambit of the law and face strict action,” she said.

Also, 35 of 44 samples of khoya failed preliminary tests at the ‘Food Safety on Wheels’ mobile testing facility. Two additional samples were also collected and sent to a laboratory for detailed examination. “The preliminary tests conducted at the site also brought to light information relating to milk powder, vanaspati and substances used for binding in the suspected material. Samples have been sent to the laboratory for further investigation into these ingredients,” an official statement said.

The Food Safety Department has been conducting sustained drives against food adulteration in view of the festive season. As part of the action taken so far, the department destroyed 2,830 kg of khoya on September 4, 610 kg on September 8 and 520 kg on October 23, as per the CMO.

World.title: Iranian woman moves Madras High Court wanting to know procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous visa
World.content:
A 30-year-old Iranian woman, reportedly born in a Zoroastrian family but forced to practice Islam in her country before converting to Christianity, has approached the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Chennai to explain to her the procedure for obtaining X-Miscellaneous Visa so that she could step out of a special camp for foreigners in Tiruchi.

Pegah Ansari, daughter of Ansari Shapour, told the court that she was born and raised in a Zoroastrian family in Tehran. Claiming that all citizens at birth get registered as Muslims, irrespective of their actual religious background or personal faith, in her country; the petitioner said: “As a result, despite being born into a Zoroastrian family, I was officially recorded as a Muslim in government records.”

She went on to state: “Throughout my life in Iran, I lived under constant fear of persecution on account of my religious beliefs and personal convictions. Over time, I came to believe in and follow the teachings of Christianity. Due to the strict restrictions imposed on religious conversion in Iran, I was compelled to practice and profess my Christian faith only in private and in secrecy.”

Ms. Ansari said, she had no other option but to flee her country in 2019 because her private conversion to Christianity came to the notice of the authorities in Iran where she faced a genuine and imminent threat of persecution, harassment and possible arrest. She flew first to Georgia and underwent conversion through appropriate religious process. She resided there till 2022.

Her second stop was Sri Lanka where stayed approximately for a month before flying down to India on a one-month-long tourist visa in April 2022. “I came to India in search of safety, stability, and the freedom to live without fear of religious persecution,” the petitioner said and claimed to have obtained refugee status from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in March 2025.

She said, the Anjugramam police in Kanniyakumari district had arrested her on December 10, 2025 when she had gone to a resort over there for decorating the venue of a birthday party. The charge levelled against her was that she had overstayed in India despite the expiry of her tourist visa on May 12, 2022. The police personnel also found that the petitioner’s Iranian passport had expired on February 17, 2024.

The petitioner was lodged at the women’s prison at Puzhal near Chennai until the Kanniyakumari Principal District and Sessions Court granted her bail on January 29, 2026. Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to the Tiruchi special camp for foreigners on the basis of a December 23, 2025 Government Order which authorised her detention in the camp until the disposal of the criminal case or her deportation.

Claiming that the State could not curtail her free movement even after grant of bail, the petitioner said, she would be able to approach the appropriate authorities for getting relocated to some other country only if she was allowed to move freely without being confined to the boundaries of the special camp. The petitioner wanted to know the procedure for obtaining the visa required to face court proceedings.

The petitioner said that she had made a representation in this regard to the FRRO on June 25, 2026 but complained that the officer did not respond.

World.title: Ladakh administration asks activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife to stop ‘unauthorised activities’ at their Leh school
World.content:
The Ladakh administration on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) asked the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Ladakh’s (HIAL) Desert Flower School, run by activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife, “to stop unauthorised activities of the school”, citing the matter pertaining to the allotment of land as “sub judice”. Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk extends support to people of Arunachal Pradesh resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.

“Desert Flower School of the HIAL Ecosystem has commenced functioning of the school without necessary clearance/approval from the competent authority. The administration asks HIAL to strictly maintain the status quo and avoid causing any prejudice to the case pending before the High Court of J&K and Ladakh,” said a spokesman of the L-G administration.

It claimed that the school “commenced activities without obtaining the requisite consent, clearances and approvals from the concerned authorities”. The administration pointed out that the matter concerning HIAL was pending adjudication before the court.

On September 22, Gitanjali Angmo, wife of Mr. Wangchuk, requested the Deputy Commissioner, Leh, for the issuance of a No Objection Certificate and clearance for the proposed members of the Managing Committee of the school located at Phyang, Leh. The Administration had cancelled the land allotment to HIAL in August 2025.

“Accordingly, the notice issued by Tehsildar, Leh, has strongly advised HIAL to maintain strict status quo and not undertake any action whatsoever towards the functioning or commencement of activities,” said the L-G order.

Meanwhile, Mr. Wangchuk, who has been campaigning for a special status for Ladakh and was jailed last year under the National Security Act (NSA), on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) wrote a letter to President Droupadi Murmu and appealed for intervention “to protect the rights of indigenous communities, democratic freedoms, and the fragile Himalayan ecology in Arunachal Pradesh”.

“I write to you with a heavy heart, as an environmental activist from Ladakh who has spent decades working to protect our fragile Himalayan environment. I urgently seek your intervention in the disturbing situation unfolding in the Siang Valley of Arunachal Pradesh, where indigenous communities, particularly the Adi people, are resisting the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. We in Ladakh understand their pain,” reads the letter.

Mr. Wangchuk said for years, people of Ladakh have been peacefully demanding constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule to protect fragile ecology, ancestral lands and cultural identity. “We know what it feels like when decisions affecting our future are taken without adequately consulting us. Coming from an indigenous tribal community yourself, you understand that for us, nature is not merely a resource to be exploited, but a mother to be protected,” the letter reads.

In the letter, Mr. Wancghuk highlighted the reports about thousands of security personnel being deployed, young activists arrested, and villagers subjected to intimidation and restrictions on movement.

“There are serious allegations of police excesses, including against elderly villagers, and criminal cases against those opposing the project. What pains me particularly is the attempt to portray people raising legitimate concerns as anti-national or foreign-funded,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

He said it was deeply unfortunate that people who have stood by the nation in its most difficult times should face such accusations. “We have witnessed such allegations in Ladakh over the past year, and now similar accusations are being made against the people of Arunachal Pradesh. Such shortsighted accusations, particularly when made without credible evidence, do not strengthen national security. They weaken it. In sensitive border regions, the trust, goodwill and active cooperation of local communities are among our country’s greatest strategic strengths,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

He also appealed for de-escalation, protection of democratic rights and biological safeguards.

“Respected Rashtrapati Ji, the Himalayas are both the water towers of India and the shield of our borders. Protecting their ecology and respecting the communities who have lived here for generations is not against national development or national security. It is essential to both. I sincerely hope that your understanding of indigenous communities and the moral authority of your office will help bring peace, justice and meaningful dialogue to the Siang Valley. Our border communities deserve to be treated as trusted partners in nation-building, not as suspects for raising their voices,” he added.

World.title: SIT report says charges against KSU activists in Veena George case cannot be sustained
World.content:
The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has submitted its final report to the court, stating that the charges levelled against Kerala Students Union (KSU) activists in connection with the alleged attack on former Health Minister Veena George at Kannur railway station cannot be sustained.

The SIT found that the protesters had not committed the offences alleged in the original chargesheet and stated that waving black flags as a form of protest did not constitute a criminal offence.

The final report was submitted by SIT chief U. Preman before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court in Kannur. The investigation team concluded that the protesters had not committed offences such as rioting, wrongful restraint, obstructing public servants from discharging their official duties or criminal trespass on railway premises.

The charge of attempted murder, which was initially included in the first information report, was subsequently dropped by the first investigation team while filing the chargesheet.

According to the SIT report, the responsibility of the police personnel accompanying Veena George was to prevent the protesters from approaching her. However, the protesters did not obstruct the police from discharging their official duties. Instead, the police stopped those waving black flags. The SIT also found that the Minister had not been wrongfully restrained by the protesters.

The report further stated that the protesters had entered the railway station after purchasing valid platform tickets. Therefore, the charge of trespassing on railway premises was not sustainable. The SIT also cited court observations that black flag protests did not constitute a criminal offence.

Meanwhile, the SIT had earlier submitted a separate report to the Director General of Police, recommending action against Veena George’s former gunman, Abhilash, for allegedly giving a false statement, as well as against officials who had allegedly failed to conduct the preliminary investigation properly.

The court will now decide on further proceedings based on the final report submitted by the SIT.

World.title: Vigilance wing pulls up Kochi Metro Rail Limited over lapses in auctioning commercial spaces
World.content:
The Vigilance wing of Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) has pulled up the agency for a slew of alleged omissions in the leasing of commercial spaces at the 22 metro stations along the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura phase-one corridor, which resulted in substantial revenue loss over the past few years.

The metro agency’s Vigilance wing observed that the auction of commercial spaces at the stations was conducted without s and in a “less transparent” manner. The auctions were conducted outside the scope of the procurement manual, and the basic principles of transparency, competition, fairness and elimination of discretion were not followed in letter and spirit. Base rates were not fixed on the basis of objective data. Instead, a trial-and-error method was adopted.

Changes in rates and other conditions, such as the earnest money deposit (EMD), resulted in prospective bidders adopting a wait-and-see approach, while creating a sense of differential treatment among existing vendors. A level playing field was missing. Moreover, e-auction or forward auction through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) was not considered. In most cases, there was only a single bidder. The absence of a standard operating procedure for conducting auctions led to ad hoc practices and subjectivity in the process, further reflecting the lack of transparency.

The Vigilance wing also took note of the absence of a finance member in the auction committee, in contravention of the provisions of the procurement manual. There were also several corrections, overwritings and omissions in the registration forms and the auction register. Adding to the concerns, the terms and conditions of the auction were relaxed midway through the process without public notice. The EMD amount kept changing from one auction to another, and it was eventually decided not to collect it at all.

In view of these findings, the Vigilance wing recommended that base rates be fixed on the basis of objective data. It also called for a consistent policy on the auction of spaces for hiring or advertising to avoid the trial-and-error approach to fixing base rates, ambiguity in deciding the mode of auction and confusion over the auction procedure.

In this regard, a forward auction module of GeM or its e-auction module should be considered, after due preparation, instead of outdated and less transparent methods such as physical or hybrid auctions. Adequate publicity, including through the media, should be ensured to prevent ad hoc practices and subjectivity in conducting auctions. A standard operating procedure (SOP) for conducting auctions should be drawn up, and a finance member should be included in the auction committee. The mandatory declaration of ‘Conflict of Interest’ by auction committee members should also be ensured.

Other recommendations include continuous videographing or recording of the auction or tender process through CCTV and preparation of the minutes after the auction.

World.title: Pakistan successfully tests its first indigenously developed air-to-air missile Fa’az: ISPR
World.content:
Pakistan on Tuesday performed a successful flight test of the country’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az, “marking another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defence capabilities”, the military’s media wing said.

According to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and can engage enemy targets at longer ranges.

“Fa’az will significantly enhance [the] operational flexibility of [the] Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defence posture. The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry,” the statement added.

The launch was witnessed by senior military officers, scientists and engineers involved in the development of the system, the ISPR said.

It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and the service chiefs congratulated the scientists.

Pakistan’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az, is test-launched from a JF-17 fighter jet in this video released on Nov 3, 2026. — Screengrab via X/DGPR_PAF

Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi issued a statement congratulating the nation on the test.

“Our scientists and engineers have once again achieved a remarkable feat that makes the nation proud,” the ministry quoted him as saying. “The successful test of the indigenously developed Fa’az missile marks a significant advancement in the field of defence.

“We are all proud of Pakistan’s distinguished scientists and engineers.”

Pakistan successfully tested two surface-to-surface missiles last month; the Fatah-2 extended range (ER) hypersonic ballistic missile was tested on Oct 13, and the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile was tested a week before that.

ISPR said that the Fatah-2 ER is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

“It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating [the] enemy’s missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features,” it added.

For Fatah-IV ER, ISPR said: “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”

It noted that the test “also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability”.

World.title: Americans vote in midterm election seen as a referendum on Trump presidency
World.content:
Americans voted on Tuesday in a midterm election seen as a nationwide referendum on US President Donald Trump that could wrest control of Congress from his Republican Party and impose major restraints on the remaining two years of his presidency.

Polls predict the Democrats will win a majority in the House of Representatives and possibly seize the Senate on the back of voter resentment at an unpopular president, soaring energy costs and the dragging conflict with Iran.

Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.

Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in an Atlanta suburb, told AFP he “voted for mostly Democratic candidates”.

“It’s just about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things,” Comer said. “It needs to change for the everyday person and I’m an everyday person.”

People exit the voting booths at the ward 2 voting site at the Barn at Bull Meadow on Nov 3, 2026 in Concord, New Hampshire. — AFP

Trump defended his record in a final TV phone-in pitch to voters on Tuesday, saying he had rebuilt the country through his immigration crackdown, war on Iran and tariff policy.

“We have to keep America great. We’re great now. We were terrible two years ago,” Trump told ‘Fox & Friends’.

All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

Demonstrators protest against US President Donald Trump as he delivers a speech marking the end of the midterm election campaign at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, DC, on Nov 2, 2026. — AFP

Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.

The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.

In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff, who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future.

“I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP.

Economic discontent

Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and anti-migrant stance will benefit voters, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radical socialists — a message that seemed to resonate with Daryl Ruley, an 84-year-old voter in Austin, Texas.

“A lot of today’s younger people think socialism is the way to go,” Ruley told AFP. “They don’t understand history if they believe that’s the case.”

But in his final public campaign appearance on Monday, Trump barely touched on the election and gave a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool.

“This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message”.

Some Republican supporters remain confident. “We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.

Republicans currently hold a 53-47 Senate majority, but the battlefield has extended into once reliably conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

US Senator Elizabeth Warren (L), Democrat from Massachusetts, joins Democratic US Senate candidate for Michigan Abdul El-Sayed at a midterm campaign rally in Eastern Michigan University in Ypsilanti, Ann Arbour, Michigan on Nov 2, 2026. — AFP

Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw Congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast projected 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Trump, who will watch the midterm results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress, he could simply defy Democrats.

“I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

Justice Department to monitor elections in all 50 states

More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating high engagement.

The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.

As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.

Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating. His administration has stepped up efforts to investigate suspected non-citizen voting, although research and election officials indicate that such cases are exceedingly rare.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.

The Justice Department also announced that it was deploying approximately 1,000 election monitors and observers across all 50 states for the first time in its history.

Voters cast their ballots inside a polling location in the social hall at St Patrick’s Church on November 3, 2026 in Youngstown, Ohio. — AFP

The expanded monitoring effort has also raised questions about the federal government’s role in elections, which are primarily administered by state and local authorities. The Justice Department is part of the executive branch headed by Trump, unlike the courts, which exercise an independent judicial function.

The department described the deployment as “the largest election-monitoring effort in its history”, saying it was intended to “protect voting rights, ensure election integrity and promote transparency”.

Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon, who heads the Civil Rights Division, described election integrity as a top priority for the administration.

“Election integrity has been one of the top priorities for this Administration and this Division,” Dhillon said.

Democratic US Senate candidate Chris Pappas speaks to members of the media after voting in the US midterm elections at Webster Elementary School in Manchester, New Hampshire, US, November 3, 2026.

The monitors will check compliance with federal laws protecting voting rights, including the Voting Rights Act. Their responsibilities will also include overseeing protections for voters with disabilities and enforcing laws prohibiting voter intimidation and suppression based on race, colour, national origin or religion.

The department said its personnel would remain in contact with state and local election officials throughout Election Day.

It also urged voters who encounter violence, threats or intimidation at polling places to contact local police immediately by calling 911. Suspected violations of federal voting rights laws can also be reported to the Civil Rights Division.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs5.45 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs3.68
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52.

The prices are applicable for Nov 4 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The latest price cut also comes as international oil prices slid about 2 per cent to a three-week low on Tuesday in volatile trade. The market weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries about additional supply disruptions from recent attacks in both conflicts.

Brent futures fell $1.63, or 2pc, to $103.14 a barrel at 8:44pm PKT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 67 cents, or 1pc, to $95.79. Brent was on track for its lowest close since Oct 7 and WTI was headed for its lowest close since Oct 14.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference today, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

He also hinted at the latest reduction in fuel prices, saying “even better news will come before us”.

Meanwhile, Jamaat-i-Islami and the government held another round of talks to discuss possible relief to low-income citizens in petroleum prices, and agreed to continue their negotiations in the coming days.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Reuters

World.title: CM Maryam incensed at Chaudhry Salik's claims of corruption in Punjab, sends him Rs5bn defamation notice
World.content:
LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks.

During a private television channel talk show on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi.

However, he also took a swipe at the present provincial administration, alleging that political considerations were increasingly shaping development priorities and influencing the allocation of public funds. He said he regularly heard complaints of corruption in Punjab, alleging that a disproportionate share of the province’s development budget was being channelled towards Lahore.

Addressing a ceremony in Attock on Tuesday, CM Maryam said: “There is a federal minister … somebody sent me his statement about corruption in Punjab. Today, I am sending him a defamation notice.”

She said that she would not hear “false allegations of corruption”.

“If you have evidence, bring it forth — otherwise I will drag you to court,” she said. She also asked him why he remained a minister in a government that he considered corrupt.

The chief minister went on to say that the reason behind the anger of the PML-Q leader was neither a matter of corruption nor progress. The issue, she said, was that she changed the deputy commissioner (DC) of Gujrat a few days ago whereas Salik had wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed.

“I will not allow anyone to interfere in the will of the people,” she said.

Maryam also took exception to Salik’s comments calling Elahi the “best-ever chief minister” in Punjab.

“The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining. Believe me … the water was up to here,” she said, gesturing to her neck.

“My Land Cruiser was completely submerged,” she said.

“It looked less like Gujrat and more like a village … now, go and look at Gujrat. Now, when it rains, the rainwater doesn’t accumulate. That work was not done by the Chaudhrys,” she said.

Subsequently, the PML-N posted on X that a defamation notice had been sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman, Muhammad Iqbal.

The notice said that the office of chief minister carried “substantial” public responsibility and required “the highest degree of integrity, credibility and public confidence”, which made any allegations of dishonesty or corruption — disseminated to “millions of viewers” via electronic or digital media — a serious matter.

It said that during the interview, Butt had “introduced and led the discussion” regarding alleged corruption in Punjab, while Salik “proceeded to make sweeping and baseless allegations against the provincial administration”.

“The manner in which the subject was introduced and pursued was not a neutral request for clarification of any identified incident, investigation or documented complaint,” the notice said.

“Rather, it provided a platform for the propagation of serious allegations without first identifying any verifiable material or establishing their factual foundation,” it added.

The notice said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province.

“The most alarming aspect of the aforesaid statements is the express admission that he possesses no evidence to substantiate the allegations,” it added.

It stated that the chief minister considered the conduct of all three individuals named in the notice “serious and unacceptable”: Salik for his “false statements”, Butt for his editorial conduct and Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the allegations.

The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question.

It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages. The notice gave a period of seven days for these actions and warned that failure to comply would lead to legal proceedings.

‘I responded honestly’

Speaking to the media in the wake of CM Maryam’s comments, Salik said he was sticking to his statement. In remarks aired by Geo News, he said: “God save us from pride and arrogance”.

Asked about providing evidence for the corruption allegations, he said: “Please go and listen to the interview again.”

He also refuted the claim that the row had to do with distracting from the matter of new provinces.

“It was an interview, someone asked a question and I responded honestly,” he said.

“Yes, there definitely is [corruption],” he added.

Responding to the remarks, CM Maryam said: “So, levelling false accusations is considered humility, while offering a response is deemed arrogance? Bravo!”

During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending, particularly the use of official aircraft, arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

His comments had also prompted a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised the PML-Q leader not to “bite the hand that feeds him”.

Bokhari had also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request for appointment of a DC of his choice being turned down.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote.

While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

World.title: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operations in Balochistan: ISPR
World.content:
A soldier was martyred and 17 terrorists were killed in two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, the military’s media affairs wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces conducted the IBOs on Nov 1 on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy Fitna al Hindustan”.

The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The statement said the first IBO was conducted in the Sanni area of Kachhi district. During the operation, “terrorists’ attempt to establish [a] road block in the city was thwarted by proactive action of security forces,“ resulting in the killing of 10 terrorists.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered,” it added.

Separately, security forces busted a terrorist hideout in Kharan and after an intense fire exchange, “seven Indian-sponsored khawarij were sent to hell”.

ISPR said that weapons and ammunition were also recovered during this operation. The statement added that Sepoy Hikmatullah, who was 25 years old and a resident of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district, was martyred during the IBO.

“Sanitisation operations are being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorist found in the area,” it added.

ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the “menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

In a statement, President Asif Ali Zardari commended the security forces for killing 17 terrorists and also paid tribute to Sepoy Hikmatullah.

“[His] sacrifice for the defence of the homeland and for peace and security will always be remembered,” the president said, extending “heartfelt” condolences and sympathy to the bereaved family.

“Operations under Azm-i-Istehkam will continue until the complete eradication of terrorism sponsored and supported from abroad,” President Zardari added.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces on the successful operations. In a post on X, the interior ministry said he also commended the professional capabilities of security forces in “thwarting the terrorists’ nefarious designs”.

He also paid tribute to the martyred soldier, saying that the “brave sons of the security forces are a source of pride for the nation”.

“The security forces remain committed to the complete eradication of Indian-sponsored terrorists,” he said.

World.title: Imran's nephew denied jail meeting this time; PTI open to possible alliance with JUI-F
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan was again denied a meeting with his family and lawyers on Tuesday – a prescribed day by the Islamabad High Court for meetings at the Adiala jail.

The denial comes just a day after Imran’s lawyer, Barrister Salman Safdar, was allowed to meet him and his incarcerated wife Bushra Bibi for consultations on a legal case.

The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives , Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted in recent months.

Speaking to Dawn on Tuesday, Advocate Awais Younas Chaudhry said a son of Imran’s sister Uzma Khanum, Abdullah Khan, reached Adiala jail as a family member to meet the PTI founder.

However, authorities did not grant him permission, said Chaudhry, who had submitted a list of lawyers and party leaders to the Adiala jail administration for meetings with Imran.

Chaudhry, whose name was also included in the list, said that lawyers, including PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, also reached the prison, but were not allowed to meet the ex-premier.

Imran’s sisters — Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan — used to stage frequent sit-ins outside the Adiala jail demanding the PTI founder’s release.

However, the three sisters have remained detained since late September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

Potential JUI-F support

Meanwhile, PTI has hinted that it can get support from Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in the struggle against the government.

Speaking to the media, the PTI secretary general remarked that no one was terming Fazl a “saviour”, but the PTI would welcome everyone who would stand by the party and struggle against the incumbent government.

“It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” Raja said.

“We do not depend on anyone, and we do not have expectations from anyone,” Raja stated. However, he emphasised that the party wanted its caravan to grow, hinting towards a possible PTI–JUI-F alliance if Fazl offers to join.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Since mid-October, the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Gohar refutes rumour that Imran ‘happy’ about KP governor’s rule

Separately, the PTI chairman dismissed the notion that Imran himself wanted his party’s government in KP to be sacked and was happy with the imposition of governor’s rule.

“It is not correct,” Barrister Gohar said.

Gohar claimed that Barrister Safdar informed him, after his meeting with Imran, that the jailed ex-premier was already aware of the measures and he did not say that it was a positive step as they did not talk much about politics.

The federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder.

Replying to a question, Gohar claimed that Barrister Safdar did not bring any political message from jail. Nevertheless, the PTI chairman welcomed Monday’s meeting with Imran as a positive development.

He hoped that the political tension would end, rejecting the reports of any forward bloc in PTI’s KP wing.

Last month, there were rumours of a group of KP MPAs endorsing Ali Amin Gandapur as the acting provincial president in the absence of Junaid Akbar.

However, PTI soon clarified that Akbar remained the party’s president for KP and named Senator Noorul Haq Qadri to take over his duties in his absence.

Similarly, after several PTI parliamentarians questioned the party’s decisions and overreliance on Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is non-functional during governor’s rule — PTI reaffirmed its support for him.

In its latest clarification a day ago, PTI insisted there was no “factionalism” or “division” within the party, and warned of action against any member who violates party discipline or policy.

World.title: 'We made a deal months ago': Trump says US will stop $4 billion funding to Israel at end of 2026
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year.

Speaking to Fox News’ ‘Fox and Friends’, Trump said Israel no longer needed the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel as a talking point to criticise Republicans.

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump told the broadcaster.

“We’ve already agreed that by the end of this year we won’t be paying Israel. Now we’ll help Israel if they need it.”

There was no immediate comment from Netanyahu’s office on Trump’s remarks.

It was not immediately clear which exact funding Trump meant.

A memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8bn in annual US military aid to Israel is approaching its expiration date in 2028, and conversations have been under way on how Washington’s assistance to Israel would evolve beyond that date.

“They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world,” Trump added.

Netanyahu said in a May interview with CBS that he hoped to wean Israel off US military support within a decade. In a June letter to a US congressman, he wrote that the time had come for Israel “to move from aid recipient to partner”.

US public support for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats.

A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48 per cent of voters and 66pc of Democrats believe the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 16pc and 20pc when the question was first asked in 2017.

Support for Israel among Democratic voters has plummeted, candidates critical of Israel are winning Democratic primaries, and even moderate lawmakers are increasingly willing to challenge decades of US support for Israel.

“The left uses the $4bn payment that everybody knows about — well, it’s no secret — as a signal of unfairness, and we can’t allow that to happen,” Trump said.

“We were giving them $4bn, we are, but it gets cut off at the end of the year. Why? Because they don’t need it.”

World.title: Binance reveals hackers used fake job interviews, malicious code in $6.3bn heist
World.content:
Binance released on Tuesday a detailed investigation into the $6.3 billion hack of its cryptocurrency platform, showing how attackers used fake job interviews and malicious code to steal the funds.

The crypto exchange said it had replenished 98 per cent of the affected assets by drawing on its own funds, with the remaining amount involving little-traded currencies that are harder to acquire.

The attack, carried out over about four hours on Oct 29, was attributed by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to North Korea-affiliated hackers.

Pyongyang has denied the allegations, with the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un calling the claim “absurd rhetoric”.

Around $2.85bn of the stolen $6.34bn has been frozen, Binance said, meaning that the attackers could not use it or convert it to another currency.

Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes.

News of the hacking attack, which is thought to be the biggest ever crypto heist, caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply.

According to Binance, attackers took their first steps towards the breach as early as June.

First, they targeted a platform engineer by getting them to download a virus-laden version of the widely-known programming software Homebrew.

Binance’s cybersecurity teams identified the malware and removed it, but the hackers had already had time to harvest information about the engineer and his colleagues.

In September, the attackers approached another Binance engineer through a legitimate job-search platform, offering him an interview for a position in a fictitious company.

After building trust with the subject through the sharing of social media photos and videos, they asked the engineer to download a test exercise as part of the interview process.

The exercise contained malware that deployed “sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques,” Binance said, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version.

That malware was critical to the success of the attack, as it allowed the hackers to establish a connection with Binance’s internal systems.

On October 20, the attackers used the access they had gained and an internal AI tool to gain control over software used by two other engineers.

Nine days later, they triggered malicious code that initiated the attack.

Binance says outflows normalised as North Korea rejects US allegation

Asset outflows from Binance have normalised and the company was in “very strong financial health”, its co-CEO said.

The world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, whose customers had withdrawn a net $4.72bn as of Monday after the financial heist, has also launched a campaign to stem outflows and woo new users.

“In the first 24 hours, there was a spike in terms of withdrawals, as can be expected. But after that … it’s pretty much normalised,” Richard Teng told a Hong Kong Fintech Week event on Tuesday.

“The company is in very strong financial health,” he said.

“This is something that we can cover. We are able to do so.”

The crypto exchange was seeing “hourly deposits exceed withdrawals”, Binance said in an X post earlier on Tuesday, adding that it reflected improving user activity and stabilising flows.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on the weekend that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in crypto assets, a crime that sent shockwaves through the industry.

Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said the US allegations proved Washington remained hostile towards Pyongyang, according to a report on Tuesday by state news agency KCNA.

Pyongyang has not responded to US President Donald Trump’s overtures, made earlier this year, to resume summit diplomacy. In the wake of the US allegations, Kim Yo Jong said North Korea had “issues to reconsider” over what she called US hostility.

“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a ‘cyber criminal state’, claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organisation ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” KCNA quoted Kim Yo Jong as saying.

“But the US assertion is absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” said Kim, a ruling party official. DPRK is short for the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.

“It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds.”

Revenue stream

North Korea faces growing scrutiny over cryptocurrency theft, which analysts say is a key source of funds for its weapons programmes.

Cybersecurity experts say North Korean hackers are among the world’s most prolific crypto thieves and the proceeds help fund the country’s efforts to develop nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles capable of hitting the United States.

North Korea has stolen cryptocurrency worth $7.6bn this year, more than in any previous year, according to estimates by blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

North Korea denies allegations linking it to cryptocurrency theft and other cybercrimes.

Analysts in Seoul said Pyongyang’s unusually swift response likely reflected concern that the allegation could lead to tighter efforts to disrupt revenue streams that North Korea is accused of using to finance its weapons.

“With sanctions already in place, cryptocurrency theft has become one of North Korea’s key channels for securing funds for regime maintenance and weapons development,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies.

Additional US measures targeting crypto wallets, laundering networks and cryptocurrency exchanges could choke off an important source of revenue, Lim said.

South Korea’s central bank estimated North Korea’s gross domestic product at 47.18 trillion won ($35.09bn) in 2025, meaning the Binance theft could be equivalent to about a sixth of its economic output.

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated 89pc of crypto hack losses in 2026 were linked to North Korea, up from 15pc in 2021.

It said the average reported loss per hack rose from $50.65 million in 2021 to $185.65m in 2026.

“I guess you could call it big game hunting, where they’re targeting these larger exchanges that may take more time and more complexity to be able to do … but the payoff can be relatively large,” said Alec Zebrick, senior manager of Asia-Pacific Global Services at Chainalysis.

Infographic depicting amount lost every month due to crypto hacks. — Courtesy Reuters

North Korea is one of the world’s most impoverished countries but has poured resources secured through illicit means and activities banned under UN Security Council resolutions into its missile and nuclear programmes.

Kim Yo Jong said North Korea would “reconsider” unspecified issues in light of the “very unpleasant US hostile attitude”, without elaborating.

North Korea has not publicly responded to Trump’s offers to resume summit diplomacy.

Binance withdrawals

Binance launched a campaign on Monday offering fee rebates, rewards to eligible users who rack up at least $10,000 in cumulative trading volume, as well as annual percentage rates of up to 10pc on certain yield-generating products.

The exchange’s “community appreciation campaign” will run through Nov 21, a post on its website showed.

Binance, which froze withdrawals for more than two days after the hack and then started allowing customers to withdraw again on Sunday morning in some assets, reopened withdrawals for more assets on Tuesday.

Since the resumption of withdrawals, Binance has seen net outflows amounting to around 3pc of the assets on its platform, it said on Monday, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up.

“The relatively contained price reaction suggests a degree of maturity and resilience,” said Maksym Repa, head of DeFi at Lombard, a Bitcoin finance protocol backed by Franklin Templeton.

“Investors appear to be distinguishing between a security failure at a centralised exchange and a problem with the Bitcoin network itself.”

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised. Solar, storage, and EV charging should receive urgent policy support. Collateral-free lines of credit should be introduced for rooftop solar. NBR should quickly implement assessment reform and a 0 percent duty.

In the medium term, within 1–3 years, renewable energy financing should be available at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent for 10–15 years. The LC margin should be limited to 5 percent. Land banks and grid infrastructure should be developed for utility-scale solar. Merchant Power Policy and MPPA should be simplified. Rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, and hybrid solar-storage projects should receive a 10–15-year tax holiday. A national program should convert 1.5 million diesel pumps into solar pumps. Rooftop solar should be made mandatory or incentive-based for government buildings, industrial zones, EPZs, economic zones, and large commercial buildings.
